items.text: JENNIE Releases Three-Track EP 'Fallen Angel' JENNIE has officially released her new solo digital EP, Fallen Angel. The three-track project released via her label Odd Atelier in partnership with Columbia Records, accompanied by a dark, fairytale-inspired music video for the title track.Described as a personal project reflecting self-expression, the release balances contrasting visual themes of light and dark. The cinematic music video for "Fallen Angel" utilizes surreal foggy landscapes, warped architecture, and heavy visual effects to build its narrative. items.title: Ridley Scott Announces Third 'Alien' Prequel Centering on Michael Fassbender's David
items.text: Ridley Scott Announces Third 'Alien' Prequel Centering on Michael Fassbender's David Summary Ridley Scott has confirmed plans to direct a third 'Alien' prequel centered on Michael Fassbender's android character DavidThe upcoming narrative follows David as he attempts to establish a brave new world for himself following the events of 'Alien Covenant'The announcement arrives alongside Scott's broader reflection on artificial intelligence during a recent interview Director Ridley Scott has officially confirmed development on a third Alien prequel feature. The filmmaker revealed details regarding the project during an interview with the L.A. Times.The planned project will focus on David, the malfunctioning AI android portrayed by Michael Fassbender in Prometheus and Alien: Covenant. According to Scott, the narrative follows David as he attempts to create a "brave new world for himself" following his previous efforts to manipulate synthetic and biological evolution.Addressing his ongoing thematic obsession with artificial intelligence—a subject explored across his filmography from Alien to Blade Runner—Scott reflected on the real-world evolution of AI technology. The director noted that while he does not currently use AI in his creative process, he views synthetic intelligence as an unpredictable force capable of outpacing human control. The film joins a slate of upcoming projects from Scott, including The Dog Stars starring Jacob Elordi and a Treasure Island adaptation featuring Hugh Jackman.Official production schedules and release dates for the third Alien prequel have not yet been announced. items.title: Nicole McLaughlin Upcycles Vintage Oakley Golf Bags Into Custom Outerwear
items.text: Nicole McLaughlin Upcycles Vintage Oakley Golf Bags Into Custom Outerwear Summary Nicole McLaughlin has revealed her latest upcycling project transforming vintage Oakley golf bags into custom outerwearThe design process deconstructs original straps pockets oversized logos and technical panels into a pair of one-off jacketsProfessional golfer Paris Hilinski was recently spotted wearing one of the completed custom creations on the course Designer Nicole McLaughlin has officially revealed her latest upcycling project, crafting custom Oakley Golf Bag Jackets from vintage equipment. Known for her functional transformations of sports gear, McLaughlin’s newest experiment turns archival golf bags into a pair of one-off wearable jackets.McLaughlin takes to Instagram to show the process of transforming the bags into leather motocross-inspired leather jackets. Starting with a collection of vintage Oakley golf bags, McLaughlin dismantled the original builds while still taking into account the branding, to repurpose their core functional elements. The resulting outerwear pieces integrate the bags' oversized brand logos, utility pockets, carrying straps, and durable technical panels directly into the jacket silhouettes. By retaining these structural details, the custom designs preserve the distinct visual language and hardware of the original golf gear.Bringing the experiment back onto the green, one of the finished custom jackets was recently worn by professional golfer Paris Hilinski, highlighting the practical utility of the upcycled technical concept.Take a look at the finished product above or below. View this post on Instagram A post shared by nm (@nicolemclaughlin) Click here to view full gallery at Hypebeast

items.title: Maluma Goes Back to His Roots With Hot Wheels and “La Matrona”
items.text: Maluma Goes Back to His Roots With Hot Wheels and “La Matrona” For Maluma, cars have always been about more than what is sitting in his garage. Long before the Colombian artist had access to some of the world’s most coveted supercars, his fascination started with Hot Wheels.That childhood connection has now come full circle as Maluma joins Hot Wheels as part of its “Challenge Accepted” campaign. But rather than looking toward the exotic cars that have become part of his life today, the Medellín native chose to revisit the vehicles and memories that shaped him growing up.At the center of the collaboration is La Matrona, a custom Toyota Land Cruiser FJ60 inspired by the rugged trucks Maluma remembers from childhood trips to the Colombian countryside. Reimagined as a 1:64-scale Hot Wheels model, the FJ60 becomes a miniature tribute to those early experiences and the beginning of an obsession with cars that has followed him throughout his career.The details keep his design firmly connected to home, as references to Colombia, Medellín, and Antioquia appear throughout the vehicle. While Maluma could have selected something faster, rarer, or more closely associated with luxury, the FJ60 tells a story built around nostalgia, family, and the memories that existed long before global tours and luxury garages.Hypebeast caught up with Maluma to discuss his lifelong fascination with cars, the childhood memories behind La Matrona, and why the Toyota Land Cruiser FJ60 felt like the right vehicle for his Hot Wheels debut. What is your first memory with Hot Wheels?"My love for cars began with Hot Wheels when I was just a young boy. I remember a very special moment when my uncle, who was studying in the United States, brought me a track set that came with several Hot Wheels cars as a gift. Given that Hot Wheels is such a legendary brand, we — as Latinos — viewed it as something completely out of reach. My uncle used to buy the products in the States and bring them to me in Colombia because we didn't have access to them. It was always a benchmark brand for me."Why did you choose the Toyota Land Cruiser FJ60 as your Hot Wheels car for the "Challenge Accepted" campaign?"Everyone thought we were going to reinterpret one of the exotic cars from my collection. Instead, I was driven by a desire to show our culture to the whole world. items.title: The Met Cancels John Galliano Exhibition
items.text: The Met Cancels John Galliano Exhibition SummaryThe Met canceled its Spring 2026 John Galliano exhibition due to backlash over his 2011 racist remarks.Galliano, Anna Wintour, and Andrew Bolton issued a joint statement supporting the decision, with Galliano apologizing.Following the July announcement of The Met Costume Institute’s Spring 2026 show, “John Galliano: Horizons,” the museum faced widespread backlash over Galliano’s past racist remarks. No more than a month later, the New York City museum released a joint statement with Galliano, Anna Wintour, and curator Andrew Bolton saying, “Following thoughtful discussions with John Galliano, we have together decided not to proceed with the exhibition."John Galliano wrote an extended remark, leading with his thanks to The Met, followed by acknowledgement of the decision. "After much reflection and discussion with The Met and all those involved, I have decided, with great sadness, that it is best for the exhibition not to take place at this time," he said. "I remain fully accountable for the pain caused by my words in the past, particularly the hurt I caused to the Jewish and Asian communities, and I remain deeply sorry for it."The words Galliano is referring to date back to 2011, when a video surfaced of the designer spewing racist remarks at a Paris cafe. The incident ultimately led to his firing from the Creative Director role at Dior, his ousting from his eponymous label, and legal fines amounting to 6,000 euros. The designer returned to the industry in 2014 as the Creative Director of Maison Margiela and most recently inked a deal with Zara in 2026 for a collaborative collection.The Met Costume Institute's curator in charge, Andrew Bolton, contributed to the statement, saying, “I believe deeply in the responsibility of museums to examine difficult histories with rigor, candor, and care. I also recognize the pain and concern this exhibition has caused." "After extensive discussion, I support the decision not to proceed," he added.As chairperson of the highly anticipated Met Gala, a response from Anna Wintour was also included: "John's decision that the exhibition devoted to his work should not take place at this time is very courageous and a measure of the man he is. I believe this is the right decision, and both he and the Museum have my full support."As of the time of writing, the museum has not shared official details of what the Spring 2026 exhibition will focus on instead. items.title: Es Devlin Builds a Temporary Society in FUTURA SEOUL
items.text: Es Devlin Builds a Temporary Society in FUTURA SEOUL Summary '3rd Poem' marks Es Devlin’s first solo exhibition in Korea.The show spans more than 30 years of work across light, sound, drawing, architecture and moving image.Visitors are folded into the exhibition through participatory works that explore presence, memory and collective experience. Es Devlin has spent much of her career thinking about what happens when people enter a space together. Her stages and installations have surrounded audiences with light, sound and architecture, often blurring the line between spectator and participant. For her first solo exhibition in Korea, that relationship between people, place and attention takes center stage.Titled 3rd Poem: Es Devlin, Come Home Again,the exhibition takes over FUTURA SEOUL in Bukchon through January 17, 2027. Spanning more than 30 years of Devlin’s practice, the show brings together drawing, sculpture, moving image, books, sound and light around a recurring idea in her work: presence.The exhibition opens with "Infinite Library," where drawings and films are projected across shelves filled with upside-down books. The structure eventually opens to reveal "Mirror Maze," an environment of reflective glass that folds the visitor into the work itself.Elsewhere, "Line of Light" began with Devlin waking one morning to a narrow strip of illumination. At Futura Seoul, the installation connects artificial light inside the building with the natural landscape beyond it. Upstairs, "Screenshare" transforms hundreds of sketchbooks accumulated over Devlin’s career into a monumental moving image of drawings, notes and fragments from past projects.At the center of the exhibition is a new iteration of "Come Home Again." Originally rooted in Devlin’s encounters with threatened species in London, the work now brings together animals and plants from both London and Seoul through drawing, spoken voices and choral recordings, expanding the exhibition’s idea of presence beyond the human.Participation continues with "Collective Portrait," where visitors sit across from strangers and draw one another at a shared table, leaving the portraits behind to accumulate throughout the run of the show.Rather than presenting a straightforward retrospective, 3rd Poem operates more like a living environment, where strangers read, draw, reflect and briefly share the same space before moving on.'3rd Poem: Es Devlin, Come Home Again' is on view at FUTURA SEOUL through January 17, 2027.F

items.title: Sage Elsesser's "Simple, Not Easy" Approach to Style
items.text: Sage Elsesser's "Simple, Not Easy" Approach to Style Sage Elsesser often feels like that one no one knows that I’m wearing… meme, in that he’s always sneaking comfort into his daily outfits. Whether it's a secretly silk-lined hoodie or a pair of shearling-lined UGG Tasman slip-ons, comfort catalyzes his current wardrobe.“I think my style has simplified a lot,” Elsesser says, sticking to a low-profile “uniform” most days: a monochrome hoodie or T-shirt (he’s not big on loud graphics these days), a wide-legged pant, and something calm and clean on the feet. “It’s all about ease and comfort — ease not in the sense that it’s easy, but in that there’s a certain energy that comes with feeling like it's not too laborious to find inspiration. Simple, but not easy is the best way to put it.”This effortless ethos is what bridges the gap between Sage Elsesser, the skateboarder, and Navy Blue, the musician. “Dressing to skate and dressing to perform are both all about how the clothing fits and feels,” he continues. “I love when people are willing to wear something less because of function, but more because of comfort. To me, the greatest luxury is comfort.”In true Sage Elsesser fashion, the multihyphenate finds himself fronting another key lookbook, this time around for a silhouette that actually remains in his uniform’s footwear rotation: UGG’s Chestnut Tasman. It’s likely because he was comfortable.Fresh off the new campaign, Elsesser sat down with Hypebeast to share more about his stripped-back approach to personal style, and how comfort is the connective tissue through it all.How would you describe your personal style?Sage Elsesser: Not only did my parents have great style, but they also gave me a lot of freedom as a child to experiment with whatever styles I was into. items.title: PUMA and Scuderia Ferrari HP Weave a Red Thread Through Michael Schumacher’s Legacy
items.text: PUMA and Scuderia Ferrari HP Weave a Red Thread Through Michael Schumacher’s Legacy In light of the 30th anniversary of Michael Schumacher’s arrival at Scuderia Ferrari HP, PUMA has reunited with the Formula 1 team to craft a new collection that pays homage to his historic career on the tracks. The limited-edition drop arrives ahead of the Formula 1 Monza Grand Prix. Considered Scuderia Ferrari HP’s home turf, the range becomes a joint expression of the team and Schumacher, with motorsport styles incorporating iconography and inspired emblems from the iconic racing era. Exemplifying this design approach is the red racing jacket, which draws from the driver’s race suit with contrasting white stitching, a high collar and the Scuderia Ferrari logo running across each shoulder. Other pieces, including the Replica T-shirt and Replica shirt, feature more direct references to his legacy, weaving the seven stars for each of his Championship wins across the backs. To elevate the aesthetic of the garments, PUMA also releases a cap with a laurel wreath embroidered on the brim. This drops alongside a pair of red Speedcat Pro and Speedcat sneakers that offer a fitting base to the rest of the collection with their deeply rooted motorsport heritage that has been particularly prevalent in streetwear over the past few years. Before its public debut on the Formula 1 Monza Grand Prix grid, Lewis Hamilton and Charles Leclerc sport the collection in a new campaign. Shot at the team’s garage, the visuals show how Schumacher’s influence lives on in the team today, with each piece celebrating his drive, discipline and commitment to Scuderia Ferrari HP. Shop the new PUMA for Scuderia Ferrari HP Limited Edition Monza Collection on the brand’s website now. Click here to view full gallery at Hypebeast

items.title: Rose Gold Meets Milano Blue On Parmigiani Fleurier’s Newest TONDA PF Skeleton Watch
items.text: Rose Gold Meets Milano Blue On Parmigiani Fleurier’s Newest TONDA PF Skeleton Watch Summary Parmigiani Fleurier debuts the 30-piece TONDA PF Skeleton in Rose Gold.Features a 40mm rose gold case, knurled bezel, and "Milano Blue" openworked movement.Powered by the ultra-thin, in-house Caliber PF777 with a 60-hour power reserve. Parmigiani Fleurier has expanded its flagship luxury sports collection with the TONDA PF Skeleton Rose Gold in Milano Blue. Limited to just 30 pieces worldwide, the watch showcases the Swiss manufacture’s architectural approach to openworking, where movement components are selectively reduced to emphasize proportion, light and depth rather than mere mechanical complexity.Housed in a 40mm case crafted from 18-carat rose gold case, the timepiece boasts anultra-slender profile of just 8.5mm in thickness. It retains the TONDA PF's signature collection design codes, including a finely knurled rose gold bezel, a screwed-in crown and 100 meters of water resistance.At its heart beats the Calibre PF777, an automatic manufacture movement with 192 components, a 60‑hour power reserve and a slim 3.9 mm profile. The satin‑finished, hand‑bevelled bridges create a refined framework, while the skeletonised 22‑carat rose gold rotor integrates seamlessly into the architecture. The Milano Blue hue adds atmosphere and tension, contrasting with the warmth of rose gold to create a layered visual depth.Each piece is engraved “1 of 30,” underscoring its rarity. More than a timepiece, the TONDA PF Skeleton Rose Gold Milano Blue embodies Parmigiani’s philosophy: mechanical elegance shaped by light, proportion, and architectural clarity. items.title: Supreme Celebrates Larry Clark's 'Tulsa' Legacy in New FW26 Collaboration
items.text: Supreme Celebrates Larry Clark's 'Tulsa' Legacy in New FW26 Collaboration Summary The Supreme x Larry Clark collaboration features archival Tulsa images and exclusive new photography across graphic apparel.Standout items includes hooded varsity jackets, sequin raglan tops, a bean bag and zines.The collaboration drops September 3 globally, followed by Asia on September 5. Supreme has officially linked up with celebrated American photographer and film director Larry Clark for a collaborative release. Continuing a creative relationship that spans over 30 years, the new release draws deeply from Clark's influential body of work. Born in Tulsa, Oklahoma in 1943, Clark spent 1962 through 1971 photographing his inner circle from an insider’s perspective, pioneering a raw, deeply personal approach to documentary photography. His seminal 1971 photobook, Tulsa, exposed the quotidian violence and self-destruction in everyday American society, going on to heavily inspire subsequent generations of autobiographical photographers - from Nan Goldin to Ryan McGinley - before Clark expanded his artistic realm with Teenage Lust (1983) and his acclaimed directorial debut Kids (1995).For FW26, Supreme and Larry Clark translate this storied photographic legacy into a focused range of graphic apparel utilizing original imagery from Tulsa alongside new photographs shot exclusively for Supreme. Leading the wearable offerings is a Hooded Varsity Jacket decorated with full-placement archival photography. The drop continues with an eye-catching Sequin Raglan L/S Top and a cozy Zip Up Hooded Sweatshirt, while graphic t-shirt options arrive in the form of the Gun Tee and the Neighbor Tee, both highlighting Clark's candid portraiture across core seasonal colorways.Extending beyond traditional streetwear staples, the capsule incorporates a curated selection of lifestyle goods, skate hardware and printed collectibles decorated with Clark’s imagery. Highlighting the home goods selection is an oversized 42- inch-by-42-inch Bean Bag emblazoned with exclusive photography, serving as a distinct lifestyle statement piece. The collaborative drop is completed by a co-branded Skateboard deck and a 48-page collectible Zine, which comes outfitted with an exclusive poster insert showcasing Clark's visual archive.The Supreme x Larry Clark collaboration is scheduled for a global release later this week. The capsule will be available online and across physical Supreme chapter locations starting Septembe

items.title: TRUNK(HOTEL) SAPPORO Introduces a 107-Room “Mid-Century Folklore” Retreat
items.text: TRUNK(HOTEL) SAPPORO Introduces a 107-Room “Mid-Century Folklore” Retreat Summary TRUNK(HOTEL) SAPPORO is set to open its doors on September 17, 2027 in Hokkaido.It features 107 rooms with a "Mid-Century Folklore" design theme.Amenities include the iconic restaurant Sushi Saito and a 40-meter water spa. Japanese boutique hotel brand TRUNK has officially announced that its newest destination, TRUNK(HOTEL) SAPPORO, is scheduled to open on September 17, 2027. Marking the boutique brand's first venture outside of Tokyo, the property will be located in the Sapporo Daibiru building within the heart of Hokkaido's central Odori district.Emphasizing a philosophy of deeply understanding the local context, the hotel aims to offer an experience uniquely shaped by Hokkaido’s history, culture, nature, and cuisine. Housed across the 10th to 18th floors, the property will feature 107 guest rooms alongside premium amenities, including an all-day dining restaurant, a lounge and bar with live music, versatile banquet space and a private entertainment studio equipped for cinema and karaoke.Designed by GENERAL DESIGN CO., LTD. and TRUNK Atelier, the hotel's overarching aesthetic follows a "Mid-Century Folklore" theme. This design concept thoughtfully reinterprets mid-century design through TRUNK's unique perspective, drawing direct inspiration from Hokkaido's natural landscapes and traditional handiwork. The guest rooms utilize wood-centric textures and finely crafted details to create a warm environment where visitors can feel the presence of nature despite being in an urban center.In addition to its beautifully appointed rooms, the hotel introduces the brand's first-ever spa, TRUNK(BATH HOUSE). Positioned on the 18th floor as an immersive "water utopia," the facility features a 40-meter waterway and ten distinct swimwear-friendly bathing zones designed with varied lighting, sound, and temperature stimuli, alongside high-temperature saunas and open-air baths.Elevating its culinary offerings, TRUNK(HOTEL) SAPPORO will also host the first Sapporo location of "Sushi Saito," the globally acclaimed Edo-mae sushi restaurant. At this exclusive 10th-floor counter, diners will be able to enjoy a unique regional style of sushi that masterfully blends traditional Edo-mae techniques with Hokkaido's exceptional local ingredients. items.text: Everything Dropping at Palace This Week Summary Palace Skateboard's latest drop is led by a GORE-TEXT jacket delivery in four colorwaysSportswear references run through the release with mesh team jerseys, rugby tops, and training sweatsPolartec fleeces with reflective and tri-ferg detailing round out this week's technical pieces Palace Skateboards has unveiled its latest Fall 2026 weekly drop, and this one balances heavy technical outerwear against a run of sports-referencing pieces. Led by a GORE-TEX jacket delivery and backed by mesh team jerseys, rugby tops, and Polartec fleeces, the release leans on performance fabrications while nodding to the sportswear vocabulary Palace regularly draws from.The technical outerwear anchors the week. Palace's GORE-TEX jacket lands in four colorways, camo, black, olive, and orange, built stormproof and finished with contrasting zips, with a matching hat available alongside each. It is the drop's clear centerpiece, offering the weatherproofing that GORE-TEX is known for across a spread of makeups broad enough to cover both loud and understated tastes.The performance theme carries into the fleeces. Palace works Polartec fabric into pieces detailed with a reflective strip and Velcro tri-ferg accents, the latter a nod to the brand's Tri-Ferg logo, pairing warmth with the kind of functional touches that keep the release grounded in technical wear rather than pure fashion layering.Running alongside the technical pieces is a strong sportswear current. The drop includes mesh team jerseys finished with custom name tapes reading Wilson, Brady, Cannon, and Clarke, plus a set of Palermo-inspired and flipped rugby tops and training sweats. Together those pieces pull from football and rugby kit traditions, giving the week a jersey-and-pitch feel that plays off the more utilitarian outerwear.The collection launches Friday, September 4 at 11:00 a.m. BST for the UK, Europe, and US, followed by Saturday, September 5 at 11:00 a.m. local time for Japan, China, Korea, and Australia. The Pokémon Company has officially announced Pokémon: Wild Card, a new feature-length animated film slated for release in 2027. items.text: Vacheron Constantin Turns to Nature and Rare Crafts for the “Tribute to the Animal Kingdom” Series Summary Vacheron Constantin unveils the Métiers d’Art Tribute to the Animal Kingdom Collection, featuring six artistic watches.Models include Feathersnake, Glassoctopus, Oraygami, Tigerbroidery, Papercroc, Woodenwings.Each piece highlights rare crafts such as marquetry, embroidery, glasswork and engraving. Vacheron Constantin has unveiled the Métiers d’Art Tribute to the Animal Kingdom Collection, a series of six extraordinary timepieces that celebrate artisanal craft and natural symbolism. Each watch is a unique canvas where traditional techniques such as engraving, enameling, embroidery, and marquetry are elevated into horological art. The collection reflects the Maison’s long‑standing commitment to blending fine watchmaking with métiers d’art, offering collectors rare expressions of creativity and cultural storytelling.The Feathersnake presents an amphibious serpent coiling through foliage, assembled by micro-plumasserie specialist Julien Vermeulen. The exquisite dial showcases delicate feather marquetry, creating a serpentine motif that captures movement and texture with remarkable realism. The dial work itself is composed of goose feathers, with over 200 tiny pieces derived from seven rare Lophophore feathers applied to silk paper and a 3D metal appliqué.Meanwhile, the aquatic kingdom is brought to life through three distinct, sculptural interpretations. The Glassoctopus features a transparent octopus sculpted from glass rods dot-by-dot using tungsten tools by artist Simone Crestani, set over a dark blue hand-guilloché gold dial base. Exploring the deep sea through paper, the Oraygami showcases six micro-origami manta rays folded by Anja Midori from self-dyed Japanese paper, mounted at varying heights on fine brass stems over a blue hand-guilloché surface with a moiré-effect crystal.Representing land and sky, three additional timepieces demonstrate extreme miniaturization in textiles, paper, and wood. The Tigerbroidery captures a prowling tiger embroidered by Laura Baverstock using 9-karat yellow and white gold threads alongside ceramic-coated copper wires on a green silk base, fitted to a perforated titanium dial plate. items.title: 'Backrooms' Is Rewriting What Horror Is Allowed to Be
items.text: 'Backrooms' Is Rewriting What Horror Is Allowed to Be Horror has always been good at monsters. What it's historically been less good at is dread without a source, the particular unease of being somewhere wrong without knowing how you got there or what, exactly, is coming for you. Backrooms fixes that, and in doing so has quietly become one of the most significant shifts in how the genre operates in years.The origins of this blockbuster is, almost, embarrassingly simple. It all started from single photograph uploaded to 4chan in 2019: an empty room, fluorescent lights, yellow wallpaper the color of old teeth, carpet that belongs in a mid-century office no one has cleaned since 1987. The caption described it as what you see when you "noclip out of reality." That image should not have produced what it did. And yet it became the seed for an entire collaborative mythology, built in comment sections and forums and YouTube videos by people who had never met, all agreeing on the rules of a place that doesn't exist.Kane Pixels, a teenager with a camera and editing software, took that mythology and turned it into a found footage series that has now been viewed hundreds of millions of times. The genius of his approach is restraint. Backrooms in his films is not loud. There are no jump scares engineered to make you spill your drink. The horror comes from fluorescent hum, from the sense of scale, from the implication of something just out of frame that has been watching for longer than you've been aware of it. It's the kind of filmmaking that understands atmosphere as a weapon.What separates Backrooms from the horror that came before it is where the anxiety lives. Traditional horror exteriorizes fear: there is a thing, the thing wants to hurt you, you run. Backrooms internalizes it. The terror is spatial and psychological, rooted in the feeling of being in a place that should be familiar but has been stripped of every marker that makes familiar spaces safe. There's no exits, no other people, no sky, no weather. Only the hum and the yellow and the sense that the geometry is slightly wrong in a way you can't quite name. Anyone who has ever woken up disoriented in an unfamiliar room at 3am knows the specific flavor of that feeling, and Backrooms has figured out how to sustain it for as long as it wants.It also changed who gets to make horror. items.title: THEMGOOD Seoul 2026 Spotlights The Biggest Van Gogh Pikachu Collection
items.text: THEMGOOD Seoul 2026 Spotlights The Biggest Van Gogh Pikachu Collection Summary Grade10 and Gana Art have formed ZZZ, a joint venture built to develop South Korea's trading card and collectibles ecosystemThe venture debuts during Seoul Art Week with THEMGOOD in Itaewon, headlined by a record-scale Van Gogh Pikachu installation and two rare complete setsThe launch arrives as South Korea's collectible-card-games market is projected to more than double by 2033 Grade10 and Gana Art have launched ZZZ, a joint venture aimed at placing trading cards inside South Korea's high-end art and collectibles world. The partnership makes its public debut with THEMGOOD, an exhibition opening in Itaewon during Seoul Art Week, that treats rare cards with the curatorial framing usually reserved for fine art.The venture pairs two different kinds of expertise. Grade10, Asia's premier trading-card venture and a division of MemeStrategy, brings its footing in the card industry, while Gana Art contributes a curatorial perspective and an international cultural network. The stated aim is an integrated ecosystem spanning exhibitions and card festivals, collector-community programs, and trading services on and offline, built to serve a Korean collector base that both companies describe as increasingly sophisticated."ZZZ represents the next phase of Grade10's commitment to build durable collector infrastructure across Asia," said Ray Chan, Chief Executive Officer of MemeStrategy and Grade10, framing the venture as a bridge between Grade10's industry reach and Gana Art's cultural standing. The gallery, for its part, positions the effort as an extension of its curatorial mission. "Trading cards are a vibrant visual culture with global resonance, and South Korea has a discerning community ready to encounter this area in new ways," said Sierra Yun, Director of Marketing and Sales at Gana Art.That ambition is anchored by the objects on show. THEMGOOD's centerpiece is a 500-card installation of "Pikachu with Grey Felt Hat" promos, each in PSA Gem Mint 10 condition, which Grade10 identifies as the world's largest display of the graded card by count. The promo originated in the Van Gogh Museum's 2023 collaboration with The Pokémon Company, marking the museum's 50th anniversary, and quickly became one of the era's most recognizable Pokémon cards. items.title: Roger Federer Takes His Place in Tennis History With His Hall of Fame Induction
items.text: Roger Federer Takes His Place in Tennis History With His Hall of Fame Induction Summary Roger Federer was inducted into the International Tennis Hall of Fame in Newport, Rhode Island, cementing his place among the sport's immortalsThe 45-year-old broke down repeatedly across a nearly 30-minute speech that moved from his childhood hero to his wife and longtime coachBroadcaster Mary Carillo entered alongside him in the contributor category, presented by Billie Jean King Roger Federer stepped into the International Tennis Hall of Fame on Saturday, closing the loop on a career that reshaped how the sport is played and watched. Introduced during the Hall's first red-carpet show as the Swiss Maestro, the 45-year-old took the stage at Newport's grass horseshoe court and spent nearly half an hour placing himself, often through tears, within the lineage of the game he grew up idolizing.Federer has always positioned himself as a student of tennis history, and the induction read as the natural endpoint of that reverence. His wife, Mirka, introduced him before he addressed a crowd thick with fellow Hall of Famers, and he admitted almost immediately that the moment outmatched him. "Oh man," he opened. "This is very high level and a tough act to follow." He conceded he "was a little stressed to be honest," then let the weight of the setting take over.The speech built its emotional core around the figures who shaped him. It turned first to Stefan Edberg, the childhood hero whose example pulled Federer toward the sport, a passage he described through what he called "happy tears." He choked up again over his longtime coach Severin Luthi, and then over Mirka, pausing before the words gave way. The through-line was less a highlight reel than an accounting of debts, the people and history that carried a kid from Switzerland into the room where the game keeps its legends.Federer became the first man to win 20 Grand Slam singles titles, held the world No. 1 ranking for a record 237 consecutive weeks, and reached 10 straight Slam finals, winning eight of them. His haul spanned eight Wimbledon titles, six Australian Opens, five consecutive US Opens from 2004 to 2008 and a lone French Open in 2009 that completed his career Grand Slam, a feat only eight men have managed. items.title: Defending F1 Champion Lando Norris Extends His McLaren Contract Through 2030
items.text: Defending F1 Champion Lando Norris Extends His McLaren Contract Through 2030 Summary Lando Norris has signed a multi-year contract extension to remain with McLaren until at least 2030The defending Formula One world champion will receive his title-winning 2025 MCL39 car as part of the new agreementNorris cited the strong team culture and recent championship success as key factors in his decision to stay Defending Formula One world champion Lando Norris has officially cemented his future with McLaren. The 26-year-old British driver signed a multi-year contract extension that will keep him in papaya until at least 2030. Announced during a friends and families day at the McLaren Technology Centre in Woking, the deal ends any speculation about a potential move to a rival constructor. Norris secured his maiden world title in 2025 and has firmly positioned himself as the centerpiece of the legendary racing outfit.The relationship between driver and constructor runs deep. Norris joined the McLaren young driver program in 2017 and made his premier class debut two years later. Navigating the team through a massive rebuilding phase, he emerged as their longest-serving driver with 163 Grands Prix under his belt. To celebrate the renewed partnership, CEO Zak Brown and team principal Andrea Stella confirmed Norris will receive one of the actual MCL39 cars he drove to championship glory last season. The reigning champion noted that the team feels like a second family and expressed a clear desire to spend his entire racing career entirely under their banner.Recent momentum undeniably influenced the commitment. Following comprehensive car upgrades, Norris secured crucial victories at Zandvoort and the Hungaroring this season to keep McLaren competitive under fresh technical regulations. While other teams actively approached him with offers, the driver remained loyal to the environment that facilitated his 13 career race wins. Financial details remain under wraps but Norris openly acknowledged the compensation sits below the massive figures commanded by Lewis Hamilton and Max Verstappen. Hamilton reportedly earns $60 million annually at Ferrari while Verstappen recently locked in a massive Red Bull extension rumored to reach $100 million.Despite the salary gap, Norris remains focused on the grid hierarchy rather than the ultimate payout. items.title: Analysts Estimate 'GTA VI's' Budget Exceeds $1 Billion USD, Making It the Costliest Entertainment Product Ever
items.text: Analysts Estimate 'GTA VI's' Budget Exceeds $1 Billion USD, Making It the Costliest Entertainment Product Ever Summary Grand Theft Auto VI is projected to be the most expensive entertainment production in history, with analyst estimates placing the development budget between $1 billion and $1.5 billionRockstar North co-head Aaron Garbut revealed the title features over 600,000 unique animations, facilitated by a dedicated Los Angeles team focused on hand-crafting individual NPCsFollowing multiple delays, the game is officially scheduled for a November 19, 2026 release on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S amid ongoing legal claims regarding alleged union busting Grand Theft Auto VI looks set to become the most expensive entertainment product ever created. Rockstar Games has not publicly disclosed the exact financial investment, but industry analysts peg the estimated budget at well over $1 billion USD. Some current estimates place the figure closer to $1.5 billion USD. This massive financial commitment outpaces the known budgets of major Hollywood theatrical releases and sets a new benchmark for AAA game development. To contextualize this scale, recent court documents revealed that Sony Interactive Entertainment spent $212 million USD on Horizon Forbidden West and $220 million USD on The Last of Us: Part II, while Activision invested roughly $700 million USD into Call of Duty: Black Ops Cold War over its life cycle.A billion-dollar budget stems directly from the modern realities of game development and a production schedule spanning nearly a decade. Creating an expansive open-world environment requires vast teams of actors, writers, programmers, animators, designers and composers. Rockstar established a specialized Los Angeles-based team specifically to art-direct every individual non-player character. Studio co-head Aaron Garbut noted in a recent interview that this technical ambition pushed the in-game animation count to 600,000. That figure dwarfs the 55,000 animations found in Grand Theft Auto V and doubles the 300,000 implemented in Red Dead Redemption 2.Publishers Take-Two Interactive and Rockstar are willing to risk unprecedented sums because the potential return on investment remains unparalleled. The previous franchise entry generated $800 million USD in sales within a single day of its 2013 launch. items.title: KidSuper x Havaianas Merge Art and Football Across a Bold Four-Piece Footwear Collection
items.text: KidSuper x Havaianas Merge Art and Football Across a Bold Four-Piece Footwear Collection Brazilian footwear icon Havaianas and Brooklyn-based label KidSuper have officially unveiled their collaborative four-piece footwear collection. Building on an ongoing creative partnership, the latest capsule bridges the gap between traditional athletic inspiration and avant-garde street style. KidSuper founder Colm Dillane applies his distinct design language directly to the renowned Havaianas footwear frame to merge art and sport.The unquestionable centerpiece of the release is the Havaianas x KidSuper "Top Turf Pitch" sandal. Originally previewed during KidSuper's FW26 runway presentation at Paris Men's Fashion Week, the model features an unorthodox material overhaul. The entire silhouette is wrapped in lush green velvet designed to recreate the visual and tactile sensation of a football pitch directly beneath the wearer's feet. This structural choice connects directly to the "futebol arte" inspiration driving the collaboration.Beyond the velvet flagship model, the collection includes three additional styles featuring original printed artwork by Dillane. These graphic iterations focus on vibrant colors, movement, and the expressive character motifs that define the KidSuper design universe. Every pair in the four-piece lineup is finalized with exclusive co-branded detailing and specialized collectible packaging. Inside the box, buyers will find a custom card equipped with four distinct metallic pins meant for personalizing the sandals alongside a co-branded KidSuper gym sack.The partnership physically extends to São Paulo, where Havaianas and KidSuper restored a public football court. Transformed using original artwork by Dillane, the space eventually served as the physical setting for the campaign shoot.The release also builds upon Dillane's deep personal relationship with Brazilian culture. A passionate football fan and former player, he previously lived in the country and spent time at Esporte Clube Vitória in Bahia. His connection to the Portuguese language and local football lore serves as the foundational creative exchange behind the footwear designs. “Havaianas is such a Brazilian icon, and for me that made it a really exciting canvas to play with. We took this shared love of football and brought it into the KidSuper world through color, art and a little bit of the unexpected. The result feels like both brands, which is always what you want from a collaboratio

items.title: mfpen Remakes the New Balance 991v1 in "Surplus Leathers"
items.text: mfpen Remakes the New Balance 991v1 in "Surplus Leathers" SummaryThe mfpen x New Balance Made in UK 991v1 uses upcycled surplus materials for a limited 90-pair release on September 3.It features a hand-debossed "N" logo, blending New Balance’s Flimby factory heritage with mfpen’s minimalist aesthetic.mfpen and New Balance give excess materials new life with their first-ever collaboration, which reimagines the Made in UK 991v1 in “Surplus Leathers.” The debut silhouette from mfpen x New Balance embraces the footwear brand’s archival history, while staying true to mfpen’s design philosophy and lived-in feel.mfpen founder Sigurd Bank offered Hypebeast exclusive insights on the partnership, sharing, “New Balance has always felt somehow connected to mfpen. I remember styling the first collections with my own thrashed New Balance sneakers. I’ve always loved the normy, dad-core look of the 99' series, so it felt like a natural fit for us to work together.”Using leftover materials from New Balance’s Flimby, England factory, mfpen’s 991v1 gets a lived-in feel from a tumbled nubuck, pigsuede, and mesh makeup. The approach aligns with mfpen’s production values, which have historically centered on deadstock, surplus, and upcycled fabrics, as well as conscious mitigation of overproduction. “I went to visit the factory in Flimby, in northern England, and went through their old stocks of leathers and materials. Everything was available in different quantities and with different options, which is why the release is limited to just 90 pairs,” Bank explained. “All upper materials are surplus from past production,” he added.Notably, the collaborative model tones down the classic N monogram with a debossed finish, lending it a minimalist sensibility, in tune with the mfpen aesthetic. “Personally, I have a hard time with logos, and I think toning down the N is a simple way to mess with the silhouette while still keeping that recognizable New Balance reference,” Bank shared.And while the subtle N stamp may feel like a contemporary development, it’s actually pulled from the New Balance archives. However, applying the archival detail to the nubuck was its own challenge: “After some trials, they got it right, but they had to do every single emboss by hand. I really liked that process and the fact that it made each pair feel connected to the factory and its history.”The unveiling of mfpen's New Balance 991v1 comes just weeks after the brand previewed a New Balance 992 at its SS27 r

items.title: New Arrivals From HBX: Maison Margiela
items.text: New Arrivals From HBX: Maison Margiela Brand Information: Maison Margiela is a Paris-based fashion house founded in 1988 by Martin Margiela. The brand is best known for its progressive aesthetic and unique approach to deconstructing, reinventing, and redefining men’s and womenswear. It is a design philosophy that permeates into a wide range of ready-to-wear items such as T-shirts, sweaters, hoodies, and crewnecks, as well as other complementary items such as bags, small leather goods, and shoes. Currently, Maison Margiela is headed by the four-time winner of British Designer of the Year, couturier John Galliano. Galliano has also served as the head designer at various French fashion companies, including Givenchy, Christian Dior, and his own label, John Galliano. Maison Margiela has collaborated with many different brands over the years, such as The North Face, Swarovski, and Mykita. The brand has also established a diffusion line named MM6 Maison Margiela.Price Range: $210.00 USD - $2,990.00 USDWhere to Buy: Available now on HBX Click here to view full gallery at Hypebeast

items.title: Bremont’s Terra Nova Nova Jumping Hour Watch Now Comes in a Compact 35mm Case Size
items.text: Bremont’s Terra Nova Nova Jumping Hour Watch Now Comes in a Compact 35mm Case Size Summary Bremont expands its Terra Nova Jumping Hour line with a compact 35mm case in 904L steel.Variants include core steel, sunray burgundy, and limited-edition shimmering Frosted and Frosted Pink models.Driven by the automatic Calibre BC634, delivering instantaneous hour changes and a 54-hour power reserve. Unveiled at Geneva Watch Days, Bremont has expanded its field-inspired Terra Nova collection with five new additions headlined by a 35mm case size. First introduced in 2024, the Terra Nova line draws design cues from early 20th-century trench and military pocket watches, reimagining classic military aesthetics through modern cushion-shaped cases with low profiles and shortened lugs. The new 35mm silhouette transforms the collection’s signature montre à guichet (jumping hour) display into a versatile dress watch format with vintage charm, joining an updated 40.5mm execution to broaden the range.The 35mm lineup is crafted from 904L stainless steel and features several distinct finishes and dial designs. The core Terra Nova 35 Jumping Hour presents a closed, brushed steel dial face with dual aperture windows at 12 and 6 o'clock for the jumping hour and sweeping minutes. Adding rich color to the range, the Terra Nova 35 Jumping Hour Burgundy introduces a sunray-lacquered burgundy dial with vertical jumping hour windows, a central seconds hand, and star and dot hour markers.For a more decorative touch, Bremont introduced two limited-edition textured models: the Terra Nova 35 Jumping Hour Frosted, limited to 150 pieces with a shimmering, diamond-like hammered case, and the Terra Nova 35 Jumping Hour Frosted Pink, limited to 200 pieces featuring a sunray pink dial, star and diamond markers, and a pale pink nubuck leather strap.At the heart of the new models is the automatic Bremont Calibre BC634, developed in exclusive partnership with Sellita. Running at 28,800 vph with a 54-hour power reserve, the movement powers a high-torque jumping hour mechanism capable of instantaneous hour changes in under one-tenth of a second. Depending on the model, the watches offer water resistance ranging from 30 meters on the closed-dial editions to 100 meters on the burgundy dial variants. Every reference is equipped with quick-release 904L stainless steel bracelets or coordinating nubuck leather straps, offering versatile styling across the updated collection. items.title: Berneron’s Mirage Miroir Shines in 18K White and Yellow Gold
items.text: Berneron’s Mirage Miroir Shines in 18K White and Yellow Gold Summary Berneron unveils the asymmetric Mirage Miroir watch in 18K white and yellow gold.Introduces the all-gold, openworked Caliber 283 with a mirrored movement construction.Limited to 36 pieces per colorway annually. Independent Swiss watch brand Berneron has revealed the Mirage Miroir, an openworked evolution of its signature asymmetric dress watch. Produced in extremely limited numbers, the Mirage Miroir is defined by its asymmetry, drawn not from external design but from the mechanics themselves. The new “mirrored construction” approach reimagines openworking, with bridges and mainplate architecture designed to guide the eye and serve as visual markers for reading the time. Crafted entirely in 18K gold, the watch embodies discreet luxury and refined elegance.At the heart of the Mirage Miroir lies the Calibre 283, Berneron’s fourth in‑house movement. Measuring just 2.83 mm thick, it features an inverted hand set with the hour hand on top, a free‑sprung balance wheel, and a 72‑hour power reserve. The seconds counter is deliberately omitted to maximize the openwork design, with the rotating seconds wheel itself acting as a running indicator. Decorative techniques such as guillochage, anglage and laser engraving elevate the movement’s architectural presence, underscoring Berneron’s commitment to artisanal craft.Reflecting Berneron's commitment to high quality and limited production, each colorway will be produced at a rate of 36 pieces per year over a 10-year cycle (Series A), with initial deliveries slated to begin in October 2027. Water-resistant to 30 meters, the watch is topped with a scratch-resistant coated Hesalite crystal and can be configured on either a Barenia leather strap or a matching 20mm 18K solid gold bracelet. Pricing for the Mirage Miroir is set at 72,500 CHF (approx. $89,528 USD) on the leather strap and 130,250 CHF (approx. $160,842 USD) on the solid gold bracelet. For more information, visit Berneron's official website. Click here to view full gallery at Hypebeast

items.title: sacai TO GO Lands in Paris With Exclusive Pieces
items.text: sacai TO GO Lands in Paris With Exclusive Pieces Summary sacai is staging a limited-time pop-up called "sacai TO GO" inside Le Bon Marché Rive Gauche as part of SUPER JAPONThe space carries exclusive merchandise spanning collaborative tees, repurposed-fabric totes, plush charms and a magnetic paper-doll setCo-curated by colette co-founder Sarah Andelman, the takeover pulls in Japanese confectioners, Paris coffee shops and a rotating cast of the label's friends sacai is bringing an immersive slice of its world to Paris with "sacai TO GO," a limited-time event on the second floor of Le Bon Marché Rive Gauche. Running as part of the store's SUPER JAPON program, the takeover blends Japanese culture with Parisian creativity across food, drink and a deep bench of exclusive merchandise.The exclusive apparel spans a run of black and white T-shirts, some carrying the sacai logo, others leaning on MA-1-inspired detailing or rocky's matcha's tiger graphic. Rounding out the shirt selection are pieces pulled from sacai's collaborations with Carhartt WIP and Nike, folding two of the label's marquee tie-ups into the same exclusive rack.Beyond the tees, the accessories carry real weight. sacai is stocking tote bags from its signature Zantan series, each crafted from repurposed archive fabrics, and pairing them with Peloqoon's plush key charms designed by plush artist Madoka Morikawa. The most unexpected object is a boxed RYVDOLL set made with French artist Ryvka Adda, a collection of magnetic paper dolls that recreate sacai's 26AW looks and let visitors mix and match styling combinations by hand.The consumables are just as considered. Toraya, a Japanese confectioner with five centuries of history, and rocky's matcha, founded by Rocky Xu, are featured throughout the run. Weekends add a rotating cast of Paris-based friends of the label, with ice cream shop F.O.L.D.E.R.O.L, bento brand Iné, kissaten-inspired sandwich and coffee spot Benchy, seasonal-cuisine specialist NIWA and coffee shop Dreamin' Man each taking a turn across the calendar.Tying the whole thing together is co-curator Sarah Andelman, co-founder and former Creative Director of the influential Paris concept store colette, who assembled a community of longtime collaborators to shape the space. items.title: côte&ciel Launches Transformative Bags and Accessories for FW26
items.text: côte&ciel Launches Transformative Bags and Accessories for FW26 The côte&ciel Fall/Winter 2026 Collection explores fashion as an active verb - an act of making, shaping, and constructing - rather than a static statement of style.Led by designer Emilie Arnault, the seasonal concept takes inspiration from Charles Fréger's photographic study Wilder Mann, which observes European folk festival costumes blending human and animal forms. This ritualistic connection to nature translates into an earthy, tactile palette that features wool-like Tweed Anthracite, home upholstery-inspired Black & Cream Tweed, lightweight Smooth Burgundy Nylon and technical Carbon Black textiles. To emphasize the craftsmanship behind the designs, the brand paired its industrial lookbook with handcrafted artistic works by Paris-based creative Aurélie Mathigot.Rooted in the philosophy of "the same song, but different instruments," the seasonal range evolves côte&ciel's iconic silhouettes through fluid, body-responsive forms that bridge the gap between bags and wearable garments. Key styles in the range include the ELVO backpack in Carbon Black, which expands and compresses to fit tech devices up to 16 inches, and the RENO shoulder bag, which unfolds into a wearable vest complete with an integrated Smooth Black hood.Furthering the origami-like construction, the compact PO S twists water-repellent nylon to transition seamlessly between a sling and a vest. The collection is completed by small accessories ("Petits Accessories"), including the AÓOS NANO pouch, eyewear cases, and modular leather charm cords like the LETGO series. The collection is available now globally through côte&ciel and will also be stocked by HBX starting September 2, 2025. Click here to view full gallery at Hypebeast

items.title: Taemin on Finding Cruelty in Beauty on 'PHASE 1: Soft Violence'
items.text: Taemin on Finding Cruelty in Beauty on 'PHASE 1: Soft Violence' Taemin has spent almost 20 arguing that a pop star can be an unsettling one too, and PHASE 1: Soft Violence is his most literal case for it yet. The album introduces itself with a sugar cube being pulled apart by ants, an image that reads as sweet and grim in the same glance, and from there he fills the record with slime, clay and holes torn through walls. None of it is set dressing. Each object stands in for a version of himself he has lived through and kept.The title is the whole thesis in two words; the SHINee and SuperM staple treats loveliness and harm as the same material rather than as opposites, which is where the "violence" in the phrase comes from. "I believe there is cruelty within beauty, and in a certain sense, that can also be a form of violence," he says. He applies the same logic to his own history, declining to sort it into wins and wounds. The hard stretches and the joyful ones, in his telling, fed the same foundation, and the injuries that keep surfacing across the album are really the many Taemins who built the one speaking now.If the album serves an accounting of the past, the tour is written in the present tense. He named it "LiMiNaL" after the threshold — the charged pause that comes before anything actually changes, and he is frank that the choice was a message to himself as much as a concept for an audience. "'LiMiNaL' refers to a boundary or a state of being on the threshold. I chose the title 'LiMiNaL' for this tour because I wanted to take a step beyond the way I had been doing things up until now," he explains. He describes the era as a doorway he is currently standing in, with the next chapter waiting on the far side. "In a way, I think 'LiMiNaL' represents who I am right now, standing at that threshold. And through 'PHASE 2,' which will follow, I want to show a version of myself that has crossed that boundary and taken another step forward."A lot of that momentum traces back to a field in the California desert. Taemin performed at Coachella billed as the first Korean male soloist to do so, and the size of the moment clearly lodged itself somewhere permanent. "I also realized, 'There's a much bigger market and a much bigger world out there,'" he says. What stayed with him was the way the crowd used the platform, moving and singing together instead of simply watching a performance, and it quietly reset his sense of the job. items.title: UNDERCOVER Turns Its ‘UNDERMAN’ Mythology Into a Feature Film With ‘UNDERGIRL’
items.text: UNDERCOVER Turns Its ‘UNDERMAN’ Mythology Into a Feature Film With ‘UNDERGIRL’ Summary UNDERCOVER is releasing UNDERGIRL, described as the first film from its UNDERCOVER PRODUCTION armThe story picks up the world of UNDERMAN, the art book tied to the label's 2011 spring/summer collection, and follows a hero's daughter stepping into his roleA limited Shibuya screening run brings the roughly hour-long feature to audiences this September UNDERCOVER is stepping into filmmaking with UNDERGIRL, billed as the debut movie from UNDERCOVER PRODUCTION. The project revives the fictional universe first laid out in UNDERMAN, the photo-and-graphic art book that accompanied the brand's Spring/Summer 2011 collection, and reanimates it 15 years later as a 54-minute feature.The narrative centers on Yuri Ibuki, the daughter of a hero named UNDERMAN who has long shouldered the sorrows of the city while protecting its people. When he vanishes without warning, a mysterious envoy called Kiko appears before Yuri and guides her toward an inescapable destiny: succeeding her father and becoming UNDERGIRL. The film follows her through the trials that transformation demands.The production is led by UNDERCOVER PRODUCTION, a unit built around Jun Takahashi alongside Tetsuya Nagato, Katsuhide Morimoto and Taro Mizutani. Morimoto, a photographer and filmmaker, directs, while the screenplay was written jointly by Takahashi, Nagato, Morimoto and Mizutani. Takahashi additionally serves as executive producer.The casting anchors the fiction with recognizable faces. Sena Nakajima plays the lead, Yuri Ibuki and UNDERGIRL, opposite Ryuhei Matsuda as UNDERMAN. Kiko Mizuhara, who appeared in the original 2011 UNDERMAN project, returns here, and Mitsuko Baisho joins as another key figure moving through the story.UNDERGIRL screens at SPACE PART 3 by PARCO in Shibuya from September 14 through September 20, 2026, with weekday showings at 6 p.m. and 7:30 p.m. and weekend showings at 2 p.m. and 4 p.m. Tickets are available from September 2 via the venue's dedicated web page.SPACE PART 3 by PARCO7th floor, Shibuya Miba BuildingTokyo Click here to view full gallery at Hypebeast

items.title: Take an Inside Look at ‘Dressing Up,’ Sandy Liang’s First Rizzoli Monograph
items.text: Take an Inside Look at ‘Dressing Up,’ Sandy Liang’s First Rizzoli Monograph Summary Sandy Liang is releasing Dressing Up: Sandy Liang, a monograph gathering ten years of the label's visual world through Rizzoli New YorkThe book leans on previously unpublished personal photography to trace her runway moments, inspirations and take on uniform dressingCreative director Ava Nirui and stylist Dean DiCriscio contribute to the project alongside Liang Sandy Liang is giving readers a look behind the curtain with Dressing Up: Sandy Liang, a new monograph arriving via Rizzoli New York. Marking more than a decade of her namesake label, the book compiles an intimate selection of ephemera from the designer's world and opens up the process behind the girlish, nostalgia-driven universe she has built.As an object, the release is a substantial one. It runs 276 pages in hardcover, and the interior is anchored by previously unpublished material, including personal film and iPhone photographs that Liang has kept as her own running record. Rather than a straight lookbook, the pages are curated through a close, personal lens, surfacing the inspirations, runway moments and evolving ideas around uniform dressing that have defined her output."I've been documenting my life through photos since high school when I got my first iPhone. Holding memories through photos has always felt as precious as keeping a childhood memento," Liang said in the announcement. "Sharing my life through my work feels intuitive for me - one does not feel complete without the other. This scrapbook of memories captures a decade of the brand through that lens."The visual language the book catalogs is instantly legible to anyone who has followed the label. Liang's collections have long trafficked in bows, Peter Pan collars, pleated skirts, ballet references, florals and kawaii touches, fusing a downtown New York attitude with cues pulled from memory, nostalgia and youth culture. A native New Yorker whose work draws heavily on growing up in Chinatown, she has turned that specific blend of femininity and intergenerational influence into a devoted global following, positioning the monograph as both a personal archive and a broader statement on her place in contemporary fashion.The book features contributions from Ava Nirui, the New York creative director known for her work on Heaven by Marc Jacobs, and Dean DiCriscio, a stylist who splits his time between New York and Los Angeles. Beyond documenting Liang's decade

items.title: BAPE Splits the Toe on Its MANHUNT Moc With the Sashiko-Stitched "MANHUNT Tabi"
items.text: BAPE Splits the Toe on Its MANHUNT Moc With the Sashiko-Stitched "MANHUNT Tabi" Name: A Bathing Ape MANHUNT TabiColorway: BlueSKU: TBCMSRP: ¥39,600 JPY (approx. $250 USD)Release Date: September 4Where to Buy: BAPEBAPE is putting a traditional spin on one of its sneaker mainstays with the MANHUNT Tabi, a new shoe that reshapes the label's MANHUNT silhouette around the split-toe form of Japanese tabi socks. The result reworks a familiar streetwear base through the lens of Japanese dress, landing somewhere between a heritage object and a modern sneaker.The craft detailing is where the meeting of old and new plays out. Rather than a printed graphic, the upper leans on sashiko, the centuries-old Japanese stitching technique, layering delicate needlework and patchwork across the shoe as a nod to the texture and handwork of the artisans behind it. An indigo-based color scheme reinforces the reference, tying the design to a palette long associated with traditional Japanese textiles while keeping the overall look restrained.That heritage framing is balanced against BAPE's own footwear engineering. The tabi is built on a lightweight MANHUNT outsole and finished with a wide Vibram sole unit, the specialist rubber the source positions for durability and grip in daily use. The pairing lets the shoe carry its traditional cues without giving up the comfort and wearability expected of a contemporary sneaker, which is the tension the brand frames as the whole point: tradition and innovation meeting in a single silhouette.The MANHUNT Tabi arrives in a single blue colorway, keeping the focus on the stitching and the split-toe construction rather than splitting the concept across multiple finishes. It reads as a fairly pointed entry in the long lineage of Japanese labels reinterpreting the tabi, filtered here through BAPE's specific streetwear vocabulary. items.title: TAG Heuer Marks 50 Years of the Monza With a Stealthy Forged Carbon Flyback Edition
items.text: TAG Heuer Marks 50 Years of the Monza With a Stealthy Forged Carbon Flyback Edition Summary TAG Heuer celebrates 50 years of Monza with a limited Flyback Chronograph.It features a 42mm forged carbon case with a motorsport‑inspired dial, and runs on a COSC‑certified Calibre TH20‑12.Limited to 500 pieces and retails for $13,400 USD. TAG Heuer marks the 50th anniversary of the Monza with the launch of the Monza Flyback Chronograph, unveiled ahead of the Formula 1 Pirelli Gran Premio d’Italia 2026. Limited to 500 numbered pieces, the watch pays tribute to the original 1976 model created to celebrate Niki Lauda’s championship victory with Ferrari, while embracing modern materials and technical innovation.Housed in a modern 42mm cushion-shaped case crafted entirely from forged carbon, the watch features a unique marbled texture that makes each individual piece unique while offering exceptional strength and lightweight comfort on the wrist. The matte black dial honors the 1976 model's visual codes with bold red accents and high-legibility layout features, including white lacquered hands filled with Super-LumiNova.Positioned across the dial are two sub-counters at 3 and 6 o'clock, an angled date window at 9 o'clock, and an outer black flange that incorporates both a tachymeter and a pulsometer scale. The case is capped with a fixed carbon bezel and domed sapphire crystal, while a black DLC steel crown and pushers complete the dark, stealthy exterior.Visible through the grade 2 titanium sapphire caseback is the in-house, COSC-certified Calibre TH20-12. The automatic movement features a flyback chronograph function, enabling wearers to reset and restart timing intervals with a single press of the pusher. Completing the design is a black perforated calfskin strap with red stitching, echoing classic motorsport style. Available via TAG Heuer, the Monza Flyback Chronograph is priced at $13,400 USD. items.title: SpongeBob Trades Bikini Bottom for the Grand Line in McDonald's ‘SpongeBob SquarePants’ x ‘ONE PIECE’ Happy Meal
items.text: SpongeBob Trades Bikini Bottom for the Grand Line in McDonald's ‘SpongeBob SquarePants’ x ‘ONE PIECE’ Happy Meal Summary McDonald's is running a SpongeBob SquarePants x ONE PIECE Happy Meal that dresses Bikini Bottom's residents as the Straw Hat PiratesThe collectible toys pair off characters from each cast, led by SpongeBob standing in for Monkey D. LuffyThe launch is backed by a special animated intro that merges the two seafaring worlds McDonald's is turning its Happy Meal into a crossover between SpongeBob SquarePants and ONE PIECE, a set of collectible toys that reimagines the Bikini Bottom cast as the Straw Hat crew. The tie-up leans on the shared nautical DNA of both franchises, mapping one universe's characters onto the other's rather than simply packaging them side by side.Each toy reworks a familiar Bikini Bottom character into a member of the ONE PIECE crew, starting with SpongeBob himself cast as captain Monkey D. Luffy. From there the swaps run deep: Patrick Star takes on Roronoa Zoro, Sandy Cheeks becomes Nami, Plankton stands in for Usopp, Squidward is remade as Sanji, and Gary the snail is reimagined as Tony Tony Chopper. The roster reaches further down both casts. Additional figures cast Pearl Krabs as Nico Robin, Larry the Lobster as Franky, Mr. Krabs as Jinbe and the town's longest-named resident as the skeleton musician Brook, filling out most of the core crew across the set. The exact number of toys is not fully settled across early coverage, with counts reported at both 13 and 15, so the final tally is worth pinning down before publication.More than a straight toy drop, the collaboration arrives with its own animated introduction. The short piece merges the visual worlds of both properties, sending the two casts crashing together in a single sequence rather than keeping them in separate frames. The result frames the Happy Meal less as a giveaway and more as an event, complete with promotional animation built specifically for the mashup.The McDonald’s SpongeBob SquarePants x ONE PIECE Happy Meal is rolling out across more than 60 territories on staggered regional dates, with a United States launch cited for September 15. Read more at Hypebeast

items.title: Seiko Revs Up Retro Motoring Style With Two Speedtimer Additions
items.text: Seiko Revs Up Retro Motoring Style With Two Speedtimer Additions Summary Seiko launches the Prospex Heritage Motoring Countdown Speedtimer HBC003 & HBC004, inspired by the 1969 Speedtimer.Powder Blue recalls the 1972 “Panda”; Petrol Blue channels 1970s “young‑timer” cars.Both feature 6R55 calibre, 72‑hour reserve, 200m water resistance. Seiko Prospex has expanded its motorsport-inspired lineup with two new timepieces: the Heritage Motoring Countdown Speedtimer in Powder Blue (HBC003) and Petrol Blue (HBC004). Drawing inspiration from Seiko’s groundbreaking 1969 Speedtimer - the world’s first automatic chronograph equipped with both a vertical clutch and column wheel - these new releases bring a refined 1970s automotive aesthetic to a modern, time-and-date format.The Powder Blue draws from Seiko’s 1972 “Panda” chronograph, featuring a flowing case shape and a light blue dial beneath curved sapphire crystal. A countdown timer with Lumibrite detailing enhances clarity, reinforcing its motorsport‑ready functionality. Meanwhile, the Petrol Blue HBC004 channels the neo‑classic “young‑timer” cars of the 1970s. Its rich petrol blue dial is paired with a sustainable LWG‑approved leather strap embossed with patterns inspired by vintage car interiors, creating a strong connection to automotive heritage.Housed in a compact, versatile 39.5mm stainless steel case AND measuring 12mm in thickness, the watches run on Seiko's in-house 6R55 automatic movement. Delivering a 72-hour power reserve and a date window discreetly positioned at 4:30, the timepieces also boast a robust 200-meter water resistance rating. Both references are available for pre-order starting now via Seikoboutique.co.uk, with retail pricing set between £840 - £870 GBP (approx. $1,137 - $1,177 USD). items.title: Universal Studios Hollywood’s ‘Fast & Furious:’ Hollywood Drift Races to a September 16 Opening
items.text: Universal Studios Hollywood’s ‘Fast & Furious:’ Hollywood Drift Races to a September 16 Opening Summary Universal Studios Hollywood has set a September 16 opening for 'Fast & Furious:' Hollywood Drift, its first outdoor high-speed coasterThe ride runs independently rotating cars across 4,100 feet of aerial track at speeds up to 72 mphUniversal is billing it as the fastest roller coaster in its global portfolio Fast & Furious: Hollywood Drift, the new high-speed roller coaster at Universal Studios Hollywood, will open to the public on September 16. Positioned as the park's first outdoor high-speed coaster, the ride translates the franchise's obsession with drifting into a physical system of spinning cars racing along an elevated track.Each car uses 360-degree rotation technology, spinning independently as the train moves so riders feel the sensation of a car breaking traction and drifting rather than simply cornering. Because the cars are programmed individually, the experience shifts depending on which vehicle a rider is seated in. The coaster reaches up to 72 mph across roughly 4,100 feet of aerial track, a distance the park compares to about 12 football fields, with the layout threading over sections of the park below. Universal frames it as the fastest roller coaster in its global lineup of parks.The build had to bend to its surroundings. Rather than clearing flat ground, the team routed the coaster down the terraced hillside of the Upper Lot, using the steep natural grade of the studio site as the structure's backbone and housing it within a red-brick, garage-themed facade. A portion of the track also runs through a transparently encased stretch of the queue, letting waiting guests watch cars race past mid-line.The vehicles themselves pull directly from the films. The ride cars are modeled on some of the saga's most recognizable machines, including Dominic Toretto's 1970 Dodge Charger, Han's Mazda RX-7, and Brian O'Conner's blue Nissan Skyline GT-R and orange Toyota Supra. The queue extends the theming with recreated props from the films and QR-code displays that open additional behind-the-scenes content through Universal's Backlot Club fan platform.Fast & Furious: Hollywood Drift opens at Universal Studios Hollywood on September 16, following earlier delays that Universal addressed in part by installing transparent sound-reduction barriers along portions of the ride. items.title: BEAMS BOY Waterproofs the Clarks Desert Trek With GORE-TEX and a Two-Layer Vibram Sole
items.text: BEAMS BOY Waterproofs the Clarks Desert Trek With GORE-TEX and a Two-Layer Vibram Sole Name: BEAMS BOY x Clarks Desert Trek GORE-TEXColorway: MochaSKU: 13320068100MSRP: ¥33,000 JPY (approx. $210 USD)Release Date: September 2026Where to Buy: BEAMSBEAMS BOY and Clarks have rebuilt the Desert Trek for wet weather, fitting the long-running silhouette with a GORE-TEX membrane in a new special-order model. The collaboration keeps the shoe's familiar shape while reengineering what protects and supports the foot, aimed at year-round, all-conditions wear.The weatherproofing is the headline change. The build integrates GORE-TEX for all-weather coverage, the source's stated case for wearing it through rain without hesitation, turning a traditionally fair-weather silhouette into something more rugged.Underfoot, the shoe uses a two-layer setup. A high-grip Vibram outsole is paired with a crepe midsole, and that stacked construction is what recreates the distinctive volume of the original Desert Trek rather than flattening it out. The leather upper is chosen to age with wear, gaining character the longer it's worn.Smaller details carry the collaboration's fingerprints. The insole is finished in a turquoise tone, a nod to the Native American jewelry long associated with BEAMS BOY, tucked out of sight as a quiet signature. The shoe also arrives with three interchangeable laces, so the finish can be dialed between understated and more playful depending on the day.The palette ties it together. The special order comes in a custom “Mocha” shade positioned between brown and beige, a restrained mid-tone meant to slide across everything from casual to trad styling. items.title: Cartier Skeletonizes the Tank Américaine for the First Time With the New 1988 MC Caliber
items.text: Cartier Skeletonizes the Tank Américaine for the First Time With the New 1988 MC Caliber Summary Cartier is expanding the Tank Américaine with a pair of skeleton watches and a burgundy Art Deco model, all keeping the collection's elongated, curved caseThe skeletons debut the hand-wound 1988 MC caliber, the first skeleton movement fitted to the Américaine, with bridges shaped as Roman numeralsThe skeletons come in platinum and rose gold, while the Art Deco model runs an automatic caliber in platinum Cartier is pushing the Tank Américaine into openworked territory for the first time, introducing two skeleton editions built around a new hand-wound caliber alongside an automatic model with a graduated burgundy dial. Each retains the elongated, curved case that has defined the Américaine since 1988, now used as a frame for very different technical and decorative treatments.The headline development sits under the crystal. Both skeleton watches run the 1988 MC, a manually wound movement making its Tank Américaine debut and named for the year the model itself launched. Rather than hiding the mechanics, Cartier shapes the movement's bridges into Roman numerals and suspends them within the case, so the openworked structure doubles as the dial's typography. The bridges curve to follow the case, reinforcing the vertical lines that give the Américaine its stretched silhouette. The caliber carries 24 jewels and beats at 28,800 vibrations per hour, with the movement measuring 33.9 x 20.8 mm across and 4.2 mm thick.The two skeletons are separated by metal and stone. The platinum reference pairs a matching platinum faceted crown set with a faceted ruby against blued-steel sword hands, and ships on two straps, a semi-matte burgundy alligator and a dark gray alligator, closed with a platinum interchangeable deployant buckle. The rose gold version swaps in a faceted sapphire on its crown, arrives on a navy blue alligator strap with a second dark gray strap, and offers roughly a 50-hour power reserve. Both measure 44.4 x 24.4 mm with a case 8.24 mm thick and are water-resistant to 3 bar.The third watch trades openwork for depth of color. The Tank Américaine large model in platinum runs the automatic 1899 MC caliber and centers on a burgundy dial worked in opaline and a satin sunray effect, matched to rhodiumized steel sword hands beneath a sapphire crystal. items.title: NOT A HOTEL and ‘Pokémon Sleep’ Turn a Poké Ball Into a Place You Can Actually Sleep In
items.text: NOT A HOTEL and ‘Pokémon Sleep’ Turn a Poké Ball Into a Place You Can Actually Sleep In Summary NOT A HOTEL and Pokémon Sleep have announced a collaboration centered on a Poké Ball-themed hotel in HokkaidoThe project reimagines the Poké Ball as a restful space for people, echoing the sleep-tracking game at its coreA campaign will give entrants the chance to stay in the one-off structure, with details due in mid-September NOT A HOTEL and Pokémon Sleep are joining forces on a Poké Ball you can spend the night inside. Set to appear in Hokkaido this September, the "Poké Ball-Themed Hotel" translates one of gaming's most recognizable objects into a real, stayable retreat, with the collaboration's full scope held back until a September 15 reveal.In the games, a Poké Ball is meant to be a comfortable home for the Pokémon inside it, and the collaboration extends that idea to human guests, shaping a space designed around deep rest and calm. That framing is a natural fit for Pokémon Sleep, the sleep-tracking app that turns a good night into a game, measuring and recording rest so players can collect the various sleeping poses of Pokémon gathering around a slumbering Snorlax.Realizing a spherical hotel as somewhere people can genuinely stay plays directly to NOT A HOTEL's wheelhouse. The company has built its name on treating architecture and technology as the whole point rather than a backdrop, commissioning one-off homes from established architects and creators and wrapping them in concierge-level service, part of a stated mission to raise the value of Japan itself. A Poké Ball dropped into the Hokkaido landscape is exactly the kind of high-concept build that reads as an extension of that approach rather than a novelty bolted onto it.For now, the brand is keeping the interior under wraps. The release stops short of showing what the space looks like or how a night in it unfolds, promising instead that the entirety of the "sleepable Poké Ball" will be unveiled on September 15. What is confirmed is the mechanism for getting in: rather than a public opening, the stay will be offered through a campaign, a winners-only experience that will not be open to the general public during its run.Full details on the Poké Ball-Themed Hotel, including how to enter the stay campaign, are set to be announced on September 15 via Pokemon Sleep.
