items.text: Off-White's "10x10: Icons Reimagined" Comes to Life at Milan's "Imaginary Palace" Summary Off-White™'s "10x10: Icons Reimagined" project invited 10 global creatives to reinterpret 10 iconic Off-White pieces, culminating in the "IMAGINARY PALACE" exhibition during Milan Fashion Week.The exhibition ran from September 23–24 at Off-White's Milan space, showcasing final pieces alongside their creative references and process. Off-White™ unveiled its “10x10: Icons Reimagined” project with “IMAGINARY PALACE," a two-day exhibition during Milan Fashion Week, illuminating the exponential potential of creative collaboration. The “10x10: Icons Reimagined” project manifested earlier this year, inviting 10 global creative forces to approach 10 of its most recognizable icons as blank canvases — starting points for personal interpretation, experimentation, and rebellion. From musicians Scott Mescudi and A$AP Nast to designers Ava Nirui, Yuta Hosokawa, Raul Lopez, and Guillermo Andrade to multidisciplinary creatives Renell Medrano, Veneda Carter, Stéphane Ashpool, and Bafic, every 10x10 creator committed to following their personal vision, hacking the system, and taking their icon into the future by questioning everything. Spanning different disciplines, perspectives, and communities, the project replaced fixed rules with individual points of view. The resulting works are not homages, but continuations, opening the Off-White™ archive to transformation, allowing its legacy to evolve through the voices shaping culture and design today.Grammy Award-winning musician and fashion designer Scott Mescudi returns the "Out Of Office” sneaker to its sport codes while proposing the product as a platform — embracing use, movement, and freedom of expression. Photographer and director Renell Medrano applies her distinct perspective to new eyewear, turning her blank canvas into an investigation of looking, being seen, and perspective. Fashion designer and creative director Ava Nirui transforms the T-shirt, bringing her signature gender-neutral viewpoint and ’90s youth culture nostalgia to an everyday Off-White™ uniform and a social platform for identity, belonging, and community. 424’s designer and founder Guillermo Andrade approaches denim as an archive of memory, construction, and what came before — pairing his deep design expertise with the concept of Virgil as the muse. items.title: Jil Sander's Next PUMA Pack Strips Back the Classics
items.text: Jil Sander's Next PUMA Pack Strips Back the Classics SummaryJil Sander and PUMA are releasing minimalist, stripped-back versions of the classic Speedcat and Suede sneakers for SS27.The collaboration features monochromatic colorways and slim silhouettes, though an official release date and price remain unconfirmed.Jil Sander and PUMA are returning to refresh two PUMA classics through a lens of subtraction. ⁠Previewed at the Milan Fashion Week SS27 runway show by guests like King Princess and Space Afrika, the designer label is coming out with a stripped-back variant of the PUMA Speedcat and the PUMA Suede.⁠Instead of adding to the design of the Speedcat, creative director Simone Bellotti reduces it, replacing the signature Formstrip with a perforated shadow. ⁠Other than the small, golden Jil Sander logo on the lacing system, the Black colorway is entirely monochromatic, giving the smoothly shaped silhouette a luxurious feel in full leather. Taking after the Black colorway, the White Speedcat is also completely monochromatic; however, for those who prefer the signature detail, the white colorway boasts a streamlined suede Formstrip for variety. The new Jil Sander x Speedcat is also joined by a white Jil Sander x PUMA Suede, featuring tonal details to complete the lineup.⁠The partners' latest collaboration takes after the SS26 Jil Sander x PUMA K-Street, which dialled in on the slim-sneaker trend. "In recent years, the slim silhouette has become very fashionable again, but I’m not someone who really follows fashion; it’s something I have always liked," he said in an April interview with Hypebeast. "I’m not a huge fan of the big, chunky silhouettes. A very slim silhouette feels more “pure” in a way; it goes to the essence of the meaning of a shoe, without having too much design or material over it," he added.As of the time of writing, Jil Sander nor PUMA has confirmed the official release date or retail price. items.title: Nike Opens Its Massive Archive at New York’s Museum of Arts and Design
items.text: Nike Opens Its Massive Archive at New York’s Museum of Arts and Design Summary “Nike: Form Follows Motion” traces the brand from early running experiments to Air, Flyknit and Vaporfly.Archival prototypes, sketches and cultural ephemera show how Nike sneakers moved from performance tools into music, fashion and street culture. Before the Swoosh became shorthand, there were sketches, prototypes and plenty of trial and error. “Nike: Form Follows Motion,” now on view at New York’s Museum of Arts and Design, looks back at more than 50 years of the brand, from Bill Bowerman’s early waffle-sole experiments to Air Max, Jordans, Flyknit and Vaporfly. Originally organized by the Vitra Design Museum, the show pulls from Nike’s internal archive of more than 200,000 objects.Waffle Trainers, Air Force 1s, Air Jordans and Vaporflys all make an appearance, but there’s more to look at than the familiar footwear hits we've written so much about. Early samples, prototypes, sketches and old testing equipment show how some of these ideas actually started, often looking pretty far removed from the finished products we know now.The exhibition starts with Nike’s running roots before moving into the Air era. Frank Rudy’s early testing machine and air-bag prototypes are here, alongside material tracing Nike’s expansion into basketball, tennis, football and skateboarding. Michael Jordan, Serena Williams and LeBron James appear throughout, as do its legendary designers including Tinker Hatfield, Diane Katz and Eric Avar.Things get a little more technical from there. Nike Free, Flyknit and Vaporfly lead into the brand’s work around biomechanics, material research and the Nike Sport Research Lab. It’s a side of Nike that tends to get buried underneath the bigger cultural moments, but it explains a lot about how the shoes ended up looking the way they do.And for the last part of the show, it moves further away from pure performance and into the wider cultural domain. Fifty footwear examples sit alongside music videos, collaborations and other material tracing Nike through streetwear, fashion, music and sneaker cosigns. The Air Force 1, for example, became inseparable from hip-hop, while the Dunk found another life through skateboarding long after its basketball origins. Some sneakers became important for reasons that had very little to do with what they were originally designed for.The best parts of "Form Follows Motion" are probably the unfinished ones. items.title: Gucci SS27: Demna Distills His "Complete Personal Vision"
items.text: Gucci SS27: Demna Distills His "Complete Personal Vision" SummaryDemna’s Gucci SS27 show in Milan debuted a subdued collection in a purpose-built boutique, a contrast to his earlier, more nightlife-inspired runway shows.Menswear featured tailored, prep-inspired looks with novel horsebit details, while womenswear highlighted ’80s-inspired office attire and asymmetrical evening gowns.At Milan Fashion Week, Demna presented Gucci’s Spring/Summer 2027 “Store Show” in a massive purpose-built Gucci boutique, showcasing what the creative director called “my complete personal vision for the brand.” He concluded that “Gucci stands for being rooted in the desire to belong to a more glamorous world, and in the audacity to remake that world in your own image.”The vision is toned down compared to what the designer presented for his debut runway show for Fall/Winter 2026 and the following Resort 2027 in New York City. Those shows leaned into the more extravagant aspects of the brand, from the flashy nightlife looks to the UK Underground rappers who made appearances on the runway and in the front row. Away from the nightclub and neon-lit streets, this show was clearly set during the day — or rather, store hours. While there are some sparkling moments, the range is subdued compared to the previous collections.Beginning with menswear, the opening looks set a more tailored mood. A range of largely monochromatic black and white suiting was followed by bouts of prep-inspired style and streetwear. The prep-leaning looks, centering around regular-fit white khakis, were styled with Ivy classics: a tan Harrington jacket, a quilted navy jacket, and blazers worn over striped polo shirts and sweaters. In the more city-ready looks, leather came forward in jackets and accessories, along with more conspicuous red and green striped and monogrammed pieces. Notably, the signature horsebit loafer buckle was recontextualized in several ways: a recurring triple-stacked horsebit belt, a supersized horsebit trouser detail, and horsebit pocket buttons on shirting and outerwear.The everyday-leaning feel of the menswear extended to the women’s collection that followed. Pointy shoulders dominated a swath of office-appropriate looks, including blouse and skirt sets at midi and mini lengths. A distinctly ’80s and ’90s feel emerged with pleated tartan midi skirts styled with puffy-sleeved jackets and branded chain necklaces. items.title: Vincent Cassel Transforms Into Quasimodo for Netflix’s ‘The Hunchback, Soul of Paris’
items.text: Vincent Cassel Transforms Into Quasimodo for Netflix’s ‘The Hunchback, Soul of Paris’ Summary Netflix unveils first-look images of The Hunchback, Soul of Paris .Vincent Cassel leads Jean-François Richet’s 1830-set historical thriller.The film premieres globally on Netflix November 27, 2026. Netflix has unveiled the first-look images for The Hunchback, Soul of Paris, offering an early glimpse at Vincent Cassel’s transformation into the film’s central hunchback figure. The images were first revealed exclusively by Vanity Fair France, introducing the production’s grimy, period-driven vision of 1830s Paris alongside Cassel and fellow cast members Benjamin Voisin, Daphné Patakia and Karim Leklou.Voisin appears as a doctor intent on capturing the protagonist for medical experiments, while Leklou plays the Director of Security leading the pursuit through a city threatened by cholera and political unrest. Rather than leaning into the gothic fantasy or musical elements associated with some previous screen interpretations of Victor Hugo’s The Hunchback of Notre-Dame, the imagery points toward a grounded historical thriller shaped by disease, class tensions and a sustained manhunt.Directed by Jean-François Richet, The Hunchback, Soul of Paris reimagines the life of a man said to have partly inspired Hugo’s Quasimodo, relocating the story to the eve of the July Revolution in 1830 as its protagonist becomes caught between political upheaval, an impossible love and those seeking to experiment on him in pursuit of a cholera cure. The premise draws on archivist Adrian Glew’s theory that Hugo may have encountered a hunchbacked stone carver, though Richet has characterized that connection as a plausible starting point rather than established history. The film reunites Richet with Cassel following Mesrine and The Emperor of Paris, with the wider cast also including Noémie Lvovsky, Sébastien Pouderoux, Eli Nachmani and Alexis Rosenstiehl. Netflix will release The Hunchback, Soul of Paris globally on November 27, 2026. Click here to view full gallery at Hypebeast

items.title: Breguet Introduces Anniversary “Quai de L’Horloge” Guilloché Dials Across the Marine Line
items.text: Breguet Introduces Anniversary “Quai de L’Horloge” Guilloché Dials Across the Marine Line Summary Breguet refreshes its Marine 5517 and Marine Chronographe 5527.New versions feature hand-guilloché “Quai de l’Horloge” dials.White gold, rose gold and titanium cases span three-hand and flyback chronograph formats. Breguet has unveiled new iterations of two flagship models within its iconic Marine collection: the Marine 5517 three-hand model and the Marine Chronographe 5527. Anchored in the house's historic appointment in 1815 as Watchmaker to the French Royal Navy under Abraham-Louis Breguet, the updated designs balance maritime heritage with modern luxury. Both models introduce subtle architectural updates, such as repositioning the date window to 6 o'clock to enhance dial symmetry, alongside a gold applique at 12 o'clock and signature maritime details like a wave-shaped crown guard and a seconds hand counterweight shaped like the nautical "Bravo" flag.The Marine 5517 keeps the collection at its most streamlined with a 40mm case, three-hand display and date window repositioned to 6 o’clock for greater symmetry. Its gold dial is decorated by hand with Breguet’s “Quai de l’Horloge” guilloché, a motif introduced for the Maison’s 250th anniversary and inspired by both the contours of Paris’ Île de la Cité and Île Saint-Louis and the movement of water. The white-gold edition receives an ice-blue dial, the rose-gold version is rendered in black, and the titanium model adopts blue, with Breguet numerals, “apple” hands and nautical cues including a seconds hand referencing the “Bravo” maritime flag. The 42.3mm Marine Chronographe 5527 develops the same visual language around a flyback chronograph, now using two counters at 3 and 9 o’clock for elapsed minutes and small seconds, alongside the date at 6. Its hand-guilloché dial appears in blue-gradient treatments for the white- and rose-gold models and a grey gradient for titanium.Powering the 5517 is Breguet’s self-winding Calibre 777A, running at 4 Hz with a 55-hour power reserve, while the 5527 uses the automatic Calibre 582QA, pairing its flyback chronograph with a 48-hour reserve. Both watches are water-resistant to 100 meters and expose their movements through sapphire casebacks, where a gold oscillating weight shaped in reference to a ship’s rudder continues the nautical theme.The new models are available through Breguet boutiques and authorized retailers, with prices for the the 5517 ranging from $26,400 USD in

BAO is extending its Mid-Autumn Festival celebrations into October with a dedicated Moon Festival Set Menu, following the one-day Moon Market held outside BAO Borough on September 24. Drawing on the festival’s traditions of gathering, abundance and communal dining, the menu will be served at BAO King’s Cross, City, Borough and Marylebone from September 29 through October 25, with generous sharing platters intended to be ordered by the whole table. The seasonal program builds on BAO’s Taiwanese-inspired approach to buns and small plates, which has shaped the London restaurant group since founders Shing Tat Chung, Erchen Chang and Wai Ting Chung opened its first permanent Soho location in 2015.Priced at £35 GBP (approx. $46 USD) per person, the set menu opens with an individual Westholme x BAO Grilled Sacha Wagyu BAO, combining North Australian wagyu striploin marinated in umami-rich shacha sauce with braised shallots and daikon pickle. From there, the meal shifts into a communal platter of guest-chef BBQ skewers created by several of BAO’s industry friends. Mambow’s Abby Lee contributes Malay Chipirones, pairing grilled baby squid with squid ink and kaffir lime curry sauce, while culinary artist Nil Mutluer, also known as Heal Goblin, serves Xinjiang Lamb seasoned with cumin, coriander and chilli. Miga’s Mr Ko adds a Korean BBQ Ribeye skewer with sake and pickled celery, and Singburi’s Sirichai Kularbwong looks to a childhood favorite for his Khao Jee Sticky Rice, coating egg-washed sticky rice cakes with Maggi sauce and finishing them with pork floss. Smacked cucumbers, kimchi and lard soy rice round out the shared spread. Dessert continues the lunar theme with BAO’s Moon Face BAO, a special-edition bun filled with salted egg custard.Several elements of the celebration will also be available separately across all BAO locations from September 29, including the Moon Face BAO for £6 GBP (approx. $8 USD), the Westholme collaboration bun for £7.50 GBP (approx. $10 USD) and a Suntory Toki Apple Highball for £10 GBP (approx. $13 USD), developed around citrus, spice and warming autumn flavors. items.title: Ulysse Nardin Gives the Freak [ONE] Blue Enamel and Guilloché Dial Finishes
items.text: Ulysse Nardin Gives the Freak [ONE] Blue Enamel and Guilloché Dial Finishes Summary Ulysse Nardin expands Freak [ONE] with Blue Enamel and Guilloché editions.Both feature 44mm titanium cases and UN-240 movements.Limited to 99 pieces each, prices start at $80,000 USD. Ulysse Nardin is extending the Freak [ONE] with two limited-edition interpretations that bring traditional decorative crafts into one of the manufacture’s most unconventional mechanical platforms. The Freak [ONE BLUE ENAMEL] and Freak [ONE GUILLOCHÉ] arrive as Ulysse Nardin marks both its 180th anniversary and 25 years since the original Freak debuted in 2001.Of the pair, the Freak [ONE BLUE ENAMEL] places the emphasis on color and métiers d’art. For the first time, the Freak [ONE] is housed in a full 44mm titanium case, framing a white-gold hour disc engraved with a radiating sunray pattern and covered by hand in vivid blue enamel at Ulysse Nardin’s Donzé Cadrans atelier. The enamel is applied in successive layers and fired at approximately 800°C before being polished, creating a saturated surface that accentuates the movement’s rotating flying carousel. By comparison, the Freak [ONE GUILLOCHÉ] adopts a more restrained palette, with its hour disc decorated in a traditional diamond-pattern “maille” motif. The original pattern is created by hand before being transferred to the production discs using the traditional flinqué stamping process, then finished in a sand-toned CVD treatment that contrasts with the light-grey titanium case. The Blue Enamel is paired with a white ballistic-textured rubber strap, while the Guilloché receives a matching grey version.Both watches retain the Freak [ONE]’s UN-240 automatic calibre, whose flying carousel completes one revolution every 60 minutes to indicate the minutes, while the rotating hour disc makes one full turn every 12 hours. Approximately 95% of the movement’s components are designed to move, with its 229-part construction incorporating a silicon oversized balance wheel and hairspring, a DIAMonSIL escapement and Ulysse Nardin’s patented Grinder automatic winding system, delivering a 90-hour power reserve. Time is adjusted through the bidirectional bezel rather than a conventional crown, while the 2026 editions introduce a subtly softened bezel profile inspired by the [Super] Freak.Both models are limited to 99 pieces: the Freak [ONE BLUE ENAMEL] is priced at $89,800 USD, while the Freak [ONE GUILLOCHÉ] retails for $80,000 USD. items.title: Margaret Qualley and Sabrina Carpenter Join Tom Holland in Sony Pictures’ Upcoming Fred Astaire Biopic
items.text: Margaret Qualley and Sabrina Carpenter Join Tom Holland in Sony Pictures’ Upcoming Fred Astaire Biopic Summary Margaret Qualley and Sabrina Carpenter join Tom Holland in Sony’s Fred Astaire biopic.Qualley will play Adele Astaire, while Carpenter portrays Ginger Rogers.Paul King directs the long-developing film, which currently has no release date. Margaret Qualley and Sabrina Carpenter have joined Tom Holland in Sony Pictures’ long-developing Fred Astaire biopic, expanding the project’s central trio of performers. Holland remains set to portray the legendary dancer and actor, while Qualley will play his older sister and original stage partner Adele Astaire, and Carpenter will take on the role of Ginger Rogers, the screen partner with whom Astaire became one of Hollywood’s most enduring musical icons.Before his film career, Fred and Adele built a celebrated act together across Broadway and London’s West End, while his later collaborations with Rogers produced some of the defining dance sequences of Golden Age cinema. The casting also places three performers with extensive dance backgrounds at the center of the film, with Holland having previously starred in Billy Elliot the Musical on the West End.The currently untitled film has been in development for nearly five years, with Holland first revealing his involvement in 2021. Paddington and Wonka filmmaker Paul King is directing from a screenplay co-written with Steven Levenson, adapting Kathleen Riley’s book The Astaires: Fred & Adele. King has indicated that the story will place particular emphasis on Fred’s formative partnership with Adele - whose dancing survives in no known footage - before tracing his emergence as a Hollywood star alongside Rogers. Amy Pascal and Rachel O’Connor are producing through Pascal Pictures, with Holland also producing via his Billy17 banner; Fred Astaire’s daughter Ava Astaire McKenzie is supporting the project, while her son Tyler McKenzie serves as consultant and co-producer. items.title: Vacheron Constantin Introduces a Lighter Shade of Blue to the Overseas
items.text: Vacheron Constantin Introduces a Lighter Shade of Blue to the Overseas Summary Vacheron Constantin celebrates 30 years of Overseas with a 200-piece perpetual calendar.The 41.5mm white gold watch debuts a lighter azure dial, powered by the ultra-thin Calibre 1120 QP/1, which measures 4.05mm and runs until 2100. Vacheron Constantin is marking the 30th anniversary of its Overseas collection with a new Overseas Perpetual Calendar Ultra-Thin, pairing an 18K white gold case with a newly developed azure dial for the first time. Limited to 200 pieces, the anniversary edition builds on a collection first introduced in 1996 as the successor to the Maison’s sport-chic 222, before evolving through subsequent generations in 2004 and 2016. The current Overseas design retains signatures including its Maltese cross-inspired notched bezel and integrated bracelet, while its tool-free interchangeable strap system reinforces the collection’s longstanding emphasis on travel and versatility.Spotlighted at the heart of its dial is a lighter interpretation of Vacheron Constantin’s signature blue. Described as less intense and less saturated than the azure tone first introduced to the collection in 2016, the lacquered dial shifts in appearance according to the light and is paired with a matching blue moon-phase display. White gold hands, markers and calendar indications add contrast without disrupting the monochromatic composition, while blue Super-LumiNova accents aid nighttime legibility. The 41.5mm white gold case measures just 8.1mm thick, and arrives on an integrated white gold bracelet alongside interchangeable white and denim-blue rubber straps, all of which can be changed without tools.Powering the watch is the Maison's self-winding Calibre 1120 QP/1, an ultra-thin 4.05mm movement comprising 276 components and offering approximately 40 hours of power reserve. Its perpetual calendar tracks the date, day, month and leap-year cycle alongside moon phases, automatically accounting for differing month lengths and leap years without requiring correction until 2100. Visible through the sapphire caseback, the Geneva Seal-certified movement features Côtes de Genève, bevelling, perlage and satin-finishing, complemented by a 22K gold rotor engraved with the Overseas compass rose.Priced at $132,000 USD, the new Overseas Perpetual Calendar Ultra-Thin Azure Dial is limited to 200 examples. items.title: JJJJound x New Balance 990v3 Revealed in Tan Suede
items.text: JJJJound x New Balance 990v3 Revealed in Tan Suede SummaryThe FW26 JJJJound x New Balance 990v3 features a monolithic tan suede upper with contrasting black accents, dropping the previous mesh base.The USA-made shoe includes discreet branding, though an official release date and retail price have not yet been announced.For FW26, JJJJound and New Balance are delivering yet another variant of the New Balance 990v3, a silhouette the collaborators have reimagined time and time again since the very start of their partnership. The 990v3 is not only the first JJJJ x NB silhouette, debuting in 2018, but also the subject of four more releases since then. Now the JJJJound x New Balance 990v3 returns in a familiar palette, echoing the hues of their debut shoe with a streamlined executionComposed of full tan suede uppers, the design gets contrast from a black N logo on the lateral and an all-black sole. Across the tongue, “New Balance USA” calls out its USA-made provenance, having originated at the shoemaker’s New England production facilities. JJJJound’s signature branding appears only on the black insoles, aligning with the Montreal label's discreet approach to brand identity. Notably, the shoe borrows some details from the 2018 JJJJ x NB 990v3, including the tan suede upper details and the black N logo. However, for 2026, JJJJound forgoes the tonal detailing and mesh backdrop for a monolithic look, interrupted only by the few striking black details.As of the time of writing, JJJJound has not announced the official release date or retail price for its latest rendition of the New Balance 990v3. items.text: Bottega Veneta SS27 Is About Wearing Less & Feeling More SummaryLouise Trotter’s Bottega Veneta SS27 collection embraces relaxed tailoring, trading heavy furs for breathable layers, deconstructed coats, and translucent fabrics.Monochromatic everyday looks are elevated by delicate lace collars, scarf-fusions, and floral fringes, capturing a quiet, optimistic shift toward summer.On September 26th, Bottega Veneta presented its Spring/Summer 2027 collection at Milan Fashion Week, showcasing a more relaxed attitude in craft-forward details, intentional imperfection, and freedom — both physically and aesthetically. With her latest collection, Creative Director Louise Trotter distills the essence of “Summer beginning to bloom” through the lens of Bottega Veneta’s subtle but meticulous craftsmanship.Against the stiffer shoulders and busier looks of Trotter’s Spring/Summer 2026, the latest collection allows “definition” around gender and “tailoring” to “loosen,” in the words of the show notes. Relating her approach to the gentler seasons experienced in Milan, Trotter delivers “light changes” to the wardrobe for warmer months: leather outerwear remains, as do wool trousers and sharply cut blazers. However, gone are the ultra-plush fiberglass furs of Spring/Summer 2026, and the hairy overcoats from Fall/Winter 2026. This season features lighter layers, less strict silhouettes, and endearing details like florals, crochet, and translucent fabrics.One model wore a black trench coat with deconstructed sleeves and shoulders that freed the arms, while the collar of a black peacoat mutated into a light shoulder wrap on one side. There are also quite simple, everyday looks, with a poetic twist: a lived-in tan leather pant paired with a plain white long-sleeve top crowned by a lace collar, and white trousers were worn with a lustrous pearl-colored button-up that fused into a scarf hung around the neck. In the brand’s discreet style, most looks linger around monochromatic and black-and-white palettes, but a handful of numbers stood out in playful colors: a violet blazer with pink satin pants and a purple intrecciatto cap, floral skirts and dresses dominated by cascading fringe florals. Elsewhere, roomy leather dresses and coats were dyed in red burgundy. The closing remarks of the show notes read, “There is optimism in lightness; in allowing the body, the clothes and perhaps oneself to move more freely. items.title: Willy Chavarria and adidas Originals Rework the Megaride for Fall 2026
items.text: Willy Chavarria and adidas Originals Rework the Megaride for Fall 2026 Name: Willy Chavarria x adidas Originals Mega Willy Low, Willy Chavarria x adidas Originals Willy Mega MidColorway: Black and Agave, BlackSKU: TBCMSRP: $230 USD, $280 USDRelease Date: October 3Where to Buy: adidas, CONFIRMED appadidas Originals and Willy Chavarria have built their Fall 2026 collection around the Megaride franchise, pairing the Mega Willy Low in Black and Agave with a Black Willy Mega Mid. The October capsule draws on '90s sportswear and scales up archival adidas shapes, continuing the designer's ongoing work with scale, identity and his own heritage.The footwear comes in two heights. The low-top Mega Willy Low arrives in two colorways, a Black pair and an Agave option, while the Willy Mega Mid raises the collar to a mid-cut and comes in Black only. The sporting references stay recognizable, but they now sit inside a fashion-led silhouette that belongs as much to the street as to the track. Click here to view full gallery at Hypebeast

items.title: Tigris Li Taps Hankook Tire to Find the Quiet Moments in Her Creative Process
items.text: Tigris Li Taps Hankook Tire to Find the Quiet Moments in Her Creative Process Artist and technologist Tigris Li is pushing the boundaries of creativity. Through her new AI-powered fragrance experience, Index, she envisions sensory impulses with electronic hardware to encourage play. Though the output hinges on interaction and conversation, the practice behind making the installations is a quiet one, requiring her to pay close attention to engineering. In a new installment of Day in the Life, Li lets Hypebeast in on this creative process, which takes place across London. Going from her new studio to several stores and workshops around the city, the feature follows her in the driver’s seat of the electric-powered BMW iX3, equipped with Hankook’s revolutionary iON Evo tires, which make the journey smooth and help her maintain an element of peace between stops. “My creative process isn’t in just one location,” the technologist shares from the confines of her new studio space where she begins her day. “It can start wherever I am, whether that’s on a drive, on a walk, or at home. It’s a constant thing.” As routine dictates, she flicks through her handy red sketchbooks, reviews the daily tasks, and sets off in the SUV ready to pick up the final components for her installation. After weaving through traffic, Li selects the materials she needs from her go-to workshop and heads to the next destination to pick up the new laser-cut pieces making up the furniture element. “Days like today can be chaotic, but as soon as I get in the car, the noise of the city fades away; it really lets me tune in,” she mentions on the journey. The technologist particularly admires the addition of the iON Evo tires to her journey, sharing that the noise reduction “lets you put your thoughts together while still being with the movement of the city.”Once the components are collected, it's back to the studio to assemble the installation with Index co-founder Isabella Smith. “We’re excited to bring this to the public with our launch, she says. Just like Hankook’s tires have been specially designed with the user experience in mind, Li shares a similar sentiment in their own creation, adding, “To have everyone come in and enter this world that we are creating for them is the reason we design.”Discover the full Day in the Life installment with Tigris Li below. View this post on InstagramA post shared by HYPEBEAST (@hypebeast) You can now explore the Hankook iON Evo range on the brand’s website.

items.title: Louis Vuitton’s Monterey Timepiece Returns in Glossy Black and Heritage Green
items.text: Louis Vuitton’s Monterey Timepiece Returns in Glossy Black and Heritage Green Summary Louis Vuitton expands the Monterey with new black and green ceramic models.Both retain the 37mm pebble-shaped case and 12 o’clock crown.An in-house automatic movement replaces the original 1988 quartz caliber. Louis Vuitton is bringing the Monterey into its permanent collection with two new ceramic interpretations that revisit the House’s earliest experiments in wristwatch design. The Monterey traces back to the LV I and LV II, created in 1988 with Italian architect and designer Gae Aulenti as Louis Vuitton’s first wristwatches. Defined by their pebble-shaped cases and unconventional crown placement at 12 o’clock, the originals have attracted renewed collector interest in recent years, appearing in Nicolas Ghesquière’s FW25 and SS26 presentations as watches, pendants and belt accessories.Following the 2025 revival of the Monterey in a 188-piece yellow-gold edition, Louis Vuitton now translates the design into glossy black and green ceramic, bringing both versions into the collection on a non-limited basis. Both models retain the original’s compact 37mm proportions and recognizable Clous de Paris steel crown at 12 o’clock, while introducing a more contemporary material treatment. The green edition takes a near-monochromatic approach, matching its polished ceramic case with a matte green lacquer dial, white railway track and vivid yellow lacquered hour and minute hands — a color choice that nods to the yellow stitching associated with Louis Vuitton leather goods.The black version creates a sharper contrast between its glossy black ceramic case and matte white lacquer dial, punctuated by red hands and railway markings and a fine blue seconds hand; its black grained calfskin strap continues the red detailing through contrast stitching. Louis Vuitton produces the ceramic cases from zirconium oxide and pigments before machining, firing them above 1,000°C, manually grinding and finally hand-polishing them to achieve the Monterey’s smooth, reflective pebble-like form.The most substantial departure from the 1988 LV II sits inside the case. In place of the original quartz movement, both Monterey Ceramic models use Louis Vuitton’s in-house LFT MA01.02 automatic calibre, a 174-component movement offering a 45-hour power reserve and running at 28,800 vibrations per hour. items.title: Burton Raids Zeb Powell's Wardrobe for "Zeb's Closet," a Baggy Outerwear Collection
items.text: Burton Raids Zeb Powell's Wardrobe for "Zeb's Closet," a Baggy Outerwear Collection Summary Burton's first globally available outerwear and apparel collection with Zeb Powell pairs waterproof shells and utility details with his signature oversized fitsThe lineup spans heavyweight hoodies, jerseys, rugby shirts, shorts, reversible bucket hats and a reversible insulated vest designed for layeringA traveling installation called Zeb's Mobile Closet debuts in New York City before visiting key snowboarding destinations around the world Burton has launched Zeb's Closet, an outerwear and apparel collection built in partnership with team rider Zeb Powell. Burton bills it as the first globally available collection it has created with the snowboarder. The range is designed around Powell's personal style rather than performance specs alone, combining technical outerwear with the loose, oversized pieces he wears both on the mountain and off it.The design brief was simple: build what Powell would actually wear. In practice, that means waterproof outerwear, utility-driven detailing and premium construction, all cut into the roomy, baggy silhouettes closely tied to his look. Every piece is meant to allow unrestricted movement, so the fit supports the loose, freestyle way he rides.The rest of the range pushes further into streetwear. Heavyweight hoodies, jerseys, rugby shirts, tees, shorts and pants sit alongside reversible bucket hats and technical shells. All of it is intended to be stacked in layers and worn long after the last lap of the day. The standout piece is a reversible insulated vest, which gives riders a functional mid-layer with enough personality to wear on its own."It's called Zeb's Closet because it's actually what I would wear - on the mountain and off the mountain," Powell said in a statement. That on-and-off-hill crossover fits the larger picture Burton sees in the collection. The brand views Powell as the face of a new generation of snowboarding shaped by creativity, self-expression and the communities changing what the sport looks like. "Zeb has inspired an entirely new generation to see snowboarding differently," said Zach Nigro, Burton's Vice President of Brand & Sports Marketing.That community focus extends to the rollout through Zeb's Mobile Closet, a custom-built traveling installation modeled on Powell's own closet. items.text: The Nike Air Max 95 Big Bubble "Cow Print" Swaps Printed Graphics for Real Calf Hair Name: Nike Air Max 95 Big Bubble “Cow Print”Colorway: Phantom/Metallic Gold-Cacao Wow-Gum Medium BrownSKU: IR5113-001MSRP: $200 USDRelease Date: Holiday 2026Nike is taking the Air Max 95 Big Bubble in an animal-inspired direction with "Cow Print," a women's release covered in real brown and white calf hair. Underneath, a cream base keeps the rest of the palette muted so the brown and white patches stand out. Leather and mesh fill in the remaining sections of the upper, balancing the calf hair with more familiar materials.The smaller details work in the same tones. At the heel, a small Metallic Gold Swoosh adds a single bright accent to an otherwise earthy color scheme.Below the upper, the pair uses the Big Bubble setup seen on recent Air Max 95 releases. items.title: GREG LABORATORY fall winter 2026 FW26 Season 7 Collection Release Info
items.text: GREG LABORATORY fall winter 2026 FW26 Season 7 Collection Release Info Summary GREG LABORATORY's Fall/Winter 2026 collection, "Time Loosens Reality," explores how the passing of time shapes the people who wear its clothesReturning staples come back in heavier fabrics, including a water-repellent cotton-nylon pant and suiting in cotton-silk blends and poly wool twillsNew pieces include a double-face fleece full-zip sweater, an updated Ventile technical jacket and a high-pile fleece vest GREG LABORATORY has released its Season 7 collection, "Time Loosens Reality," for Fall/Winter 2026. The theme is time itself, including both its rewards and its toll, and how it shapes the brand's recurring cast of "Protagonists." In practice, that idea shows up in clothing designed to age well: everyday staples built to work across seasons, climates and settings.Fabric is central to the collection. GREG LABORATORY mixes natural and synthetic fibers throughout the range, aiming for pieces that perform, stay practical and hold up over years of wear. The approach fits how the label works overall: every garment is designed, tested and made in New York City using performance-focused Japanese materials.Several returning staples now come in heavier fabrics. The brand's signature pant comes back in a heavyweight cotton-nylon with added water repellency, making it more suited to bad weather. The returning shirt and suiting move into weightier cotton-silk blends and textured poly wool twills, giving the tailoring more structure for colder months.The newer pieces build on earlier designs. The full-zip sweater updates a past model in a double-face fleece that is both heavier and softer to the touch. The technical jacket from Spring/Summer 2026 also returns in a more refined version, now made in mid-weight Ventile with a DWR finish, with hidden chest and hand pockets, and with pleating across the back that gives it a rounder shape.The most notable addition is the new High Pile Fleece Vest. It is lined in the same fabric as the shell and cropped to sit right at the waist. It has two hand pockets plus the circular chest pockets that have become a GREG LABORATORY signature.GREG LABORATORY's Season 7 "Time Loosens Reality" collection is available now exclusively online. items.title: Focus Features Unleashes Haunting Second Trailer for Robert Eggers’ ‘WERWULF’
items.text: Focus Features Unleashes Haunting Second Trailer for Robert Eggers’ ‘WERWULF’ Summary Robert Eggers’ WERWULF gets a new official trailer.Aaron Taylor-Johnson, Lily-Rose Depp and Willem Dafoe lead the medieval horror film. WERWULF opens exclusively in theaters on December 25, 2026. Focus Features has unveiled the latest official trailer for Robert Eggers’ WERWULF, offering a more unsettling look at the filmmaker’s stripped-back approach to werewolf folklore. Set in 13th-century England, the footage places Aaron Taylor-Johnson’s unnamed Man at the center of a brutal transformation, moving through mud-soaked landscapes, religious dread and mounting suspicion as his condition begins to consume him. The trailer builds around physical deterioration and the fear spreading through the surrounding community, while Lily-Rose Depp appears as Woman and Willem Dafoe as Old Hunter.WERWULF follows Eggers’ 2024 Nosferatu and reunites the director with Taylor-Johnson, Depp and Dafoe, while also bringing back The Northman collaborator Sjón as co-writer. Eggers has positioned the film as an attempt to return lycanthropy to its older folkloric roots, moving away from familiar Hollywood conventions such as silver bullets and other modern werewolf mythology in favor of the superstitions and anxieties of medieval Europe. The latest trailer arrives alongside a wider promotional campaign built around the lunar cycle, including an alternate reality game timed to full moons leading up to the film’s release. WERWULF is set to open exclusively in theaters on December 25, 2026. Read more at Hypebeast

items.title: Tan Suan: Reshaping Time Beneath Light and Shadow
items.text: Tan Suan: Reshaping Time Beneath Light and Shadow For Hypebeast China's latest digital cover, we have no interest in retelling the overnight-success myth of a fashion influencer. Instead, through Tan Suan, we want to reflect how an entire generation of young women creators grows and defines itself as time moves forward. Her path from individual creator to a broader cultural presence also offers a window into how China's new generation of creative talent is being seen by the world, and how it is starting to shape global fashion and luxury culture.In an era that treats "effortlessness" as gospel, ease is the aesthetic face she presents to the world. Her deep reverence for the craft and her constant self-scrutiny are the homework she keeps for herself. The outside world tends to reduce top-tier access, flawless polish and an idealized life into data points and labels. On the other side of the light is her clear-headed reflection. Social media may capture her present, but it cannot simply define what kind of woman she is. Her humility and focus, her habit of "keeping herself low," is not timidity. It is a creator's deepest instinct: to avoid the floating froth of a restless visual tide and build her own aesthetic order and artistic perspective.This is not only about Tan Suan. It captures a moment in which women creators are moving from "being looked at" to "expressing themselves." They are no longer content to be pretty faces generating noise and numbers in front of the camera. Over time, they are turning the camera into an extension of self-expression and artistic exploration. In fast-cycling pop culture, she delivers liveliness and cool with precision in front of the lens. Behind it, she quietly refines the aesthetic logic behind her content, her deeper understanding of style, and the ultimate question of "who am I."Tan Suan's trajectory also offers an entry point into how Chinese creative culture is changing. In the past, young Chinese creators were largely watched and defined within the context of global fashion and pop culture. Today, more and more of China's new creative talent is entering conversations around global fashion and luxury on the strength of their own taste, visual language and cultural experience, and becoming part of what shapes trends and sets context. items.title: Saucony Goes Full “Space Cowboy” With a Five-Shoe Collection
items.text: Saucony Goes Full “Space Cowboy” With a Five-Shoe Collection Name: Saucony “Space Cowboy” CollectionMSRP: TBCRelease Date: October 2Where to Buy: SauconySaucony is merging futuristic runner aesthetics with Americana in its expansive new "Space Cowboy" Collection. Translating classic Western motifs across five silhouettes that span archival runners, lifestyle footwear and modern performance models, this release spotlights the Progrid Triumph 4, Progrid V2, 586i, Endorphin Elite 3 and Endorphin Azura silhouettes.The ProGrid Triumph 4 “Space Cowboy” delivers the collection’s most overtly futuristic interpretation, layering burnt-orange mesh and leather with high-shine chrome overlays and Saucony branding. Brown-and-white cow-print hair covers portions of the toe and heel, while black accents and speckled rope-style laces add further contrast to the heavily layered design. The ProGrid V2 takes a warmer approach, pairing white mesh with cognac-toned leather panels embellished with decorative Western-style stitching. Chrome sections around the toe and heel supply a metallic counterpoint, while tufts of cow-print hair around the collar reinforce the ranch-inspired theme.The 586i “Space Cowboy” shifts away from the animal-print treatment in favor of details borrowed more directly from traditional Western boots. Its predominantly black leather upper is traced with highly visible white contrast stitching, including embroidered motifs around the toe and side panels, while braided black-and-white laces heighten the graphic effect. A wide fringed tongue panel secured by metallic studs becomes the defining feature, introducing a tassel-like finish reminiscent of Western leatherwork. A translucent brown gum sole softens the otherwise monochromatic palette, giving the lower-profile silhouette a warmer, vintage character compared to the more metallic ProGrid models.The Elite 3 dresses its technical black mesh upper with brown suede-like accents around the tongue and collar, while a cow-print band wraps above its exaggerated, mirror-like silver midsole, creating the collection’s strongest collision of Western texture and space-age shine. The Endorphin Azura reverses that balance with a largely white engineered-mesh upper, black and chrome detailing and warm brown accents, while cow-print graphics wrap portions of its thick sculpted midsole. items.title: AFTERSHOCK's $14,200 USD Cherry Bloom Gaming PC Has 70 Hand-Painted Titanium Petals That Bloom With Heat
items.text: AFTERSHOCK's $14,200 USD Cherry Bloom Gaming PC Has 70 Hand-Painted Titanium Petals That Bloom With Heat Summary AFTERSHOCK released the Cherry Bloom, a $14,200 gaming rig built around a kinetic cherry blossom sculptureThe interior features 70 hand-formed titanium petals that physically curl open as the system heats upThe hardware is powered by a Ryzen 7 9800X3D processor, a Zotac RTX 5080 GPU and 64GB of memory AFTERSHOCK has officially launched the Cherry Bloom. This $14,200 USD rig features a heat-reactive cherry blossom tree planted inside the chassis and is billed as the world's first blooming gaming PC. The entire build sits securely inside an APNX V2 chassis wrapped in glass across a full 270 degrees.Seventy hand-formed and hand-painted blossoms make up the system's kinetic center. A titanium alloy specifically engineered to react to heat comprises these blossoms. The mechanical movement relies entirely on the metal responding to temperature without using motors, software firmware or RGB lighting. A demonstration shows the Cherry Bloom sitting fully closed at a resting temperature of 18 degrees Celsius. As internal temperatures rise, the metal petals physically curl open before folding shut once the machine cools.A Ryzen 7 9800X3D processor paired with a Zotac RTX 5080 graphics card powers the rig. The system pushes output using 64 gigabytes of DDR5-6000 memory and a 2TB PCIe Gen4 SSD. This build includes a 1300W Platinum power supply to support the components. While the titanium tree provides the visible mechanical display, a custom open-loop liquid cooling system handles the internal thermal load.The Cherry Bloom hit the market priced at roughly $14,200 USD, converted from an asking price of $19,995 AUD. Customers can order the machine now with next-business-day dispatch, though the price does not include shipping. This strategy reflects a luxury approach where the engineering and hand-finishing of reactive metal petals account for much of the cost. By turning exhaust heat into a visible display, the system transforms thermal management into kinetic art. Click here to view full gallery at Hypebeast

items.title: The World's First ‘Minecraft’ Roller Coaster Launches Riders Out of the Nether
items.text: The World's First ‘Minecraft’ Roller Coaster Launches Riders Out of the Nether Summary Escape the Nether puts riders in minecarts alongside Steve and Alex, fighting through hostile mobs and plenty of lava before launching back to the OverworldThe Minecraft Hotel features Nether Portal-inspired lifts, mine-tunnel corridors and bedrooms styled with the game's blocks, items, mobs and texturesBoth attractions anchor Minecraft World, a new land opening at Chessington World of Adventures Resort in 2027 Minecraft is getting its first roller coaster, Escape the Nether, as the headline ride of Minecraft World, a new land coming to Chessington World of Adventures Resort in southwest London in 2027. Alongside it is the Minecraft Hotel, the first official hotel built around the game. The land is being developed by Mojang Studios and Merlin Entertainments.Escape the Nether starts, like the game, in a minecart. Riders board and join Steve and Alex, Minecraft's default playable characters, on a run through the Nether, the game's fiery underworld dimension. Along the way they face hostile mobs head-on before a launch sends them back to the Overworld. The Nether setting also means the ride's scenery features lava throughout.The hotel is themed from the moment guests arrive. Check-in is designed to look like the Overworld, with blocky trees and animals setting the scene. The lifts are styled after Nether Portals, and the hallways are built to look like mine tunnels, so getting to a room feels like exploring the game.The bedrooms, which the hotel calls "respawn points," bring the game's visual style into real life. Rooms are designed with Minecraft's blocks, items, mobs, textures and colors, aiming to appeal to longtime players and newcomers alike.Food and drink follow the same approach, each tied to a specific part of the game. The restaurant is underwater-themed, inspired by Minecraft's ocean biomes. The bar is modeled on the Woodland Mansion, and its drinks are styled as the game's colorful potions. Beyond the ride and hotel, the wider land will include areas based on the Overworld's lush caves, mineshafts and plains, along with mob meet-and-greets, play areas and themed shops.Minecraft World, Escape the Nether and the Minecraft Hotel are set to open at Chessington World of Adventures Resort in 2027, with an exact date yet to be announced. items.title: NITRO MICROPHONE UNDERGROUND Drops New Track "Eclipse," Produced by MACKA-CHIN
items.text: NITRO MICROPHONE UNDERGROUND Drops New Track "Eclipse," Produced by MACKA-CHIN Legendary dream team NITRO MICROPHONE UNDERGROUND—a driving force in the Japanese hip-hop scene—has finally dropped their highly anticipated new track, "Eclipse." An official music video was released alongside the single.Production comes courtesy of crew mastermind MACKA-CHIN, who continues to carve out his own lane as a producer and DJ. The MCs trade verses with effortless fluidity over a solid, eerie, one-loop track infused with heavy dub techniques. For the mix, the group tapped master engineer D.O.I., a longtime pillar of the Nitro sound.The visuals are equally striking. Creative direction for the cover art and music video was spearheaded by Nitro MC GORE-TEX, the creative force behind the apparel brand raidback®︎fabric. Co-directed with filmmaker Hirotaka Shimizu, the video delivers a smoky, atmospheric aesthetic, blending ominously flickering lights in the pitch black with the commanding presence of each member.To mark the release, MACKA-CHIN shared the following message on Instagram:"It’s been a minute, but I made a track for NITRO! The instrumental’s theme is purely dope. Heavy dub on an insane one-loop. Honestly, it’s just the sound we're vibing with right now (my aging eyes are blinding me to whatever the rest of the world is doing). By the way, the MV was directed by Tora (GORE-TEX) alongside Nitro's 37th assassin, Shimizu. I’d be beyond thrilled if there are fans out there who’ve been waiting for a track dripping with this kind of underground flavor. What do you guys think?"— MACKA-CHIN"Eclipse" is top-tier underground hip-hop, seamlessly fusing the unique aesthetic the group has cultivated since the ’90s with the raw dopeness its members embody today. It’s a concentrated hit of the rugged, unfiltered Nitro attitude that fans have been craving—an absolute must-experience both sonically and visually.NITRO MICROPHONE UNDERGROUND "Eclipse"Label: NITRICHRelease Date: Wednesday, September 23, 2026Format: Digital ReleaseStreaming LinkAdditionally, the raidback®︎fabric x NMU LA TORA JACKSON THIRTEENHEARTS. "D'EVILSD’RIPS" HOODIE worn by the members in the "Eclipse" music video is currently available exclusively via their official online store. Offered in both white and black, the hoodie retails for ¥19,800 (tax included). Be sure to check it out alongside the new track and visual. items.title: Stephen Curry Signs a $116 Million USD Extension With the Golden State Warriors to Stay Through 2029
items.text: Stephen Curry Signs a $116 Million USD Extension With the Golden State Warriors to Stay Through 2029 Summary Stephen Curry agrees to a two-year, $116 million contract extension with the Golden State WarriorsThe historic agreement pushes Curry to approximately $650 million in guaranteed career earningsCurry accepts a discount of over $20 million to provide the franchise with vital salary cap flexibility Stephen Curry is securing his future while continuing his run in the Bay Area. This 38-year-old superstar agreed to a massive contract extension with the Golden State Warriors, a move the franchise formally announced. Valued at $116 million USD over two years, according to ESPN, the agreement ensures the defining player of this era remains exactly where he started. He enters his 18th NBA season, all of which have been played exclusively with the Warriors. The contract features a built-in player option for the 2028-29 NBA season.The scale of this extension rewrites the league's financial record books. This agreement pushes his trajectory higher and takes Stephen Curry to approximately $650 million USD in guaranteed career earnings, the highest total in NBA history. He stands as the highest-paid player in the league right now with a $62.6 million USD salary locked in for the 2026-27 season. Reports from ESPN indicate his cap figure will come in at $55.7 million USD for the 2027-28 season.Despite setting earnings records, the iconic guard took a deliberate pay cut to keep his squad competitive. Stephen Curry was eligible to pull in close to $137 million USD over the two-year span if he sought the maximum amount. Instead, he willingly absorbed a discount of more than $20 million USD below his maximum eligible salary. Accepting this reduction provides the Golden State Warriors with immediate salary cap flexibility. This financial sacrifice changes the team's outlook and prioritizes the ability to construct a championship-contending roster around their cornerstone rather than maxing out his personal payout.That level of organizational commitment reinforces his status within the building. Following the official announcement, Warriors general manager Mike Dunleavy highlighted the magnitude of the guard's impact. Dunleavy stated he does not think there has ever been a better face to a franchise in professional sports history than Curry. Click here to view full gallery at Hypebeast

items.title: ‘Avengers: Endgame Encore’ Reclaims the Box Office With an $86 Million USD Global Weekend
items.text: ‘Avengers: Endgame Encore’ Reclaims the Box Office With an $86 Million USD Global Weekend Summary 'Avengers: Endgame Encore,' Disney and Marvel's re-release of the 2019 blockbuster with added footage, topped the domestic box office over several new releasesThe film earned $26 million USD from 3,060 North American theaters and $60 million USD from international marketsThe result arrives ahead of 'Avengers: Doomsday,' which opens in December Avengers: Endgame Encore has returned to No. 1 at the domestic box office, finishing ahead of several new releases in its return to theaters. Disney and Marvel’s re-release of the 2019 blockbuster, which adds extra footage to the original cut, brought in $86 million USD worldwide over the weekend.In North America, the film earned $26 million USD from 3,060 theaters, which works out to an average of roughly $8,500 USD per location. That's a strong result for a film that has been available to stream at home for years. International audiences drove most of the total. Overseas markets added $60 million USD, more than double the domestic haul, bringing the global figure to $86 million USD.Those numbers are well beyond what re-releases usually earn. "Re-releases rarely earn more than $10 million USD," said David A. Gross, who publishes the box office newsletter FranchiseRe. Gross also pointed to the run's value as marketing, noting that it helps build early buzz for what Marvel has coming next.The next release is Avengers: Doomsday, which opens in December and brings back nearly the full Avengers roster for another fight to save the universe. With Endgame Encore posting numbers usually reserved for new releases, the re-release is an early sign of how much demand exists for Doomsday. Click here to view full gallery at Hypebeast

items.title: Unique Rolex "Four Seasons" Daytonas Shatter Records With $49.5 Million USD Charity Auction
items.text: Unique Rolex "Four Seasons" Daytonas Shatter Records With $49.5 Million USD Charity Auction Summary Rolex and Phillips auctioned four piece-unique Cosmograph Daytona timepieces for a record-breaking total of $49,467,260 USD (£37,300,000 GBP)Each watch interprets a different season using rare natural stone dials precious metals and custom gemstone bezelsAll proceeds directly support early childhood education through the Federer Foundation and environmental conservation via Re:wild Rolex and Phillips have made watchmaking history after selling four piece-unique Rolex Oyster Perpetual Cosmograph Daytona models for a record-breaking total of $49,467,260 USD (£37,300,000 GBP). Auctioned in London by Aurel Bacs, the historic single-consignment charity sale marks the highest amount ever raised for a watch charity event.Titled the "Four Seasons" collection, each timepiece reimagines the iconic chronograph through a distinct seasonal lens utilizing rare hard-stone dials, high-jewelry gem-setting, and precious metals. The "Winter" reference, cased in 950 platinum, fetched $13,262,000 USD (£10,000,000 GBP) with its blue opal dial, lapis lazuli sub-dials, and blue-to-fuchsia sapphire bezel. The 18 ct white gold "Spring" edition garnered $9,018,160 USD (£6,800,000 GBP), boasting a chrysoprase dial, lepidolite counters, and purple sapphires.Leading the individual sales, the "Summer" model in 18 ct Everose gold commanded $13,659,860 USD (£10,300,000 GBP) via a turquoise dial, heart of ruby sub-dials, and pink sapphires. Completing the quartet, the 18 ct yellow gold "Autumn" edition brought in $13,527,240 USD (£10,200,000 GBP) featuring a mookaite dial paired with chrysoprase counters and green tourmalines. All four references are driven by Rolex's in-house Calibre 4131 movement.100% of the proceeds will be split between Roger Federer’s Federer Foundation to support early childhood education across Southern Africa and Switzerland, and Leonardo DiCaprio’s Re:wild initiative dedicated to global ecosystem restoration.The four unique Rolex Cosmograph Daytona timepieces were sold individually via Phillips in London on September 28, 2026. Click here to view full gallery at Hypebeast

items.title: Kader Sylla Unveils First Signature Shoe With adidas Skateboarding
items.text: Kader Sylla Unveils First Signature Shoe With adidas Skateboarding SummaryKader Sylla’s first signature adidas shoe, the $110 "Kader," blends '90s basketball style with durable skate performance.The versatile suede sneaker launches today in two colorways, kicking off the North American leg of his global tour.Professional skater Kader Sylla has teamed up with adidas Skateboarding to introduce his first-ever signature sneaker: The Kader. Arriving today in two colorways, the Kader is both an ode to adidas archives and a non-traditional development of adidas' signature details.“I wanted to make something that felt like me and that I’d actually want to wear every day,” Kader shared in an official statement. "We looked at a lot of different references and kept pushing until it felt right. It’s built for skating, but it doesn’t feel limited to the skatepark. I’m excited for people to experience it and take it wherever they go," he added.Drawing core inspiration from '90s adidas Equipment basketball silhouettes, the mid-top model is engineered for versatility from the streets to the skatepark. In brown suede with yellow snake stripes and black suede with purple speckled stripes, the Kader reinterprets the iconic Three Stripes by integrating them directly into the lacing system, blending branding with functional details. Built for heavy impact, the sneaker features a durable cupsole, a full-length Lightmotion midsole, Adituff underlays, and a premium suede upper.To celebrate the launch, Kader is taking his kicks on the road for a massive global World Tour. The North American leg kicks off tomorrow, October 1, bringing demos and skateshop appearances to local communities from Minneapolis to Los Angeles.Kader Sylla's adidas Skateboarding signature shoe is available now for $110 USD at adidas. Click here to view full gallery at Hypebeast

items.title: InScope's Hayley Smith on What Galleries Keep Getting Wrong
items.text: InScope's Hayley Smith on What Galleries Keep Getting Wrong Summary 'State of Art' is a new HypeArt series inviting artists, curators, collectors and other leading voices to weigh in on the ideas, debates and cultural shifts shaping contemporary art. Through intimate questions and personal recommendations, the series offers a closer look at what is exciting the art world, what needs to change and where things may be heading next. For decades, gallery representation was seen as a major sign that an artist had made it. Galleries opened doors to collectors, institutions and curators, while artists depended on them to build visibility, establish a market and grow their careers. That dynamic is starting to shift.Artists can now build global audiences, sell work directly, stage their own shows and create communities without waiting for traditional gatekeepers. But for Hayley River Smith, director of InScope (formerly Scope Art Show), that does not mean galleries are losing their relevance. It means the relationship between artists and galleries has to change.For the latest edition of Hypeart’s ‘State of Art,’ Smith talks about what meaningful representation looks like in 2026, whether the traditional 50/50 split still holds up and why belief, trust and real investment in an artist may matter more than representation alone."What people are craving now is real connection beyond what is transactional."Do artists still need galleries? Why or why not?For me the question isn't whether artists need galleries anymore rather what we want that relationship to be. We have spent a long time painstakingly applauding what is predictable. We know what a gallery is supposed to do, what an artist is supposed to do, what a fair is supposed to look like, and what success is supposed to look like. We have reached a point where we're looking at that model grimacing while we all continue to participate in the sameness of it all.Artists have more ways to build audiences and sell work directly than ever before, but that doesn't mean the relationships are less important. The opposite is true.What people are craving now is real connection beyond what is transactional. The best gallery relationship can offer exactly that: someone who knows the artist, understands the work, takes a risk on it, and is invested in where that practice could go rather than simply what can be sold this season. items.title: Blue Bottle’s First Jazz Album Is Made for Slow Listening
items.text: Blue Bottle’s First Jazz Album Is Made for Slow Listening Summary Blue Bottle Coffee debuts Notes in Repose , its first limited-edition jazz vinyl.It features 10 contemporary tracks interspersed with ambient cafe recordings.Limited to 1,500 copies, the release celebrates the brand's Signature Blends. Blue Bottle Coffee has unveiled Notes in Repose, its first-ever compilation album celebrating the shared language of jazz, coffee and composition. Created in celebration of its Signature Blends, the limited-edition vinyl brings together 10 contemporary jazz compositions from artists spanning nine cities across Blue Bottle’s North American and Asian cafe markets.The lineup includes Ali Shaheed Muhammad, Makaya McCraven, Jeff Parker, Angel Bat Dawid and the Kyoto Jazz Sextet, with the individual tracks woven together by ambient recordings captured inside Blue Bottle cafes. Conceived as an invitation to slow down and listen with greater intention, the project draws a parallel between musical composition and coffee blending — bringing distinct elements together while preserving their individual character to create a more balanced whole.Jazz has influenced Blue Bottle's creative approach since its inception, rooted in founder James Freeman’s background as a working clarinetist and inspired by the focused listening environments of Japanese jazz kissas. This deep-seated connection to music is already evident in the brand's bold, chocolatey Giant Steps blend, named after John Coltrane's iconic 1960 composition. Even the title Notes in Repose reflects that sensibility, framing the record as a moment of pause in which coffee, sound and physical album artwork become part of the same experience. Limited to 1,500 copies, Notes in Repose will be available beginning October 6 via Blue Bottle’s website while supplies last, while Giant Steps remains available year-round online and at Blue Bottle cafes. Click here to view full gallery at Hypebeast

items.title: Nothing Headphone (1) Pro Bridges Everyday Listening and Studio Control
items.text: Nothing Headphone (1) Pro Bridges Everyday Listening and Studio Control Summary Nothing’s Headphone (1) Pro evolves the original with upgraded materials and a refined transparent design.A triple-driver system and Metropolis Studios tuning add more precise listening controls.Priced at $399 USD, it launches today via the brand's official webstore. Following the announcement of BTS' V as Nothing’s new Global Brand Ambassador, the London-based tech brand has officially unveiled its flagship audio release, the Headphone (1) Pro. Positioned as the London-based brand’s new flagship audio product, the over-ear headphones are conceived around bridging two traditionally separate listening environments: everyday wireless use and the more precise controls associated with studio work. Rather than departing from the visual identity established by the Headphone (1), the Pro model develops the same transparent, industrial vocabulary with upgraded materials, a revised internal architecture and a greater emphasis on customization.Aesthetically, the Headphone (1) Pro represents the most distilled execution of Nothing's signature transparent design language to date. Refining the brand's aesthetic approach, the outer ear cups feature shatter- and scratch-resistant 9H Panda glass that offers a subtle view of the complex internal architecture within. Available in sleek metallic black and white colorways, the chassis pairs lightweight aluminum with titanium, replacing conventional steel headband arms to reduce the total weight to 327 grams. Ergonomic enhancements—including a wider headband with thicker padding, softer ear cushions, and an adaptive fit—ensure long-lasting comfort across extended listening sessionsThe biggest change sits beneath that semi-transparent exterior. Where conventional headphones typically rely on a single driver, Headphone (1) Pro uses a three-driver architecture, dividing bass, midrange and treble duties between a bass dynamic driver, precision dynamic driver and xMEMS treble driver. Nothing has partnered with Metropolis Studios to extend that hardware toward more studio-minded listening, introducing a dedicated Flat EQ Switch for a neutral sound profile alongside “Studio B,” a Dynamic Spatial Audio mode modeled around the acoustic character of a mixing room. items.title: POST ARCHIVE FACTION (PAF) Rolls Out “Drifter” FW26 Collection
items.text: POST ARCHIVE FACTION (PAF) Rolls Out “Drifter” FW26 Collection Summary POST ARCHIVE FACTION’s FW26 collection revisits performance and established wardrobe forms.The Eclipse set uses strip-like paneling to create fluid movement.Pom-pom accessories, Petal Sneakers and Cut Out Boots round out the release. POST ARCHIVE FACTION (PAF) is rolling out its Fall/Winter 2026 collection following the season’s “Drifter” runway presentation earlier this year. The range reflects PAF’s continued interest in moving between performance-minded design and unconventional reinterpretations of established forms, with a subdued palette allowing its proportions, textures and construction details to take focus. Footwear further expands the collection’s interplay between technical and traditional references.Leading the release is the archival River Jacket, arriving in Sky Blue, Navy and Olive Green. Elsewhere, the Eclipse Bomber and its matching pants make a statement through their all-black palette and intricate construction. Built from an array of strip-like panels sewn together, the set creates a fluid, almost rippling effect with movement, while its stealthy color scheme keeps the overall look restrained.Other featured pieces extend into knitwear and accessories, ranging from a button-up cardigan to hats and gloves. Pom-poms emerge as a recurring motif, appearing at the top of the Pom Beanie across three versatile colorways, covering the Pom Pom Pom Trapper, and finishing each fingertip of the Pom Pom Gloves. Footwear rounds out the release with the low-profile Petal Sneakers, offered in Malva Grey, Brown, Black and White with a suede-like finish and subtle cutout detailing. Meanwhile, the lace-up Cut Out Boots arrive in black and earthy beige with a more classic construction. The FW26 drop will be available through PAF’s official webstore and authorized stockists worldwide. Click here to view full gallery at Hypebeast

items.title: Marshall’s Bromley 150 Brings Concert Energy to a More Portable Form
items.text: Marshall’s Bromley 150 Brings Concert Energy to a More Portable Form Summary Marshall introduces the Bromley 150, its most portable party speaker yet.The Black and Brass design combines 360° sound with concert-inspired stage lighting.The IP55-rated unit delivers 40-plus hours of playtime and modular components. Marshall is expanding its Bromley party-speaker lineup with the Bromley 150, a more compact take on the format established by the larger Bromley 450 and 750. Designed to carry the same stage-inspired character in a more portable package, the speaker arrives in Marshall’s familiar Black and Brass finish, pairing a black grille and PU leather-wrapped cabinet with metallic accents and softened TPU corner caps. Its proportions have been tightened considerably, while a built-in retractable handle reinforces the grab-and-go concept. Compared with its larger siblings, the control panel has also been moved to the side, leaving the entire front face open for the grille and integrated lighting system.That lighting remains one of the Bromley family’s defining visual features. Positioned behind the grille, the built-in stage lights take cues from live concert rigs and move in response to the music, with three presets ranging from restrained ambience to a more pronounced light show. Marshall’s True Stereophonic 360° system is intended to distribute mids, highs and bass around the room rather than concentrating sound in one direction, while dedicated microphone and instrument inputs allow the speaker to shift from playback into karaoke or impromptu performance use. Portability is further supported by an IP55 rating, more than 40 hours of battery life and a replaceable battery, while components including the corner caps, handle, grille, knobs and battery lid can also be replaced to extend the product’s lifespan.The Bromley 150 carries much of the visual and functional identity of the Bromley 450 and 750, but scales it down for smaller spaces and easier transport rather than simply reducing the output. Its cabinet uses FSC 100%-certified wood and contains 19% recycled material by weight, while the combination of tactile physical controls, protective detailing and concert-inspired lighting keeps the model rooted in Marshall’s longstanding stage aesthetic. The Marshall Bromley 150 is available for pre-order from September 29 at Marshall’s website for just under $500 USD, with general availability beginning October 13, 2026, through Marshall and select retailers.
