items.title: doublet x POTR Flip Yoshida & Co.’s Standards Into a Bag With Two “A-Sides”
items.text: doublet x POTR Flip Yoshida & Co.’s Standards Into a Bag With Two “A-Sides” Summary POTR and doublet have built a bag with no designated back, inspired by the double A-side singles of the CD eraThe design fuses a mini backpack with a duffel bag, pairing POTR monogram jacquard with a turquoise liningInterchangeable shoulder and hand straps let it be worn crossbody or carried by hand whichever side faces out POTR has joined forces with doublet on a collaborative bag that merges a mini backpack and a duffel into a single, double-sided form. Rather than assigning a front and a back, the piece treats both faces as equals, giving wearers two distinct looks from one silhouette.The concept comes straight from doublet’s design playbook. Masayuki Ino’s Japanese label builds wearable, real-world clothing around humor and surprise, swapping out pieces of familiar staples for unexpected ideas until the result feels just slightly off from the everyday. Here, that thinking lands on the classic Yoshida & Co. bag, borrowing its logic from the double A-side CD single, a release where neither track was treated as the lesser cut.Ino frames the reversible format as a deliberate refusal to settle on one answer. “By not fixing the front and back and reversing the perspective, a new expression is born. The direction changes each time you carry it, and it resonates with your mood and outfit of the day,” he says in a translated statement.Each face gets its own construction. The backpack side is cut from an original jacquard woven with POTR’s monogram and carries a zippered front pocket sized for small essentials like wireless earbuds or lip balm. Flip it around and the duffel side offers a snap-button pocket that doubles as storage: when the backpack face is worn forward, the duffel handles tuck neatly inside it, keeping the profile clean.Color work ties the two halves together. On the pink and khaki versions, the zipper tape is dyed to match the body fabric, so neither side reads as secondary. Open the bag and a turquoise lining, a shade closely tied to POTR’s identity, runs through the interior.Versatility extends to the carry. Two straps come included, an adjustable, detachable shoulder strap and a hand strap, and they swap depending on which face is out front. Whether the backpack or duffel leads, the bag works both as a crossbody and as a handheld.The doublet x POTR bag drops on October 10 at the PORTER flagship store, PORTER Shinjuku and Kobe, POTR Ikebukuro, Nagoya, Namba an

items.title: Inside the World of Anyma: From ‘Genesys’ to ‘ÆDEN’ and His Singapore Debut
items.text: Inside the World of Anyma: From ‘Genesys’ to ‘ÆDEN’ and His Singapore Debut For Anyma, electronic music goes beyond sound. The DJ and producer has built an audiovisual world exploring technology, science fiction and humanity’s relationship with the digital age. With his Genesys trilogy behind him, he’s now expanding that vision through ÆDEN, a new chapter that continues to evolve with each performance.Having taken his productions to the Las Vegas Sphere, Coachella and the Pyramids of Giza, Anyma now makes his Singapore debut during Formula 1 race weekend. The performance marks a return to his club roots, bringing his latest audiovisual world into a different setting after a run of large-scale shows. He takes the stage at MARQUEE Singapore on October 10, 2026.You’re making your Singapore debut right in the middle of race weekend, one of the city’s biggest weekends. What are you looking forward to experiencing while you’re here?Experiencing Singapore and its people properly, as it’s such a beautiful country, as is all of Southeast Asia in general. This region in particular is one I’ve been deeply inspired by in its modern and ancient forms.“Each ÆDEN show is different, with the narrative constantly evolving through new songs and visuals.” Visuals have become a defining part of the Anyma experience. What do you want people to feel when they see them live? I want people to feel an emotion deeper than a party performance. I hope the takeaway feels valuable for the fans and that the thematic narratives of future, past, humanity, and technology ultimately resonate deeper. Of course these are primarily subjective and up to interpretation, but if people leave an ÆDEN show and feel moved in some way, then I’ve achieved my goal.Anyma has grown into an entire world beyond the music. At this point, where does Matteo end and Anyma begin?Creating the Anyma project was really just a combined reflection of who I am and what my passions have been throughout my life. Video games, anime, sci-fi, and fantasy worlds were huge influences on me outside of music, so Anyma came about as the best way I knew how to put all of my personal self into one persona.After spending years building Genesys, you’ve now entered a new chapter with ÆDEN. items.title: New Era Revisits Takehiko Inoue’s ‘Real’ With Three 9TWENTY Designs
items.text: New Era Revisits Takehiko Inoue’s ‘Real’ With Three 9TWENTY Designs Summary Takehiko Inoue and New Era collaborate to celebrate the 17th volume of Real .Features low-profile 9TWENTY caps, jersey number 99 embroidery, and interior comic panel prints.Includes adjustable headwear and heavyweight graphic tees showcasing iconic manga artwork. Renowned manga artist Takehiko Inoue - celebrated for defining works like Slam Dunk and Vagabond - has teamed up with New Era for a commemorative collaboration centered on his acclaimed wheelchair basketball series, Real.Created to celebrate the release of the manga's 17th volume, the joint collection brings the intense, human narrative of the series into lifestyle apparel and headwear. The core of the capsule highlights New Era's low-profile, unstructured 9TWENTY silhouettes, offering a relaxed fit and a casual, low-crown profile. Three variations spotlight Kiyoharu Togawa, Tomomi Nomiya and Hisanobu Takahashi, retaining the character-specific details established in the first release. Each cap also features an interior lining printed with memorable scenes selected from the manga’s latest collected volume, Volume 17, introducing a more understated reference to Inoue’s illustrations beneath the otherwise familiar baseball cap silhouette.The Real x New Era 9TWENTY collection is scheduled to launch in Japan on October 15, 2026, at 10 a.m. JST, with each cap priced at ¥6,600 JPY (approx. $44 USD). items.title: Sci-Fi Fantasy and Come Tees Team Up For a Hand-Painted Capsule Collection
items.text: Sci-Fi Fantasy and Come Tees Team Up For a Hand-Painted Capsule Collection Summary Sci-Fi Fantasy and Come Tees have teamed up on a capsule collection that blends Sonya Sombreuil’s hand-painted graphics with Sci-Fi Fantasy’s signature typography.Made in LA, the lineup includes a white Dragon Tee, a magenta Girl Tee, a baby blue Girl ringer tee, a embellished butterfly zip-up hoodie, and a studded “Fantasy” trucker hat.The Sci-Fi Fantasy and Come Tees capsule collection is available now at Sci-Fi Fantasy and Come Tees' official websites. Sci-Fi Fantasy and Come Tees join forces to merge Jerry Hsu’s graphic-heavy skate brand with Sonya Sombreuil’s Los Angeles-based DIY streetwear label. The collection combines Sombreuil’s hand-painted fine art graphics and recurring motifs, such as dragons and her self-described “Girl” imagery, with Sci-Fi Fantasy’s signature typography and bold, effortless visual style. The collection is made in LA on custom blanks, using garment-dyed cotton jersey that is screen-printed, then enzyme-washed for a soft, vintage feel. The collaboration lineup includes: a white, boxy Dragton Tee, a vivid magenta 90s-fit Girl Tee, a light blue Girl ringer Tee with a brown neckline, a teal, puff-logo embellished butterfly zip-up hoodie, and a dark blue studded "Fantasy" trucker hat. Pro skateboarder, photographer, and artist Jerry Hsu founded Sci-Fi Fantasy in 2017. The brand started as an experimental Instagram account filled with cryptic, lo-fi imagery before growing into an apparel and skateboarding line with a cult following. Painter Sonya Sombreuil launched Come Tees in 2009, and it operates as a small, DIY, studio-style operation where blanks become canvases for her hand-drawn graphics, jagged lines, and surreal imagery. The collaboration connects longtime friends and fans of each other, as both brands are small, artist-led, and built on limited runs and Los Angeles production. While describing the collection and working with Sombreuil, Hsu wrote on Sci-Fi Fantasy’s Instagram account, “She’s an incredible artist and makes some of the most interesting clothing I’ve come across. We’ve talked about doing something together for a long time, and it is so satisfying to finally make it happen." He added that the collection is “a little different from what we normally make, and we’re really happy with how everything turned out."The Sci-Fi Fantasy & Come Tees capsule collection is now available on scififantasy.co and shop-cometees.biz. items.title: Manual Photo Lab Is NYC Chinatown's New Kid on the Block
items.text: Manual Photo Lab Is NYC Chinatown's New Kid on the Block Summary Manual, the New York camera lifestyle label, just opened its first permanent store, Manual Photo Lab, in ChinatownAt 85A Allen Street, the space is designed as a hangout, film lab, equipment store, stocked with cameras, film, books, zines, and moreOpening doors with an exhibition by Leon Xu, founder Malcom Dia says more shows, zine launches, DJ sets, and workshops are in the works New York loves Manual, and Manual loves New York. Since its founding nearly a decade ago, the label has stayed true to its core creative community, ranging from photo buffs to photo-curious, with a steady flow of pop-ups, parties, and shows cropping up around the city. Now, with the opening of Manual Photo Lab, its first permanent foothold, day-ones and first-timers have a permanent hangout.The 400-square-foot setup in Chinatown was inspired by the mom-and-pop camera stores founder Malcolm Dia grew up around, places that not only specialized in equipment, but served as meeting spots for like-minded artists immersed in their craft. "They were where people met, traded tips, and got their film back. We think there's a real appetite for that kind of place, especially among younger people picking up cameras again," he said.On the shelves, alongside the brand's digital and disposable cameras — both arriving in a slew of colorways — are Kodak film stocks, books, zines, and merch from local and international publishers, like Loose Joints, Super Labo, Pomegranate Press, Monolith Editions, and Dobedo UK. It also offers film processing with 35mm color development starting at $15 and a two- to three-business-day turnaround.The space launched with an exhibition presented alongside Silvertooth Agency, featuring an original painting by Leon Xu and work by emerging artists. items.title: ‘Roy Lichtenstein: Like New’ Isn’t Your Parents’ Pop Art
items.text: ‘Roy Lichtenstein: Like New’ Isn’t Your Parents’ Pop Art We can’t help it: Roy Lichtenstein is everywhere. From the pixels that make up on-screen images and the thick, brazen linework of even today’s greatest makers to the split-second shot of a tear-stained heroine, his impact is nearly impossible to shake. It’s fast, it’s in your face. But how has his household comics-and-dots shorthand eclipsed a more complex story?“Just because we can recognize something doesn’t mean we fully understand what it is,” said Meg Onli, one of the curators of Roy Lichtenstein: Like New. Opening at the Whitney Museum in New York on October 11, the show brings together over 130 works by the Pop master, including paintings, drawings, collages, prints, and sculptures, created over Lichtenstein’s six-decade career. And while its comic-inspired canvases are plenty, it also unearths lesser-known threads that resemble the artist, both as he saw himself and how his then-radical love for high-low would presciently play to the screen-happy realities of today’s audiences.From the serious, and seriously strange, teachings of Hoyt Sherman at Ohio State University that would later prove formative to Lichtenstein’s outlook on the mark to works created in his last year of life, extending into the 1997 show just downstairs, Like New shines a light on the artist who understood the future of images and a deft appreciation for the eternal making and unmaking of meaning. The introductory, nearly 100-foot recreation of his “Greene Street Mural” (1983), one of four murals recreated by co-curator and artist Alex Da Corte’s studio, sets the tone right.A historic highlight is a literal trip back to Lichtenstein’s New York: a gallery-within-a-gallery reconstruction of the artist’s 1962 debut solo at Leo Castelli gallery. It’s the first reunion of all the works since, down to “Laughing Cat” (1961), originally owned by Andy Warhol. Then lie some of his best-known heroines — “Drowning Girl” (1963), “Crying Girl” (1963), and “Girl in Window (Study for World’s Fair Mural)” (1963), also blown up to larger-than-life on the balcony outside. Beside them are near-identical reproductions and sources, like Elaine Sturtevant’s duplicate, for which Lichtenstein supplied the stencils. He even signed a Richard Pettibone painting as if it were the real deal. items.title: Apple and The King’s Trust Launch New Mentoring Program
items.text: Apple and The King’s Trust Launch New Mentoring Program Apple and The King’s Trust are taking their partnership to the next level with the launch of their new educational program, Creative Labs.Recognizing the direct impact of systemic disadvantages and educational exclusions on young people in the UK, Creative Labs addresses the power of accessibility in carving out a successful career. Building upon both of their long-standing commitments to nurturing young talent, the collaborative initiative is set to teach invaluable skills by enlisted experts, expand opportunities, and break down barriers to entry to creative industries.As well as aligning their strengths to provide access to top industry connections through mentorship and training on the latest suite of Apple technology, the program will help members discover their passions, fuel creativity and transform ideas into practice.“Allowing me to tap into younger versions of myself and help give a small nudge in a direction where they might not see themselves. For me, it’s a special opportunity, being a creative myself and throwing rocks at Goliath when I was trying to figure out my path in the industry,” Prophet Guillory, Apple Music's head of Artist Services, Tools, and Community, tells Hypebeast. “Leaving the world a better place than when you found it is one of the first things somebody told me that you could do when you work at Apple. 11 years in the game, I’m here to tell you it’s true.”The program kicked off this week at the newly opened Apple Music Hall in Battersea Power Station, where 20 young people joined Guillory to experience immersive workshops centered around music. From Logic Pro tutorials using iPads to learning about the various avenues there are to take in the industry, attendees met with surprise special guests King Charles, Tim Cook and Sir Elton John, as well as got an exclusive behind-the-scenes look at Sky Newman’s sound check and were front-row for an intimate performance by Nectar Woode.Wanting to empower the next generation of creators to unlock their full potential, Creative Labs aims to be a growing hub for creativity and exploration. The inaugural program will be followed by more sessions that branch into other creative disciplines in the Apple ecosystem throughout the next year. View this post on InstagramA post shared by HYPEBEAST UK (@hypebeastuk)Watch Hypebeast get exclusive access to the first Creative Labs workshop in the video above. For more information on Apple Music

items.title: KidSuper Is Bringing DC's Most Notorious Villains Into Its Universe
items.text: KidSuper Is Bringing DC's Most Notorious Villains Into Its Universe Colm Dillane's world of KidSuper has never been about playing it safe. So, naturally, it makes sense that the Brooklyn-based designer would find some common ground with DC Comics' most notorious Super-Villains for his latest collaboration.Joining forces with DC and Warner Bros. Discovery Global Consumer Products, KidSuper is bringing eight of DC's most iconic Super-Villains into its colorful, hand-drawn universe for a new collection spanning apparel, home goods, and collectibles.The lineup includes The Joker, Catwoman, Poison Ivy, The Penguin, The Riddler, Mr. Freeze, Clayface, and Bane, each receiving their own take on KidSuper's signature Face Hoodie alongside collectibles inspired by their personalities. Included in the range is a Poison Ivy planter, Clayface bookends, a Riddler puzzle, and even a Penguin umbrella. The collection also features a heat-reactive Mr. Freeze puffer jacket and Catwoman trench coat."I always wanted KidSuper to become a real superhero character. And by working with DC and WBDGCP we are getting closer than ever," Dillane shares. "It was really special to go through the archives and see the early sketches of some of the most iconic IPs ever created and to think they started off as doodles."To celebrate the release, KidSuper is bringing the collection to life through a "Rogues Gallery" activation in Brooklyn, featuring original artwork, objects, and installations. Open to the public from October 20–23, the collection will be available exclusively on-site before dropping online at KidSuper.com on October 23 at 12 p.m. Prices range from $15 USD to $850 USD. items.title: CMF’s First Speakers Are Built Around Color, Modularity and Portability
items.text: CMF’s First Speakers Are Built Around Color, Modularity and Portability Summary CMF debuts its first portable speakers with the Speaker S and Speaker M.Both models feature modular designs, swappable panels, Stereo Mode and Auracast-powered Party Mode.Prices start at $59 USD, with sales beginning today. CMF by Nothing is expanding into portable audio for the first time with the Speaker S and Speaker M, a two-model lineup that carries the brand’s geometric, modular design language into a new category.The pair establishes the foundation of its audio range with two scales of the same visual idea: Speaker S is a compact, upright model designed to slip into a bag or clip onto a strap or carabiner, while Speaker M enlarges the format into a more substantial desktop or room speaker with an integrated handle. Both are offered in White, Dark Grey, Orange and Turquoise, with CMF’s characteristically playful use of color amplified by swappable front panels and control knobs. Standardized 3D-printable component designs also let users create their own replacements or visual variations, extending the customization approach seen across CMF’s broader product philosophy.The two speakers are differentiated less by styling than by scale and output. Speaker S uses a single 45 mm full-range driver with dual passive radiators for a lighter, more portable setup, while Speaker M steps up to a dual-driver architecture with a dedicated woofer and tweeter for greater separation, deeper bass and a fuller room-filling sound. Both incorporate Adaptive Tuning, which continuously adjusts playback and EQ at the hardware level, alongside Ultra Bass, Wide Soundstage and four selectable EQ presets through the Nothing X app. For multi-speaker setups, two matching units can be paired into true left-and-right Stereo Mode, while Auracast-powered Party Mode can synchronize playback across multiple compatible speakers, including supported models from other brands.Despite the more expressive styling, CMF has kept the interaction deliberately straightforward. A tactile knob handles playback, track navigation, volume and Ultra Bass, while dedicated controls cover power, Bluetooth pairing and Auracast. Connectivity includes Bluetooth 6.0, NFC tap-to-pair, Google Fast Pair, Microsoft Swift Pair and USB-C audio, while both models carry an IP68 rating and offer up to 18 hours of playback at 50% volume with Ultra Bass enabled. items.title: Everything Dropping at Palace This Week
items.text: Everything Dropping at Palace This Week Summary Palace Skateboards continues its Winter 2026 season with a drop led by a Caravaggio ShirtOuterwear and layering pieces include the Pertex Squared Jacket and the Thermal Bonded Hoodie across multiple colorwaysThe release rolls out on October 16 in the UK, Europe and the US before reaching Asia-Pacific the following day Palace Skateboards has unveiled the latest drop from its Winter 2026 collection, headlined by the Caravaggio Shirt and backed by a lineup of cold-weather layers. The release balances an art-referencing statement piece with practical outerwear, knitwear and denim built for the season.The Caravaggio Shirt that features "Saint Jerome Writing" leads the callouts, listed alongside the P90 Baggy Jean, a jacket and a plate. The name nods to the Italian Baroque painter known for his dramatic use of light and shadow, continuing Palace’s habit of pulling high-culture references into its streetwear offering.On the technical side, the Pertex Squared Jacket arrives in Army Green, Black and Navy. Pertex is a performance fabric brand recognized for lightweight, weather-resistant materials, positioning the jacket as one of the drop’s more function-focused pieces. The Thermal Bonded Hoodie offers the widest color range in the release, available in Black, Grey Marl, Racey Green and Woodprint. Knitwear comes via the Hairy Tiger Knit, offered in Blue, Grey and Orange.The Palace Skateboards Winter 2026 drop launches Friday, October 16, at 11:00 a.m. BST in the UK, Europe and the US, followed by Saturday, October 17, at 11:00 a.m. local time in Japan, China, Korea and Australia. items.title: Naruto TCG Sets June 2027 Worldwide Launch
items.text: Naruto TCG Sets June 2027 Worldwide Launch Summary The Naruto Card Game is set for a simultaneous worldwide launch in June 2027.Launch products include three pre-constructed Starter Decks and the first Booster Pack, Enter: Naruto Uzumaki!A global campaign in spring 2027 will distribute one million Demo Decks to introduce the game. Bandai Card Games has confirmed that the Naruto Card Game will launch simultaneously worldwide in June 2027, revealing the release window during New York Comic Con alongside a new teaser featuring original artwork by Studio Pierrot, the animation studio behind the Naruto anime.The teaser received its public premiere during the NYCC presentation, building on the trading card game’s initial world debut at Gen Con 2026 and placing the franchise’s familiar ninja imagery at the center of its latest promotional push. At launch, players will be able to choose between three pre-constructed Starter Decks led by Naruto Uzumaki, Sasuke Uchiha and Gaara, each built around its own Leader, lineup of ninjas and strategic play style. The first Booster Pack, titled Enter: Naruto Uzumaki!, will arrive alongside them with additional characters, techniques and cards drawn from both Naruto and Naruto Shippuden, with newly created card illustrations also unveiled during the presentation.Bandai is also planning an extensive lead-up to the global release, beginning with Premier Demo Events at participating TCG stores from February 2027, followed by a spring campaign distributing one million Demo Decks worldwide to introduce players to the game’s mechanics and “ninja-style mind games.” The events will additionally offer advance access to an Official Playmat featuring Naruto versus Sasuke and the Premium Card Collection Vol.00 – CHAKRA Set, with select products also appearing at Bandai Card Games Fest events in Orlando and London. Further details on the Naruto TCG are scheduled to be revealed at Jump Festa 2027 in December. Read more at Hypebeast

items.title: Supreme and Martine Rose Team up for Fall 2026 Collaborative Collection
items.text: Supreme and Martine Rose Team up for Fall 2026 Collaborative Collection Summary Supreme has collaborated with London-based designer Martine Rose on a comprehensive collection for Fall 2026The apparel and accessories range includes a Jeff Hamilton Shearling Coat, Patchwork Leather items, and a custom JBL speakerThe release features an exclusive Nike Dunk Low made specifically for Supreme and Martine Rose Supreme has officially unveiled its Fall 2026 collaborative collection with designer Martine Rose. The expansive apparel, footwear, and hardware capsule marks a major partnership between the New York streetwear staple and the London fashion label.The Fall 2026 range centers on heavy outerwear and statement tailoring, anchored by a Jeff Hamilton Shearling Coat alongside a Patchwork Labels Leather Jacket and matching 5-Pocket Leather Jean. Additional outerwear and track options include a Lined Cordura® Hooded Jacket, a Suede Zip Up Cardigan, a Metallic Stripe L/S Shirt, and co-branded Track Jackets with matching Track Pants.Rounding out the apparel selection are athletic tops and graphic layers, including a Hockey Jersey, a Rugby shirt, a Zip Up Hooded Sweatshirt, and two T-shirts titled the Now Tee and Champion Tee. Headwear and hardware showcase a Patchwork Labels Box Logo New Era®, Jacquard and Base Layer Beanies, a Shearling Mini Duffle Bag, and a custom Supreme/Martine Rose JBL Partybox Encore Essential 2 speaker. The collection is completed by a co-branded Nike Dunk Low silhouette engineered exclusively for the release.The Supreme x Nike Fall 2026 collection releases on October 15, via the official Supreme webstore and flagship locations, with an Asia release following shortly after on October 17. items.title: TAG Heuer Marks 10 Years of Oracle Red Bull Racing With a Team-Themed Solargraph
items.text: TAG Heuer Marks 10 Years of Oracle Red Bull Racing With a Team-Themed Solargraph Summary TAG Heuer marks 10 years with Oracle Red Bull Racing via a 38mm edition.The $2,250 USD steel watch features a blue, red, and yellow dial.A solar-powered TH50-00 movement runs 10 months per charge TAG Heuer is celebrating 10 years of partnership with Oracle Red Bull Racing with a new Formula 1 Solargraph special edition, translating the team’s familiar racing colors into the brand’s compact, motorsport-rooted sports watch. The relationship dates back to 2016 and has since produced a succession of collaborative timepieces tied to Red Bull Racing’s rise through the modern Formula 1 era.For the anniversary release, TAG Heuer turns to the 38mm Formula 1 Solargraph, itself rooted in the brightly colored Formula 1 watches that introduced a younger audience to Swiss watchmaking during the 1980s. The new edition combines that retro-informed silhouette with contemporary solar-powered technology, positioning the watch as both a celebration of the partnership’s first decade and a more youthful expression of TAG Heuer’s racing identity.Oracle Red Bull Racing’s palette dominates the design, led by a blue sunray-brushed dial surrounded by a vivid red minute track and matched with a blue TH-Polylight bidirectional bezel. A yellow lacquered central seconds hand and matching outline around the 3 o’clock date window introduce another flash of team color, while black lacquered hour and minute hands and applied indexes are filled with white Super-LumiNova that glows green in low light. The 38mm sandblasted stainless-steel case brings a matte, technical finish to the brighter dial treatment and is paired with a three-row steel bracelet fitted with a folding clasp and adjustment extension.On the other side, the solid steel caseback combines the Oracle Red Bull Racing logo with a checkered-flag motif, reinforcing the motorsport connection without adding further branding to the already vibrant dial. The watch is powered by the Caliber TH50-00 Solargraph movement, which uses natural and artificial light to recharge its battery. Exposing the dial to direct sunlight for one minute provides enough power for a full day of operation, and a full charge of 40 hours yields up to ten months of continuous running time in total darkness. items.title: Trettitre’s Retro Audio System Puts Three Generations of Music on One Wall
items.text: Trettitre’s Retro Audio System Puts Three Generations of Music on One Wall Summary Trettitre’s Retro system combines vinyl, CD and cassette players on a magnetic wall rack.Each player blends nostalgic physical controls with modern Bluetooth connectivity.The $529 USD system follows a Kickstarter campaign backed by over 5,300 supporters. Trettitre is bringing physical music formats back into view with its new Retro Wall-Mounted Ambient Audio System, a modular setup that turns vinyl, CDs and cassettes into part of the room rather than equipment to be hidden away.Built around the idea that each generation formed a different relationship with recorded music, the system brings together the TTT-LP3 vinyl player, TTT-DP3 CD player and TTT-CP3 cassette player alongside a dedicated smartphone slot for streaming. All three players attach magnetically to the TTT-W wall rack, creating a clean, gallery-like composition that spans several decades of listening culture.Each component interprets its respective format through a different retro-futurist lens while sharing a common mix of geometric forms, plastic and metal construction. The LP3 can be mounted vertically or horizontally, pairing an Audio-Technica cartridge with a self-balancing tonearm that automatically manages tracking pressure, while a diffused rear light panel allows the player to double as ambient illumination. Its wireless charging connection with the rack also keeps visible cabling to a minimum.The circular DP3, meanwhile, takes inspiration from the UFO imagery associated with 1990s and early-2000s pop culture, using a transparent magnetic cover to keep the spinning disc visible alongside raised tactile controls and a compact OLED screen. The CP3 takes a more utilitarian route, retaining the chunky mechanical buttons associated with traditional cassette players while adding Bluetooth connectivity. All three units are battery-powered and can be removed from the rack for use elsewhere in the room, extending the system beyond its wall-mounted presentation.The project also reflects a broader shift in Trettitre’s design language from simply referencing vintage audio equipment to rethinking how those formats can function within contemporary interiors. Wireless connectivity sits alongside deliberately analog interactions - lowering a stylus, inserting a disc or physically pressing a cassette key - allowing the system to retain the rituals associated with each medium without recreating vintage hardware wholesale

items.title: 'Blade Runner 2099' Trailer Returns to a Reborn Los Angeles With Michelle Yeoh and Hunter Schafer
items.text: 'Blade Runner 2099' Trailer Returns to a Reborn Los Angeles With Michelle Yeoh and Hunter Schafer Summary Prime Video has premiered the official trailer for its sci-fi sequel series 'Blade Runner 2099' at New York Comic ConMichelle Yeoh and Hunter Schafer star as an unlikely duo navigating a reborn Los Angeles 50 years after 'Blade Runner 2049'All eight episodes of the Ridley Scott-produced limited series land on the platform on November 25 Prime Video has officially unveiled the first trailer for Blade Runner 2099 at New York Comic Con. The eight-episode limited series acts as a direct continuation set 50 years after the events of Denis Villeneuve's 2017 feature Blade Runner 2049.Created and showrun by Silka Luisa, the narrative takes place in a reborn Los Angeles. The story centers on fugitive Cora, played by Hunter Schafer, who adopts a final identity as a Blade Runner and is forced into a partnership with Olwen, a near-death Replicant portrayed by Michelle Yeoh. Together, the duo must hunt down a runaway harboring a secret that threatens to collapse the entire city.Rooted in Philip K. Dick's 1968 novel Do Androids Dream of Electric Sheep?, the series is executive produced by original franchise director Ridley Scott alongside Alcon Entertainment. Jonathan van Tulleken serves as an executive producer and directed the first two episodes of the season.All eight episodes of Blade Runner 2099 premiere November 25, 2026, exclusively on Prime Video. Watch the trailer above. Read more at Hypebeast

items.title: Crocs Gives ‘Chainsaw Man’ Four Wildly Different Classic Clogs
items.text: Crocs Gives ‘Chainsaw Man’ Four Wildly Different Classic Clogs Name: ‘Chainsaw Man’ x Crocs Classic Clog CollectionMSRP: $70 - $80 USDRelease Date: October 27Where to Buy: CrocsCrocs is bringing the chaotic visual world of Chainsaw Man to the Classic Clog with a four-style collection centered on Denji/Chainsaw Man, Power, Pochita and the wider cast.The main Chainsaw Man pair takes the most aggressive approach, dressing the clog in vivid red with black and yellow graphic striping, jagged black blade-like elements running along the upper and tooth-like detailing around the forefoot. Black tooling and a dark heel strap ground the saturated finish, while Chainsaw Man and Pochita Jibbitz charms add another character-driven layer. Power’s edition shifts into a dusty blue upper contrasted by cream tooling splashed with blood-red graphics and a red outsole. Translucent red chain detailing crosses the vamp, while the fuzzy white heel strap is finished with Power’s signature horns, giving the design a deliberately theatrical mix of texture and color.The Pochita Classic Lined Clog is the most sculptural of the set, recreating the character through a bright orange body with graphic eyes, a chainsaw blade rising from the toe and a pull-cord-inspired tail wrapping around the sole. Orange fuzzy lining continues the character’s warm palette into the interior, while black and metallic-looking details sharpen the chainsaw motif.In contrast, the Characters Classic Clog uses a predominantly black foundation as a canvas for imagery of Denji, Pochita, Power, Makima and Aki, with scattered red splatter effects and darker graphic details wrapping around the sole. Five character-themed Jibbitz charms further layer the printed design, giving it more of an all-over manga/anime collage effect than the character-specific pairs. All four styles retain the familiar Crocs formula of lightweight construction, ventilation ports and pivoting heel straps, though the Pochita version swaps to the Classic Lined Clog for a softer, insulated build. items.title: JJJJound Reimagines the New Balance 990v3 With an All-Suede Construction
items.text: JJJJound Reimagines the New Balance 990v3 With an All-Suede Construction Summary JJJJound and New Balance have unveiled an all-suede iteration of the MADE in USA 990v3 silhouetteThe collaborative sneaker completely removes traditional mesh underlays for a full monochromatic suede upperThe pair features contrasting black outsoles trims and branding and is scheduled to release on October 22 JJJJound and New Balance have officially presented the collaborative New Balance MADE in USA 990v3 in suede, revealing the official release date. The upcoming collaboration reimagines the iconic running silhouette through a singular material expression, replacing its standard mesh construction with a premium, all-suede finish.Designed to explore how the heritage running silhouette feels when constructed entirely in suede, the project eliminates traditional mesh underlays to give the sneaker a more elevated character. By substituting the usual mesh base for a full monochromatic suede upper, the release introduces a new material language to the partnership's ongoing MADE in USA lineup.The monochromatic upper is offset by contrasting black outsoles, trims, and signature branding details, delivering a sharper, more understated profile. Operating at the intersection of luxury materials and athletic heritage, the shoe balances the familiar proportions of a Made in USA performance runner with an elevated design approach.The JJJJound x New Balance MADE in USA 990v3 in suede releases on October 22, 2026, via JJJJound. items.title: Sasuke Uchiha Inspires Absolutely Ridiculous' Latest ‘Naruto’ RARE Edition Baseball Glove
items.text: Sasuke Uchiha Inspires Absolutely Ridiculous' Latest ‘Naruto’ RARE Edition Baseball Glove Summary Naruto and Absolutely Ridiculous collaborate on a Sasuke Uchiha-inspired baseball glove.Limited to 125 examples, the RARE Edition glove retails for $499 USD.The collection also features a matching softball glove and Akatsuki-themed protective gear. The world of Naruto is stepping onto the baseball diamond as sports equipment label Absolutely Ridiculous (ARiA) introduces an officially licensed collaboration inspired by Sasuke Uchiha.Part of the brand's RARE Edition series, the collectible baseball glove transforms the iconic shinobi's identity into a piece of functional sporting equipment, bridging Japanese anime culture with the craftsmanship of professional-grade baseball gear. Rather than treating the glove as conventional merchandise, the release reflects ARiA's approach to wearable sports art, where distinctive designs are intended for both competitive play and display. The Sasuke-inspired glove is limited to just 125 examples, positioning it as an exclusive release for collectors and fans of Masashi Kishimoto's celebrated manga and anime franchise.Limited to 125 units, the Sasuke RARE Edition softball glove, priced at $499 USD, alongside a selection of Akatsuki Clouds protective equipment, is avaiable via Absolutely Ridiculous' website. items.title: Rudo Gloves Up for GEEKS RULE’s New 'Gachiakuta' Collaboration
items.text: Rudo Gloves Up for GEEKS RULE’s New 'Gachiakuta' Collaboration Summary GEEKS RULE has created two 'Gachiakuta' T-shirts, a Manga Version and an Anime Version, each tied to a different side of the seriesBoth are made with the Japanese label’s signature silkscreen process for a worn-in, vintage-style finishThe tees debut at KODANSHA HOUSE 2026 in New York ahead of a lottery release in Japan GEEKS RULE has teamed up with Gachiakuta on a pair of silkscreen-printed T-shirts celebrating the manga series and its TV anime adaptation. The collection splits into a Manga Version built around creator Kei Urana’s original artwork and an Anime Version featuring a fresh visual of protagonist Rudo, giving fans a choice between the page and the screen.The Manga Version centers on a dense, high-impact illustration by Urana showing the series’ bandaged hands. Within the Gachiakuta world, the wrapped hands carry real weight, standing for the connections, powers and bonds that drive the story, which makes them an apt single image for the graphic. The design is printed on both White and Black bodies.The Anime Version shifts focus to the adaptation. Its graphic is an official visual of Rudo, newly illustrated by the anime’s character designer Satoshi Ishino to mark the series’ jump to TV, showing the hero locked in mid-motion as he pulls his treasured gloves tight. Above him sits a street-art logo created by the manga’s own graffiti artist, a nod to the graffiti culture woven through the series. This version comes only in Black.Both shirts run through GEEKS RULE’s silkscreen printing process, which the label uses to give its graphic tees the texture and character of a well-worn vintage shirt rather than a flat, fresh-off-the-press print.The GEEKS RULE x Gachiakuta T-shirts pre-release worldwide on October 15 at KODANSHA HOUSE 2026 in New York, Kodansha’s brand-experience pop-up running October 9 through October 18 in Hudson Yards. Admission is free, though some areas require a reservation or lottery entry. A lottery release will follow in Japan via the GEEKS RULE online store at a later date.GEEKS RULE x Gachiakuta Pop-Up508 W 37th StreetNew York City Click here to view full gallery at Hypebeast

items.title: Nicolas Cage Refuses AI Waiver on 'Spider-Noir' and Vows to Cut Ties With Amazon
items.text: Nicolas Cage Refuses AI Waiver on 'Spider-Noir' and Vows to Cut Ties With Amazon Summary Nicolas Cage revealed at New York Comic-Con that he refused to sign an AI waiver for Prime Video's Spider-NoirThe actor criticized Amazon's investments in artificial intelligence and stated he will likely avoid working with the studio againCage championed handcrafted filmmaking with Gen Z directors while confirming plans for 'True Detective' Season 5 Nicolas Cage has taken a public stand against artificial intelligence, confirming he refused to sign an AI waiver for Prime Video's Spider-Noir. Speaking at a New York Comic-Con panel, the actor revealed that his refusal to grant digital likeness rights means he will likely not work with Amazon again due to the company being "very AI-friendly."Addressing the entertainment industry's growing reliance on generative technology, Cage directly cited Amazon's massive financial backing of artificial intelligence as the catalyst for his decision. “How do you survive AI?” Cage stated. “Amazon is a very AI-friendly company to the tune of 50 billion dollars invested in OpenAI. I am not an AI-friendly actor….I’m not a member of their club. I didn’t sign the waiver to let them use AI on Spider-Noir. I’m probably not going to be working with that studio again, but that’s okay.”Rather than embracing automated studio workflows, Cage emphasized his intention to collaborate with emerging Gen Z creators who produce films by hand. Between upcoming feature roles like Perish, the actor also confirmed plans to stay active in television, teasing that he is set to star in Season 5 of HBO's True Detective. items.title: Seiko’s Latest Marinemaster Draws From Okinawa’s Mangrove Forests
items.text: Seiko’s Latest Marinemaster Draws From Okinawa’s Mangrove Forests Seiko is revisiting one of the most important chapters in its dive-watch history with the new Prospex Marinemaster 1968 Heritage Save the Ocean Limited Edition, a 900-piece release inspired by Okinawa’s mangrove forests. The model draws directly from Seiko’s landmark 1968 Diver’s watch - the world’s first hi-beat diver - preserving the broad case silhouette and professional-tool character while introducing a more expressive color palette. Its deep green dial is paired with rose gold-colored accents, creating a warmer, more refined contrast that references the dense coastal ecosystems where land and sea meet.Functionally, the watch remains firmly rooted in Seiko’s professional diving lineage. The case retains the original model’s streamlined profile and signature 4 o’clock crown, alongside a unidirectional rotating bezel, LumiBrite detailing and 300 meters of water resistance in accordance with ISO diving standards. Inside sits Seiko’s Calibre 8L45, delivering accuracy of +10/-5 seconds per day and a 72-hour power reserve, while the bracelet is fitted with a three-fold clasp, push-button release and slide adjuster for practical use over a wetsuit or on the wrist.The Prospex Marinemaster 1968 Heritage Save the Ocean Limited Edition is restricted to 900 pieces worldwide, positioning it as one of the more exclusive contemporary Marinemaster releases. Official pricing is set at £3,300 GBP (approx. $4,370 USD), it's currently available to order through the Seiko Boutique website, with deliveries scheduled to begin in November 2026. items.title: Michelin-Starred Andō and Wana Yook Unite for a Two-City “Fire & Water” Collaboration
items.text: Michelin-Starred Andō and Wana Yook Unite for a Two-City “Fire & Water” Collaboration Summary Michelin-starred Andō and Bangkok’s Wana Yook partnered for a "Fire & Water" collaboration.Following a sold-out Hong Kong leg, the exchange moves to Bangkok on October 15, 2026.The menu pairs Thai heat with Andō’s signature ocean-inspired seafood dishes. Following its two-night Hong Kong run last week, Andō x Wana Yook is preparing to take the second chapter of its two-city collaboration to Bangkok on October 15, 2026. The exchange brings together Andō founder and Executive Chef Agustin Ferrando Balbi and Wana Yook’s Thai-Indian chef and co-owner Chalee Kader, pairing two Michelin-starred restaurants whose cooking is closely tied to personal history and place.Framed around “Fire & Water,” the concept assigns fire to Kader’s bold use of heat, spice and aromatics in Thai cooking, while Balbi responds through water — seafood, citrus, chilled preparations and oceanic flavors informed by Andō’s Japanese-leaning precision. Rather than forcing the two approaches into a single style, the collaboration is conceived as a dialogue between them. After debuting at Andō in Hong Kong, the exchange concludes at Wana Yook in Bangkok on October 15, with prices starting at ฿5,900 THB (approx. $176 USD) per guest.The Hong Kong event offered a preview of that conversation, opening with Wana Yook’s Kao Soi, layering herbs and crisp textures around a beef curry, before Andō answered with a tart of kinmedai, lemon gel, uni and baby basil. Kader’s Kung Chae Naam Pla paired amaebi with turmeric, lime, chilli, pomelo and bitter gourd, while Balbi countered its heat with cured buri, citric panna cotta and ginger-lime granita.Later courses moved between Wana Yook’s warming Tom Jiw of Scallops and Andō’s crisp-scaled Coral Grouper with Seaweed, Crêpe and Maitake, before the two approaches converged around rice: coconut rice accompanied Wana Yook’s Melayu-influenced Curry Tumis and Hormok Morel, the latter stuffing morels with fish mousse and red curry paste. Desserts continued the exchange with Andō’s Air Chocolate, Coconut and Dulce de Leche, followed by Wana Yook’s taro-filled Bua Loy and Andō’s fig and ricotta tart.The collaboration also reflects the distinct identities the two restaurants have developed independently. items.title: Kim Jones Announces Eponymous Label With FW27 Debut Collection
items.text: Kim Jones Announces Eponymous Label With FW27 Debut Collection Summary Kim Jones OBE has officially announced his self-titled label KIM JONES debuting with a Fall/Winter 2027 collectionThe apparel lineup will be predominantly manufactured in Japan alongside Italian-made leather goods at a considered price pointRetail distribution begins online in mid-2027 followed by the brand's first flagship store opening at Central Yards in Hong Kong in October 2027 Kim Jones has officially announced the launch of his brand KIM JONES, marking the return to his own eponymous label with a debut Fall/Winter 2027 Collection. Building on over two decades leading global luxury fashion houses—including artistic director tenures at Louis Vuitton, Dior Men, and Fendi—the standalone label introduces a new independent chapter for the British designer.Designed with versatility at its core, the collection offers a broad wardrobe unrestricted by traditional menswear or womenswear categories. The apparel range is predominantly manufactured in Japan to uphold precision craftsmanship, while the leather goods line is produced in Italy. Positioned at a considered price point, the label combines street culture fluency, heritage utility, and high-fashion tailoring.“After many years working with incredible houses and collaborators, it feels like the right moment to do something under my own name again,” stated Kim Jones OBE. “This brings together the things I’ve always been interested in — fashion, art and design — and gives me the space to work with people I admire and explore new ideas.”The physical launch strategy centers heavily on the Asian market following its global digital debut. The brand's physical retail rollout will be anchored by its first brick-and-mortar storefront at Central Yards in Hong Kong, followed by additional store openings across Asia and partnerships with selected global stockists.The KIM JONES Fall/Winter 2027 collection launches mid-2027 exclusively via kimjones.com, followed by the flagship store opening at Central Yards in Hong Kong in October 2027. items.title: 'The Social Reckoning' Flops With Dismal $5.5 Million Box Office Debut
items.text: 'The Social Reckoning' Flops With Dismal $5.5 Million Box Office Debut Summary Aaron Sorkin’s Facebook drama 'The Social Reckoning' opened in fifth place with a disappointing $5.5 million USD debutBlumhouse horror feature 'Other Mommy' led the North American box office with a $27.5 million USD premiere'The Social Reckoning' fell short of projections and the box office legacy of 2010’s The Social Network Sony Pictures and director Aaron Sorkin’s The Social Reckoning opened to a disappointing $5.5 million USD at the North American box office, crumbling into fifth place during its opening weekend. The R-rated Facebook drama fell short of its $7 million to $8 million USD projections.Written and directed by Sorkin, The Social Reckoning serves as a companion piece to 2010’s The Social Network. Starring Mikey Madison as a Facebook engineer leaking internal documents to a reporter played by Jeremy Allen White, the $30 million USD production struggled to incentivize theatergoers, earning a mixed 54% Rotten Tomatoes score and a "B-" CinemaScore. In comparison, the original 2010 David Fincher film opened to $22 million USD before grossing $224 million USD globally.Meanwhile, Universal and Blumhouse’s horror feature Other Mommy, starring Jessica Chastain, claimed the weekend's top spot with a $27.5 million USD domestic debut and $45.19 million USD worldwide total against an $18 million USD budget. Other box office holdovers included Tom Cruise’s $160 million USD satire Digger, which plummeted 60% in its second weekend to $3.2 million USD, alongside Amazon MGM’s Verity and Sony’s Resident Evil reboot.The Social Reckoning and Other Mommy are currently playing in theaters nationwide. items.title: Arkadia-Life’s $30,000 USD Porsche 911-Inspired Sofa Is Basically a Sports Car With a Fridge
items.text: Arkadia-Life’s $30,000 USD Porsche 911-Inspired Sofa Is Basically a Sports Car With a Fridge Summary Arkadia-Life’s P01 Classic Sofa takes its design cues from 1960s GT sports cars, right down to bug-eye headlights and chrome bumpersA lift-up rear lid and opening fenders reveal seven storage compartments, including a refrigerator and wine storageA UK-made SENSONUM audio system, ambient lighting and knock-sensing controls are built into the bodywork Arkadia-Life’s P01 Classic Sofa is a single-seat lounger built to look like a vintage sports car, and it’s packed with more hidden features than most living rooms. The design brand, which keeps a showroom in Shanghai and credits Italian master artisans for its work, draws on what it calls “legendary iconic automobiles” under its “The One and Always” philosophy, turning a classic coupe silhouette into a collectible piece of furniture.The car references run deep. Round bug-eye headlights and amber indicators sit up front, slim chrome bumpers wrap the body, and twin exhaust tips peek out beneath an engraved rear plaque. Arkadia-Life only ever cites 1960s GT sports cars as its inspiration, but the long-hood proportions read unmistakably like an early Porsche 911. The paint list adds to the case: GT Silver and Jet Green come standard, while Miami Blue, Crayon and Speed Yellow cost extra.The seat itself is upholstered in channel-quilted cowhide, pleated like a vintage bucket seat and offered in eight leather colors. Despite the “sofa” name, it holds just one person.Storage is where the P01 earns its keep. The rear lid lifts on small prop rods, much like an old engine cover, to reveal seven compartments. Inside are a refrigerator measuring 8.7 x 13.4 x 5.5 inches, wine storage, adjustable cup holders and a wireless charging pad. Both rear fenders also swing open into drawers sized for watches and model cars, a detail that makes the target buyer pretty clear.Sound runs through a UK-made SENSONUM system that pairs a professional amplifier and subwoofer with 13 speakers for surround-style playback. It streams over Bluetooth, and a dedicated app lets owners tune the sound to taste. Rather than buttons, the P01 is controlled through five knock-sensing panels built into the bodywork, a setup Arkadia-Life bills as an industry first. Multicolor ambient lighting glows from beneath the side sills and can shift to suit the room’s mood, and the system is rated at 500W.Arkadia-Life says the chair brings together hundreds of precisi

items.text: Pokémon and Santa Cruz Announce 30th Anniversary Blind-Bag Skateboard Collection Summary Pokémon and Santa Cruz have unveiled a blind-bag skateboard deck collection to celebrate Pokémon's 30th anniversaryThe release features 30 distinct deck designs inspired by iconic Pokémon Trading Card Game art and energy typesEach blind bag includes a limited-edition Player's Guide booklet showcasing 30 deck designs and 3 rare variations Pokémon and Santa Cruz have officially announced a 30th Anniversary Blind-Bag Skateboard Collection. Arriving in celebration of three decades of the iconic franchise, the collaboration introduces a series of random mystery decks inspired by classic Pokémon Trading Card Game (TCG) history.The blind-bag collection centers on 30 distinct skateboard deck designs, each incorporating original artwork from memorable Pokémon TCG cards spanning the past 30 years. Reimagined through Santa Cruz's skate heritage, the custom deck graphics emphasize core gameplay elements such as elemental energy types and character themes. Beyond the main deck lineup, the capsule also includes accompanying apparel and custom grip tape.Each randomly packaged skateboard deck arrives sealed alongside a limited-edition Pokémon Player's Guide booklet. items.title: Google Japan’s New Gboard Conveyor Belt Keyboard Is a Wild One-Handed Typing Concept
items.text: Google Japan’s New Gboard Conveyor Belt Keyboard Is a Wild One-Handed Typing Concept Summary Google Japan unveiled a conceptual conveyor belt keyboard mimicking a factory production lineThe joke prototype promotes the Gboard Android app and claims to reduce typing fatigueBlueprints, firmware and circuit diagrams are available as an open-source GitHub project Google Japan unveiled an unorthodox hardware concept, introducing the Gboard conveyor belt keyboard. Designed to operate like a localized factory production line right on a desk, the device reimagines traditional typing mechanics. Aesthetically, the sprawling peripheral resembles a hybrid between a standard office keyboard and a miniature fitness treadmill. According to an automated translation of the official Japanese press release, the rotating mechanism of the conveyor belt continuously loops so that the physical keys flow directly into the user's resting hand.A project blog post detailing the launch claims that this conveyor belt keyboard is designed for one-handed use. Rather than forcing the typist to stretch across a static board, Google claims that the design cuts down on typing fatigue. By relying on the motorized belt, the hardware allows users to wait for the correct keys to arrive directly under their fingertips rather than manually moving their hands to hunt them down.The stunt operates as an elaborate promotional joke intended to draw viral attention to Google's Gboard keyboard app for Android. Its release continues an annual Google Japan tradition of creating highly unusual, heavily engineered keyboard prototypes to hype the software.Unsurprisingly, the conveyor belt keyboard is not available for purchase as a mass-market commercial product. However, for those looking to manifest the joke in the physical world, Google made the blueprints for the keyboard available as a DIY project hosted on GitHub. The open-source GitHub repository containing all project files is named mozc-devices. To ensure that anyone can construct the peripheral, the GitHub release includes all circuit diagrams required to build the DIY keyboard from scratch. Furthermore, the repository provides the proprietary firmware source code required to run and operate the device. To keep everything accessible to the public, all DIY keyboard files and software are distributed on GitHub under an Apache-2.0 license. Click here to view full gallery at Hypebeast

items.title: Even Realities’ Dystopian Sculptures Are Keeping a Watchful Eye on You
items.text: Even Realities’ Dystopian Sculptures Are Keeping a Watchful Eye on You Technology company Even Realities has launched new sculptures around central London as part of its latest installation, “The Watchers.” Revealing the chilling reality of camera glasses, the installation takes shape with CCTV-mounted heads featuring camera lenses. Despite being in the tech space, Even Realities has crafted digital glasses without cameras to fit naturally into human life without interfering with others in public. Its work has long been supported by ongoing data and medical professionals, so when new research from Focaldata came to light, stating that 81% of British people would support a ban on camera glasses, it delved deeper into the rising threats of the popular product.In an open letter calling for tighter control of smart glasses, Founder and CEO Will Wang shared, “Smart glasses don’t need cameras now. While there are benefits in how they enable devices to collate visual context, the privacy trade-offs, for both the user and those around them, mean cameras should never have progressed past the blueprint without proper guardrails.”Enhancing public awareness of camera glasses, "The Watchers" installation has been fitted on Berwick Street in London’s busy Soho area. Designed in collaboration with creative production studio The Robin Collective and special effects artist Will Harvey, each sculpture is made with 3D scanning, printing and live silicone castings for a hyper-realistic yet noticeably shocking appearance.To continue highlighting the dangers of intrusive filming, the company releases a short film showcasing the sculptures in everyday locations like pubs and gyms. The video illustrates how camera glasses leave no public space untouched, advocating for long-term regulatory measures.You can now watch the film in the gallery above. To find out more about the project, read the open letter online now. Click here to view full gallery at Hypebeast

items.title: JW Anderson Brings Loafer Details to Classic UGG Silhouettes
items.text: JW Anderson Brings Loafer Details to Classic UGG Silhouettes SummaryJW Anderson and UGG’s first collaboration updates the Classic Boot and Tasman with sophisticated penny loafer details.Launching October 15, the suede and fur-lined footwear features an autumnal color palette of Chestnut, Khaki, and Orange.In a first-time collaboration, JW Anderson and UGG have partnered for a collection that reimagines classic UGG silhouettes with sophisticated updates from designer Jonathan Anderson. Continuing Anderson’s tradition of bringing loafer-inspired details to different products, UGG’s Classic Boot and Tasman have been reimagined with distinct characteristics inspired by penny loafers.In a statement, Jonathan Anderson shared more insights on his approach: “UGGs are instantly recognisable, and I was interested in seeing something so familiar through the lens of JW Anderson.” “We’ve explored the loafer extensively at JW ANDERSON, not only as footwear but also through its details applied to bags and ready-to-wear. I wanted to see how that language could translate into UGG,” he added.While maintaining their iconic shape and comfy feel, the casual models are imbued with renewed elegance through penny keepers placed over the toe box and visible box stitching. Boasting full suede uppers and a furry white lining, the Classic Boot features a JW Anderson tag on the back heel, while the Tasman slides showcase the logo on the lateral collar. The release comes in an Autumnal palette of Chestnut, Khaki and Orange, hand selected by Anderson.While sneaker loafers have been in the menswear zeitgeist for the last couple of years, bringing sports-inspired performance details to the dress shoe style, JW Anderson takes the trend in a different direction. After bringing penny keeper details to his Loafer handbags, Anderson extends the concept to a collaboration that cleverly softens its loafer-inspiration rather than upping its technical appeal.The JW Anderson x UGG Classic Boots and Tasmans are set to drop on October 15 in stores and at JWANDERSON.COM.
