items.title: Rest in Crisps: Pringles Offers 200 Years of Free Snacks if You Agree to Be Buried in a Can
items.text: Rest in Crisps: Pringles Offers 200 Years of Free Snacks if You Agree to Be Buried in a Can Summary ringles has introduced its Once You Drop Halloween sweepstakes offering a custom precious metal urn and 200 years of free chipsThe activation draws inspiration from can inventor Fredric Baur whose ashes were buried inside one of his packaging designs in 2008Participants can enter by signing a digital will and taste-ament through October 22 with one winner chosen around October 31 Pringles has officially launched the Pringles "Once You Drop" Campaign, challenging die-hard snackers to trade their final resting place for a 200-year supply of chips. The tongue-in-cheek Halloween activation promises one winner a custom burial urn modeled directly after the brand's iconic cylindrical container.The campaign leans into eccentric snack lore, drawing direct inspiration from Fredric Baur, the chemist and packaging pioneer who invented the tubular Pringles can. Following his passing in 2008, Baur’s family honored his final wish by placing a portion of his cremated remains inside a Pringles container before burial. Reviving that macabre legacy, the sweepstakes features a one-of-a-kind urn forged from precious metal, complete with a removable lid, personalized engraving, and the signature dimensions of the original canister.Alongside the bespoke container, the winner receives what the brand terms an “afterlifetime” supply of chips spanning two centuries, which can be legally bequeathed to future heirs. “Pringles has always been about the joy of the unexpected and this campaign takes our ‘Once You Drop’ campaign tagline literally: the pop don’t stop, not even once fans ‘drop,’” said Mauricio Jenkins, Salty Snacks Brand & Content Lead at Mars Snacking North America. The rollout is further amplified by licensed funeral director Dan McDonald, known across social media as @DanTheFuneralMan, who headlines the promotional video.The Pringles "Once You Drop" sweepstakes is open to legal US and Washington, DC residents aged 18 and older on Pringles.com through October 22 at 11:59 PM ET, with the winner notified around October 31. Click here to view full gallery at Hypebeast

items.text: BABY MILO® Debuts "12 Zodiac Blind Box Series" for FW26 A BATHING APE®’s lifestyle brand BABY MILO® has unveiled its first-ever “12 Zodiac Blind Box Series,” arriving as one of the key releases from its Fall/Winter 2026 collection. Accessories expand the astrological narrative into everyday wear, ranging from the character-shaped BABY MILO® Mobile Bag to medium and large backpacks covered in colorful zodiac-themed graphics.The BABY MILO® FW26 Zodiac Blind Box Series and Collection will officially launch on October 22, 2026. items.title: Nico Hulkenberg and Gabriel Bortoleto Star in ic! berlin’s Inaugural Motorsport Campaign
items.text: Nico Hulkenberg and Gabriel Bortoleto Star in ic! berlin’s Inaugural Motorsport Campaign German eyewear label ic! berlin has officially launched its first campaign as the Official Partner of Audi Revolut F1® Team, starring drivers Nico Hulkenberg and Gabriel Bortoleto.Shot by photographer Rupert Tapper under the creative direction of Leif Podhajsky and Sophie Holm-Nielsen, the campaign incorporates artistic motion blur to evoke the physical acceleration and precision of high-speed racing. Establishing a narrative that fuses cutting-edge optical craftsmanship with peak motorsport performance, the partnership debuts trackside across key global racing destinations, including Monza, Singapore’s Marina Bay and Austin.Central to the release is the special eyewear collection featuring two ic! berlin signature frames: the IC0067_20C_GABRIEL and the IC0065_15D_RYAN. Worn in the campaign by Hulkenberg and Bortoleto respectively, these iconic models combine a sleek, contemporary aesthetic with functional sport-inspired ergonomics. Built for clarity and stability under demanding conditions, the frames reflect a joint commitment between ic! berlin and Audi Revolut F1® Team to deliver technical excellence both on and off the circuit.Anchored by the tagline "From 0.5 mm to 300 km/h: engineering performance and precision at speed," the campaign draws direct design parallels between elite race car development and high-end eyewear. Just as the Audi R26 relies on lightweight dimensions and active aerodynamics for agility at high speeds, ic! berlin frames are handcrafted in Berlin from 0.5 mm cold-rolled stainless steel.The newly introduced ic! berlin eyewear capsule will launch globally this October in addition to designated authorized eyewear retailers worldwide; readers in Hong Kong can purchase the collection directly online at HBX. items.title: Why Denis Villeneuve Needed James Bond to Finally Leave 'Dune' Behind
items.text: Why Denis Villeneuve Needed James Bond to Finally Leave 'Dune' Behind Summary Denis Villeneuve revealed that signing on to direct the next James Bond film gave him the momentum needed to conclude his 'Dune' trilogyAdapting Frank Herbert’s Dune Messiah the third chapter picks up 17 years later as Paul Atreides succumbs to tyrannical powerWarner Bros will release Dune Part Three in theaters on December 18 2026 Warner Bros. and director Denis Villeneuve have shared fresh insight into Dune: Part Three, with the filmmaker revealing how the upcoming James Bond installment serves as his creative escape from the sci-fi franchise. In an interview with Empire, the director reflected candidly on avoiding complacency for the final chapter.Explaining his decision to return to Arrakis, Villeneuve noted that his motivation stemmed from fatigue rather than fond memories. "Maybe it's a good idea to go back to this project, not out of nostalgia, not because I miss it, but the opposite — I'm tired of it," Villeneuve explained. "I want to make sure that I will be severe with the material. That I will not be complacent. I thought, 'When it's done, I need a very powerful rocket to pull me away from Arrakis.' When I was asked to do the next Bond, I said: 'OK, this is what I need.'"Adapting Frank Herbert’s Dune Messiah, the concluding installment jumps 17 years into the future to chronicle Paul Atreides’ (Timothée Chalamet) descent into tyrannical rule. "The idea was to try to make a movie that will have the same DNA — it’s a Dune movie — but it's a very different movie," Villeneuve said. "It has a different pacing. We are back with the same characters, but this time the world has totally changed. Their psyches, their perspective on reality has totally changed, and Paul is living with the burden of what he created, trying to find a way out of this spiral of violence."Dune: Part Three hits theaters on December 18, 2026. items.title: Craig McDean Celebrates ‘Ducati's 750 Supersport’ in New Tokyo Photography Exhibition
items.text: Craig McDean Celebrates ‘Ducati's 750 Supersport’ in New Tokyo Photography Exhibition Summary Craig McDean presents 750 Super Sport , a Ducati-inspired photography exhibition at UNDER R TOKYO.Exclusive merchandise includes graphic T-shirts and long-sleeved tops featuring McDean's motorcycle photography.Running October 23 - November 6, the exhibition also features a photography book. UNDER R, in partnership with Ron Herman, is set to host a photographic exhibition by British fashion photographer Craig McDean this month.Based in New York, McDean first gained recognition through influential publications such as i-D and The Face in the early 1990s before establishing himself as one of fashion photography's leading figures, shooting campaigns and editorials for brands including CHANEL, Jil Sander and Calvin Klein. Titled 750 Super Sport, the exhibition shifts his focus from fashion to the mechanical artistry of Ducati, presenting a series of photographs dedicated to the Italian motorcycle manufacturer's legendary 750 Supersport Green Frame. Accompanied by a photography book of the same name, the project captures the motorcycle's sculptural forms, engineering details and enduring cultural significance, translating its industrial design into a photographic study of craftsmanship and beauty.At the heart of the exhibition is the Ducati 750 Supersport Green Frame, a motorcycle whose origins trace back to the early 1970s. Developed under Ducati chief designer Fabio Taglioni, the 750cc L-twin racing machine made an immediate impact at the 1972 Imola 200, securing first and second place on its debut. Its subsequent road-going iteration became one of the marque's most coveted collector's models, with just 401 examples of the Green Frame produced. Distinguished by its single-seat configuration, open exhaust system, triple disc brakes and desmodromic valve technology, the 1974 model embodied an uncompromising approach to performance and hand-built engineering.Extending the project beyond the gallery, UNDER R has also developed a collaborative apparel capsule featuring short-sleeved and long-sleeved T-shirts in black and white. The short-sleeved designs feature McDean's motorcycle imagery on the front with “750 Super Sport” typography on the reverse, while the long-sleeved versions incorporate a top-down motorcycle photograph alongside printed text and sleeve graphics. items.title: Baracuta x WILD THINGS x WACKO MARIA Go Reversible and Furry
items.text: Baracuta x WILD THINGS x WACKO MARIA Go Reversible and Furry Summary WACKO MARIA reconnects with Baracuta and Wild Things for a three-style Fall/Winter 2026 outerwear capsuleBaracuta’s G9 Harrington Jacket goes fully reversible, pairing a cotton-polyester face with an all-polyester side in blackWild Things delivers the PrimaLoft-insulated Happy Vest in nylon and a leopard faux fur version in beige and pink Baracuta and WILD THINGS x WACKO MARIA have unveiled a Fall/Winter 2026 outerwear lineup made up of the Reversible G9 Harrington Jacket, the Happy Vest and the Leopard Faux Fur Happy Vest. The Tokyo label pulls a signature piece from each partner, then reworks it through fabric choices and insulation tuned for the colder months.The Reversible G9 Harrington Jacket gives Baracuta’s classic two distinct personalities in a single garment. One side is cut from a 58% cotton and 42% polyester blend, while the reverse switches to 100% polyester, so the wearer can trade a softer, more traditional hand for a slicker synthetic face simply by turning the jacket inside out. Both offerings arrive in black, keeping the focus on texture and material contrast rather than color, and the jacket is listed at two separate price tiers without further detail on what separates them.WILD THINGS handles the insulation side of the capsule with the Happy Vest, built from a 100% nylon shell packed with PrimaLoft insulation. The sleeveless format keeps the core warm while leaving the arms free, making it a natural layering piece over hoodies or under heavier coats, and it comes in black or gray for a utilitarian finish.For a louder alternative, the Leopard Faux Fur Happy Vest keeps the same PrimaLoft fill but swaps the nylon for a 100% polyester faux fur exterior. The leopard pattern, a recurring WACKO MARIA motif, sits directly on the plush surface, and the vest comes in beige or pink, pushing the outdoor staple firmly into statement territory.The Baracuta and Wild Things x WACKO MARIA FW26 collection is available now via WACKO MARIA stores and authorized stockists, and the WACKO MARIA online store. items.title: The Nike Air Force 1 Low “Lace Metallic Gold” Swaps Leather for Woven Texture and Floral Trim
items.text: The Nike Air Force 1 Low “Lace Metallic Gold” Swaps Leather for Woven Texture and Floral Trim Name: Nike Air Force 1 Low “Lace Metallic Gold”Colorway: Sail/Gum Light Brown-Metallic GoldSKU: IX7038-121MSRP: $120 USDRelease Date: Fall 2026Nike is set to deliver the Air Force 1 Low “Lace Metallic Gold,” a women’s take on the silhouette dressed in a Sail, Gum Light Brown and Metallic Gold palette. The pair departs from the shoe’s typical all-leather build, pairing a woven, textured upper with gold leather accents and floral lace details for a softer, more ornamental finish.The base layer is where the biggest change happens, as a textured Sail fabric replaces leather across the toe box and side panels. Metallic Gold leather then frames the shoe at the mudguard, eyestays and heel, with the side Swooshes finished in the same gold to tie the overlays together.Closer inspection reveals a handful of subtler touches, starting with eyestays cut with a scalloped edge for a decorative silhouette along the lacing area. Miniature Swooshes are stitched near the toe, while the tongue and heel tab are rendered in gold fabric and topped with a layer of floral lace, each carrying embroidered Nike branding beneath the pattern.The finishing details keep the palette clean, with white laces and a white collar contrasting the gold, plus Nike Air branding printed in gold on the insole. Underfoot, a Sail midsole sits atop a Gum Light Brown outsole, giving the familiar Air Force 1 sole unit a warm, vintage-leaning base. Click here to view full gallery at Hypebeast

items.title: NSQK on 'MOSCA', Kafka, and the Dark Side of Chasing Greatness
items.text: NSQK on 'MOSCA', Kafka, and the Dark Side of Chasing Greatness NSQK was watching his career reach new heights when a mysterious fly infestation turned his apartment into something straight out of a horror movie. As his album ATP gained momentum and bigger stages came into view, the Mexican artist found himself killing up to 20 flies a day in his Monterrey home. What started as a bizarre inconvenience soon became the unlikely foundation for his third studio album, MOSCA.At the time, NSQK was reading Franz Kafka’s The Metamorphosis, a story that began to feel strangely connected to his own life. Between the unexplained infestation, a spiritual cleansing, and the growing pressures of the Latin music industry, he questioned how success seemed to transform him. The flies became a symbol of everything that comes with chasing greatness: envy, ego, criticism, competition, and the constant hunger for more.That tension runs throughout MOSCA. Bringing rock influences into his signature blend of electronic music, pop, and hip-hop, NSQK pushes his sound into new territory across 17 heavy-hitting tracks. Collaborations with Julieta Venegas, Jean Dawson, Eslabón Armado, Kevin Kaarl, and Riosse also mark a shift in his creative process, as he opens the door to more voices and perspectives.We caught up with NSQK to discuss the strange events that inspired MOSCA, the artistic evolution behind his most ambitious record yet, and his plans to bring an entirely new live experience to Mexico City's Estadio GNP Seguros in January 2027.What inspired the title of your new album, MOSCA?“In 2024, I moved into a small apartment in Monterrey with my girlfriend, who is now my wife. We were in the middle of rolling out ATP, we had announced my show at the WTC Pepsi Center in Mexico City, and a lot of exciting things were happening with the project. Everything was really taking off, and suddenly these big, ugly, aggressive green flies started appearing in my apartment.”How did Franz Kafka’s The Metamorphosis influence the concept behind the album?“Around that time, I happened to be reading Kafka’s The Metamorphosis, about a man who wakes up transformed into a giant beetle. I started drawing parallels between that story and what was happening in my career. The project was growing so much, but we were also facing new feelings and experiences within the music industry that we had never encountered before.”How does MOSCA explore the darker side of success and the pressure to keep growing?“The

items.title: ‘All About Alana’ Charts the Making of an NYC It Girl
items.text: ‘All About Alana’ Charts the Making of an NYC It Girl Summary 'All About Alana,' a new group photo show curated by Ryan McGinley, has opened at Primary Photographic's Rectangle Room in NYCThe exhibition figures actress, model, and musician Alana Jessica Martin through the lens of 30+ notable downtown photographers, exploring the mythology of the muses throughout art history and the role they play in contemporary culture Dating almost as far back as art history is the artist’s muse. One of its more enduring forms in culture is the It Girl, the one who will never wear wrong, always influence, not be influenced. She might not be the first you notice when you walk in a room, but will be the only one you think of when you leave, mastering the kind of elusive cool that won’t ever budge. Every era of New York can be understood by its It’s, Grace Jones, Jenny Shimizu, or Chlöe Sevigny, among them. It's 2026, and a new star has risen.All eyes are on Alana Jessica Martin in a new photo show at Rectangle Room in New York. Curated by Ryan McGinley, All About Alana puts the actress, model, musician, and nightlife darling center stage, tracing the lure of the modern-day muse and her many mythologies.The exhibition features work by over 30 New York-based photographers, spanning selfies, Polaroids, photobooth strips, and gritty black-and-whites, each capturing Martin’s likeness in their own signature styles. One image, the wall-wide opener, channels the drama of a pop confessional, Martin laid bare, with a tear-stained stare locked on the lens; another, high-flashed, sees the artist coolly sipping on Pepsi at Katz’s. Some are explicit in their nod to the other reigning All-American bombshells, with a tattered stripes-and-stars flag high, while Martin stands knee-deep in waves.It’s also a who’s who of downtown photography, so study up, pulling an intergenerational lineup of some of the most exciting image-makers on the scene, such as Daniel Arnold, Charles Caesar, Quil Harwood-Lemons, Jonah Ali Hodari, Jae Kim, Clifford Prince King, Danielle Levitt, Marcus Maddox, Luisa Opalesky, Sam Penn, Richie Shazam, Maxwell Vice and more.All About Alana is now on view at Rectangle Room at Primary Photographic in New York until November 15. items.title: Kim Jones Launches Label & Exits Occur at McQueen & Calvin Klein Collection in This Week's Top Fashion News
items.text: Kim Jones Launches Label & Exits Occur at McQueen & Calvin Klein Collection in This Week's Top Fashion News SummarySeán McGirr exits Alexander McQueen, and Veronica Leoni leaves Calvin Klein Collection.Kim Jones debuts his eponymous fashion label; dunhill heads to Pitti Uomo 111.Tyler, The Creator redesigns FC Barcelona’s kits, while SZA drops her earthy Vans campaign.Kim Jones Announces Eponymous Label With FW27 Debut CollectionAfter much anticipation from fans of the designer, Kim Jones launched a standalone fashion house under his own name. Branching out from his executive tenures at legacy luxury brands like Dior and Fendi, the British designer’s independent label kicks off with a Fall/Winter 2027 collection. Bridging high fashion, streetwear, and utilitarian design, the garments will be primarily crafted in Japan, while the leather accessories will hail from Italy. The inaugural line arrives digitally in mid-2027, with plans for a flagship store opening at Central Yards in Hong Kong that October.McQueen Parts Ways With Creative Director Seán McGirr After Three YearsFollowing a three-year stint at the London label, Seán McGirr officially stepped down as creative director of Alexander McQueen. Parent conglomerate Kering confirmed the departure amidst a broader structural pivot for the brand, which includes staff layoffs and scaling back its 135-store retail footprint. The label recently suffered financial woes driven by over-expansion and a heavy reliance on sneaker sales, which have declined. Brand CEO Luca de Meo emphasized the aim to establish “a bold new direction for the house, building on its unique heritage of exceptional tailoring, uncompromising creativity and rebellion.”Veronica Leoni Steps Down as Creative Director of Calvin Klein CollectionAfter just four seasons, Veronica Leoni concluded her run as the creative director of Calvin Klein Collection. PVH appointed the Céline and The Row alumna in 2024 to resurrect the American brand's premium runway division, which had sat dormant since 2018. Although her minimalist, body-centric vision sparked industry chatter, it failed to generate commercial momentum against a broader 7% quarterly sales dip for Calvin Klein. items.title: Lil Yachty’s Nike Tech Collection Is Larger Than Life
items.text: Lil Yachty’s Nike Tech Collection Is Larger Than Life Summary Lil Yachty’s first Nike apparel collab drops today, with an oversized Tech Fleece zip-up hoodie and below-the-knee shorts, both in black and navy, with heavyweight double-layer construction and Yachty branding.The raffle is for the Lil Yachty x Nike Tech Collection is exclusively available on yachty.shop. Lil Yachty’s first Nike apparel collaboration lands today, October 16, with a reworked take on the iconic Tech Fleece. Dubbed the “best-dressed rappers on the scene” by the brand, the lineup pushes proportions to the extreme in Yachty-style elevated basics, oversized silhouettes, and techy details.The collection features a Tech Fleece zip-up hoodie and 3/4-length shorts, both in black and navy colorways. Both pieces use an oversized fit, double-layer heavyweight construction, and the signature Nike Tech chevron lines. The zip-up adds a structured balaclava hood, adjustable bungee cords, and thumbholes. The fleece shorts fall below the knee and feature cargo pockets, adjustable snaps, and bungee cords, all reimagined with updated neck-tag branding, snap pockets, and custom label graphics with Yachty’s touch.With the tagline “Not everybody fits in,” the campaign stars NBA player Bol Bol alongside Yachty, with teasers directed by the rapper and Cam Hicks. In one, Yachty towers over a crowd at a DMV in his blacked-out Tech Fleece. When asked to straighten up for his photo, he knocks his head through the ceiling, and drywall dust lands on his shoulders. In the campaign’s other teaser, Bol Bol squeezes into a crammed elevator and tries to get someone to press the button for his floor, but everyone is too distracted by his 7'3" stature. The raffle for Lil Yachty’s Nike Tech collaboration is exclusively on yachty.shop. Click here to view full gallery at Hypebeast

items.title: Pro Photographer Megan Collante's Latest Shoot Exemplifies Unbreakable Tradition
items.text: Pro Photographer Megan Collante's Latest Shoot Exemplifies Unbreakable Tradition Toyota has tapped NYC-native photographer Megan Collante to present "A City in Frame: Some Things Never Change," featuring the bZ, part of Toyota’s New All-Electric Family.Since middle school, Kenny and Alex have had a ritual: after school, Alex would be waiting outside by the buses and the two would go get ice cream – no plan, no discussion needed. It's stuck around ever since, even as everything else about their lives changed.Kenny has finally put his brushes down after a 12-hour day in the studio, paint still under his fingernails. His art has only gotten bigger, messier, more demanding as his career has taken off – bigger canvases, later nights, more of himself poured into every piece. But no matter how complicated the day gets, the drive to their spot never does. Alex just puts the bZ in gear and goes, its electrifying performance makes the trip through Manhattan traffic feel effortless and exhilarating, like no time has passed since they were 12 years old. With the touch of a finger, the same playlist they’ve been curating since middle school plays on repeat, turning the bZ into a sanctuary of comfort. And when their one scoop turns into a long night of unwinding through the driving roads near Storm King Mountain, there’s no worry about getting home: miles of charge means a night of memory making.Their tradition bends, but it never breaks. In the end, some things never change.Check out Megan Collante's "A City in Frame: Some Things Never Change," and learn moreabout the all-electric bZ here.Disclaimer: All vehicles displayed are not in motion. items.title: Bartosz Sztybor Warns Fans Not To Get Too Attached to ‘Cyberpunk: Edgerunners 2'
items.text: Bartosz Sztybor Warns Fans Not To Get Too Attached to ‘Cyberpunk: Edgerunners 2' Night City has always been the real antagonist of the Cyberpunk universe — a sprawling, neon-drenched meat grinder where people don't so much survive as try to go down in flames on their own terms. That bleak philosophy gave the original Cyberpunk: Edgerunners much of its emotional punch, turning a standalone anime into a gateway to the wider Cyberpunk universe while helping to revitalize interest in the game franchise.But part of what made the anime resonate so deeply with audiences was precisely that David and Lucy's story had reached a definitive conclusion. In today's entertainment landscape, where successful franchises are rarely allowed to end on their own terms, that sense of finality was arguably one of Edgerunners' greatest strengths. Naturally, when Cyberpunk: Edgerunners 2 was announced, it raised a rather obvious question: what exactly was left to continue?As it turns out, showrunner Bartosz Sztybor had already been developing ideas for future Edgerunners stories while writing the original series. Conversations with Studio TRIGGER about the franchise's future were also underway before its 2022 premiere. The distinction, however, was never about revisiting David and Lucy's story, but rather exploring the countless other lives unfolding across Night City.Scheduled to premiere on Netflix on October 20, the new ten-episode series introduces an entirely different ensemble, with Kai Ikarashi taking over directorial duties from Hiroyuki Imaishi. But beyond its new characters and creative direction, Edgerunners 2 also raises bigger questions about how CD Projekt Red intends to develop the wider Cyberpunk universe.Just days ahead of the premiere, Hypebeast jumped on a Zoom call with Sztybor to unpack the sequel's secret origins, Studio TRIGGER's changing of the guard, and why viewers should never get too attached to anyone in Night City.When the first Edgerunners aired, CD Projekt Red made it quite clear that it was intended as a standalone story. When did that shift into the decision to tell more stories in Night City?Bartosz Sztybor: It was actually before that. I already had ideas for more Edgerunners stories while writing the first season. I don't want to say that the initial claim was unfortunate, because it was completely true: we never wanted to continue David’s story or Lucy’s story. items.title: Vacheron Constantin’s First Concours d’Élégance Spotlights 34 Historic Watches
items.text: Vacheron Constantin’s First Concours d’Élégance Spotlights 34 Historic Watches Summary Phillips and Vacheron Constantin announced 34 finalists for the inaugural Concours d’Elégance Horlogère.A 14-member jury evaluated over 550 vintage timepieces spanning 1755 to 1999.Winners will be revealed in Geneva on November 10 following a public exhibition. Organized as an initiative by Phillips in Association with Bacs & Russo, Vacheron Constantin has officially announced the finalists for its inaugural Concours d’Elégance Horlogère. Billed as the first-ever "Concours d'Élégance" dedicated exclusively to haute horlogerie, this landmark event pays tribute to the international community of watch collectors and the Swiss manufacturer's 271-year heritage.The competition invites enthusiasts from around the globe to showcase their historically significant Vacheron Constantin timepieces, celebrating the pure, timeless beauty and enduring legacy of watches that have been cherished and passed down through generations. More than 550 owner-submitted timepieces were entered following the competition’s announcement earlier this year, spanning pocket watches and wristwatches made by Vacheron Constantin between 1755 and 1999. After authentication and evaluation by the Maison’s master watchmakers and Heritage experts, 95 pieces advanced to jury review before being narrowed to 34 finalists.The competition is divided across seven categories - Chronographs, Métiers d’Art, Chronomètre Royal, Astronomical Complications, Multiple Complications, Design and Chiming Mechanisms - creating a cross-section of more than two centuries of Vacheron Constantin watchmaking. Among the finalists are exceptionally rare and, in some cases, unique pieces: a steel Reference 4072 chronograph from 1940; a 1957 rectangular platinum full-calendar and moon-phase watch produced as a single piece; a one-off 1940 “Don Pancho” minute repeater with retrograde full date; and ornate cloisonné enamel watches depicting maps of the Americas and Europe. The selection also stretches into later neo-vintage territory, including skeletonized perpetual calendars, world timers and highly unusual references whose historical importance has, in some cases, only become clearer through the competition itself.Judging is being overseen by a panel of international watchmakers, historians, collectors, journalists and industry figures, co-chaired by Aurel Bacs and Christian Selmoni, with members including Felix Baumgartner, Benjamin Cly

items.title: SEGA’s ‘Stranger Than Heaven’ Act 1 Trailer Introduces Snoop Dogg’s Orpheus
items.text: SEGA’s ‘Stranger Than Heaven’ Act 1 Trailer Introduces Snoop Dogg’s Orpheus Summary Stranger Than Heaven ’s Act 1 trailer follows Makoto Daito’s arrival in 1915 Kokura.Snoop Dogg’s Orpheus plays a major role in shaping Makoto’s early path.The game launches January 15, 2027. SEGA and Ryu Ga Gotoku Studio (RGG) have released the “Act 1: Kokura Story Trailer” for Stranger Than Heaven, offering a closer look at the opening chapter of Makoto Daito’s 50-year journey.Set in 1915, the footage follows the Japanese-American teenager as he flees persecution in the U.S. and secretly boards the vessel of globe-trotting merchant Orpheus, portrayed by Snoop Dogg, hoping to reach his late mother’s homeland. Orpheus features heavily throughout the trailer, discovering Makoto aboard his ship before gradually recognizing his musical talent and exposing him to the harder realities of the world awaiting him.The voyage also brings Makoto together with fellow stowaway Yu Shinjo, who later becomes one of his closest friends, before the pair arrive in Kokura, Fukuoka and encounter an environment every bit as unforgiving as the one they escaped. Set against jazz and rap-inflected sequences, the trailer introduces several figures who will shape Makoto’s early life while charting the circumstances that begin pushing him toward a career as a showman.The Kokura trailer is the first in a planned series of story previews following Makoto across Stranger Than Heaven’s five eras and cities, spanning 1915 to 1965. RGG Studio’s latest action-adventure moves from Kokura to Kure in 1929, Minami in 1943, Atami in 1951 and eventually Kamurocho in 1965, using each period to trace the protagonist’s changing identity against a reimagined half-century of Japanese history.First introduced as Project Century before receiving its official title, the game combines the studio’s character-driven storytelling and close-quarters combat with show-business elements, with Orpheus’ early influence appearing to establish music and performance as an important part of Makoto’s development. Stranger Than Heaven is scheduled to launch on January 15, 2027 for PlayStation 5, Xbox Series X|S and PC, with the title also available through Xbox Game Pass. Read more at Hypebeast

items.title: ‘Bleach: Thousand-Year Blood War – The Calamity’ Drops Its Final Trailer
items.text: ‘Bleach: Thousand-Year Blood War – The Calamity’ Drops Its Final Trailer Summary Bleach: Thousand-Year Blood War - The Calamity releases its final promotional trailer.The preview centers on Ichigo’s climactic confrontation with Yhwach.The final two episodes arrive October 19 and October 26, 2026. Bleach: Thousand-Year Blood War - The Calamity has released its final promotional trailer ahead of the anime’s last two episodes, bringing Ichigo Kurosaki’s confrontation with Yhwach into its closing stretch.Titled “THE LAST PV,” the video opens by condensing the major battles and turning points that have carried the Thousand-Year Blood War arc toward its climax, before shifting into new footage from the finale. Ichigo and Yhwach remain at the center of the preview as the Quincy King’s plan threatens all three worlds, while Uryu Ishida, the remaining Soul Reapers and their unlikely allies are shown converging on the final conflict. The trailer leans heavily into the scale of the endgame, moving between fractured landscapes, rapid combat sequences and the mounting destruction surrounding Yhwach’s attempt to reshape reality.The Calamity serves as the fourth and final cour of the Thousand-Year Blood War adaptation, which began in 2022 and brought Tite Kubo’s concluding manga arc to animation more than a decade after the original Bleach television series ended. Produced by PIERROT FILMS, the final installment premiered in July 2026 under chief series director Tomohisa Taguchi and series director Hikaru Murata, with Kubo continuing to supervise the adaptation. Episodes 49 and 50 were previously delayed to allow additional production time as the series approached its climax; the penultimate episode will now stream on October 19, followed by the series finale on October 26. In the U.S., both subtitled episodes will arrive on Hulu, while Disney+ will carry the conclusion internationally. Read more at Hypebeast

items.title: CJ Hendry’s “Juju Mega” Takes the Cult Collectible Online for the First Time
items.text: CJ Hendry’s “Juju Mega” Takes the Cult Collectible Online for the First Time Summary CJ Hendry expands her Juju universe with Juju Mega in 10 colorways.A Hong Kong pop-up previews the release from October 28–31, 2026.The first global online drop launches November 1 in blind-box format. CJ Hendry is scaling up her cult-favorite Juju universe with Juju Mega, the artist’s first-ever online release for the collectible series. The new drop expands on Hendry’s ongoing exploration of the space between fine art, design and consumer culture, reimagining her rabbit-like character in 10 distinct colorways.Each plush retains the familiar Juju language of soft, fluid contours, exaggerated drooping ears and a leather flower covering one eye, turning the character into something that sits somewhere between art object and everyday companion. Before the global release, Juju Mega will make its physical debut through a four-day pop-up in Hong Kong, marking Hendry’s sixth major project in the city.The installation follows her previous Juju appearances with Phillips and the immersive jujuworld presentation at Pacific Place, this time transforming a Central location into a lilac faux-fur environment designed around a sense of comfort and childhood nostalgia. Visitors will be able to select their preferred colorway directly for HK$620 each, while the online edition will switch to a blind-box format. As with earlier Juju releases, availability is intentionally finite: once a variation sells out, it will not be restocked.The online drop launches November 1 at 7 p.m. EST via CJ Hendry Studio, priced at $79 USD per blind box, with worldwide shipping available for a flat $20 USD including customs and duties. Each collectible comes in a dustbag, with the broader presentation also incorporating a metal tin, fold-out “map” poster featuring all 10 variations and stickers. The Hong Kong Juju Mega pop-up runs from October 28 - 31 at 2–8 Wellington Street in Central. Click here to view full gallery at Hypebeast

items.title: MAS Transforms Karimoku’s Tokyo Gallery Into an Imaginary Japanese Inn
items.text: MAS Transforms Karimoku’s Tokyo Gallery Into an Imaginary Japanese Inn Summary MAS transforms Karimoku Commons Tokyo into an imagined Japanese inn for “Oyado MAS.”The exhibition explores the brand’s “New Japanese Comfort” through furniture, craft and hospitality.Collaborators include NEW LIGHT POTTERY, Nao Tesuki Washi, SEKISAKA, sheep and sinso. Karimoku is bringing MAS’ idea of “New Japanese Comfort” into a more immersive setting with “Oyado MAS,” a special exhibition transforming the first-floor gallery of Karimoku Commons Tokyo into an imagined Japanese inn.Founded in 2018 under Design Director Wataru Kumano, MAS has developed its furniture through an ongoing dialogue with Japan’s forests, with a particular focus on softwoods and the possibilities they offer for contemporary living. Rather than presenting the collection as isolated objects, Oyado MAS places the pieces within a holistic environment inspired by the rhythms and hospitality of an oyado, allowing furniture, light, craft and everyday objects to collectively define a new vision of domestic comfort.The installation expands on MAS’ functional, understated design language, where the warmth and familiarity of timber are balanced by clean proportions and forms intended to feel relevant beyond a single stylistic moment. Here, that approach is contextualized alongside work from NEW LIGHT POTTERY, Nao Tesuki Washi, SEKISAKA, sheep and sinso, collaborators that also joined MAS during this year’s 3daysofdesign. Bringing these different makers under one roof introduces layers of lighting, handmade paper, objects and textiles around the furniture, creating a lived-in atmosphere closer to an actual guesthouse than a conventional showroom. The result emphasizes material texture and quiet utility over spectacle, presenting Japanese craftsmanship as something integrated naturally into daily routines.In that sense, Oyado MAS builds on the brand’s previous presentations by shifting the focus from individual furniture pieces toward the relationships between objects, people and space. The imaginary inn format offers visitors an opportunity to experience how MAS’ collection functions within a broader interior ecosystem, reinforcing its pursuit of universally approachable design while grounding it in distinctly Japanese materials and sensibilities. “Oyado MAS” is on view at Karimoku Commons Tokyo until October 20, 2026, presenting the brand’s evolving interpretation of comfort through furniture, craft and contempo

items.title: Anna Uddenberg Explores Corporate Control in 'White Noise'
items.text: Anna Uddenberg Explores Corporate Control in 'White Noise' Summary Anna Uddenberg transforms Telegraph Gallery into a sterile office environment for her first solo exhibition in the Czech Republic.Sculptural figures merge with Herman Miller chairs and desks, exploring how corporate spaces influence the body and everyday behavior.Curated by Samuel Staples, White Noise opens October 22 and runs through February 4, 2027. For Anna Uddenberg's latest exhibition, White Noise, the Berlin-based artist is turning Telegraph Gallery in Olomouc, Czech Republic, into a corporate environment where furniture and the human body become increasingly difficult to separate.Opening October 22, the exhibition marks Uddenberg's first solo presentation in the Czech Republic. Known for her unsettling sculptures that explore body culture, consumerism and the influence of technology, the Swedish-born artist takes aim at the everyday objects and spaces that quietly dictate how we move, sit and behave.Most of what we've seen come out of Uddenberg's studio practice, sculptural figures appear to grow through desks and chairs, becoming extensions of the very objects designed to support them. And what initially resembles a functional office gradually reveals something more uncomfortable, where ergonomics gives way to control and the body becomes another piece of corporate furniture. Uddenberg has spent much of her career examining the relationship between people and the objects they use, often drawing from fashion, technology, wellness culture and public interiors. Her sculptures push these familiar references into strange territory, questioning whether the things designed to make our lives easier might also be shaping our behavior in ways we barely notice.White Noise opens October 22, 2026, and runs through February 4, 2027, at Telegraph Gallery in Olomouc, Czech Republic.Telegraph GalleryJungmannova 3, 779 00Olomouc 9-HodolanyCzechia Click here to view full gallery at Hypebeast

items.title: ‘Virgil Abloh’s ‘The Codes’ Retrospective Is Coming to NYC
items.text: ‘Virgil Abloh’s ‘The Codes’ Retrospective Is Coming to NYC Summary The Virgil Abloh Archive™ and Nike will present a New York iteration of 'Virgil Abloh: The Codes,' a retrospective exhibition exploring the late designer's influence across fashion, culture, art, and designThe presentation features everything from finished products, prototypes, archival materials, sketches, to a recreation of Abloh's Paris office The showcase will run from December 10, 2026 through January 18, 2027, with tickets going on sale October 23, 2026 for $25 The Virgil Abloh Archive™ and Nike are bringing back Virgil Abloh: The Codes, the global exhibition dedicated to the life, work, and legacy of the visionary designer.Opening on December 10, 2026, at The Shed in New York City and curated by Chloe Sultan and Mahfuz Sultan, the showcase features nearly 1,000 pieces that illuminate Abloh’s work, creative process, and cultural influence across fashion, art, architecture, graphic design, and music.Grounded in his open-source philosophy, better known as his “Codes,” the forthcoming presentation builds on the methodologies explored in earlier iterations in Paris and Miami, with a greater focus on making “Abloh’s creative thinking tangible,” per a Nike statement.Expect finished works, prototypes, sketches, archival material, and more gems telling of his experimental approach to form and collaborations. Also on view will be a recreation of his Paris office and an interactive media lab loaded with raw design files for a closer look at his processes.Previous editions have debuted previously unreleased footwear, from the Off-White™ x Nike Terra Forma in Miami to the V.A.A. x Nike Zoom M9 Cryoshot in Paris. While anything’s yet to be confirmed, another V.A.A. sneaker could be on the table.“As we mark the fifth anniversary of Virgil’s passing, this exhibition is an opportunity to honor his tireless spirit and how he changed the way people think about creativity, collaboration and what is possible,” says Shannon Abloh, the founder of Abloh's Archive™ and Foundation.“Virgil believed in opening doors and making knowledge accessible, and The Codes brings that spirit forward by sharing his process, his ideas and the extraordinary breadth of his work with new generations. His legacy lives on through the people he inspired and the opportunities we continue to create in his name.”A month-long schedule of performances, workshops, and conversations will accompany the exhibition, with details still to c

items.title: McLaren Racing and PUMA Take Notes From James Hunt’s Rebellious Wardrobe for New Collection
items.text: McLaren Racing and PUMA Take Notes From James Hunt’s Rebellious Wardrobe for New Collection For their latest collaboration, McLaren Racing and PUMA revisit racing’s golden era to craft a new collection honoring James Hunt. One of the most pioneering drivers at the time, Hunt’s legacy extends beyond the track with a rebellious personal style that still stands out today. The James Hunt collection was previewed last month at McLaren’s Designed to Race: Front Row runway show ahead of London Fashion Week. With racing drivers, music artists, and industry experts in attendance, the event highlighted the icon’s effortless dress sense through relaxed racing jackets, throw-over mid-layers, and graphic T-shirts. It showed that racing-inspired fashion isn’t confined to one look but spans more pared-back and playful aesthetics.Now, McLaren Racing and PUMA share a closer look at the garments. Combining cues from the film Rush and the nostalgic red-and-white scheme on Hunt’s car, the black racing jacket features striking piping and the driver’s signature on the collar. These elements are replicated on the grey hoodie, adopting a boxy cut and embroidered red logos. Elsewhere, T-shirts play on Hunt’s expressive approach to customizing his clothes with doodles and text. One piece stamps a “1976” graphic at the center in homage to his World Drivers' Championship-winning year, while another features a heart-shaped motif similar to the badge the driver often wore. Throughout the campaign, the garments are styled with caps and a muted pair of PUMA Speedcat sneakers, in keeping with Hunt's laissez-faire style. Discover the full collection in the lookbook via the gallery above. The McLaren Racing x PUMA James Hunt Collection is now available on McLaren’s online store and selected PUMA stores. Click here to view full gallery at Hypebeast

items.title: Performance Apparel Maker Rhone Brought Pure Playground Chaos to New York Corporate Life
items.text: Performance Apparel Maker Rhone Brought Pure Playground Chaos to New York Corporate Life New York City’s bustling Hudson Yards took an energetic break from the daily hustle when performance apparel brand Rhone transformed the Public Square & Gardens into a massive outdoor playground. Timed right ahead of the NBA season tip-off, the Adult Recess event brought New Yorkers together near the iconic Vessel for a full day of pick-up basketball and classic games. The initiative was part of Rhone's 12 Pursuits, a year-long framework for building a stronger, steadier version of yourself, with October highlighting the pure joy of play—challenging the relentless grind of corporate life by reminding busy adults that progress is about how you live, not just how much you work.The court was alive with non-stop action from morning to evening. Participants jumped into open pick-up games or tried their hand at lower-stakes, nostalgic classics like HORSE and Around the World. Beyond the hoops, attendees customized complimentary Rhone hats with their favorite NBA team, while a live DJ kept the energy high with music, giveaways, and unexpected prizes.The main event hit high gear when two-time NBA All-Star Joakim Noah dropped by to sign autographs, pose for photos, and run the court alongside everyday New Yorkers. Rhone’s leadership team—including Co-Founder Ben Checketts and former NBA executive Dave Checketts—also joined the fun, alongside a crowd of influencers and Rhone Reserve members.The single-day takeover also highlighted Rhone's growing role as an Official Lifestyle Apparel Partner of the NBA, following the launch of their expanded licensed apparel line—which includes women’s gear for the first time.Adult Recess gave New Yorkers a rare, refreshing excuse to trade their meeting calendars for court time. By translating their brand philosophy into an engaging real-world experience, Rhone’s message was importantly about moving, connecting, and playing. Before heading back to their desks, participants walked away with customized gear, fresh memories, and a QR code to keep the spirit of play going all year long. Click here to view full gallery at Hypebeast

items.title: Saint Laurent Spotlights Martin Parr's Playful Self-Portraits in Paris
items.text: Saint Laurent Spotlights Martin Parr's Playful Self-Portraits in Paris Summary Saint Laurent Montaigne presents 'Autoportrait,' a selection of Martin Parr's self-portraits curated by Anthony Vaccarello.Taken between 1996 and 2015, the images capture Parr's playful take on tourism, identity and the quirks of everyday life.The exhibition pays tribute to the late British photographer and runs through January 13, 2027, in Paris. Saint Laurent is paying tribute to the late British photographer Martin Parr with Autoportrait, a new exhibition at its Montaigne location in Paris. Curated by creative director Anthony Vaccarello, the presentation brings together a selection of self-portraits taken between 1996 and 2015, offering a look at the photographer's signature humor from the other side of the lens.Best known for his colorful, often absurd observations of everyday life, Parr spent decades photographing everything from crowded beaches and tourist attractions to the peculiar habits of modern consumer culture. For Autoportrait, however, he became the subject himself, handing the camera over to professional photographers, local amateurs and photo booths during his travels around the world.The resulting images are anything but conventional. With kitschy backdrops, elaborate disguises and occasionally heavy-handed retouching, Parr poked fun at the familiar rituals of vacation photography. Works featured in the exhibition include portraits taken in Singapore in 2007 and London in 2008, each reflecting his fascination with how people choose to present themselves.The exhibition also builds on Parr's longstanding relationship with Saint Laurent, which previously tapped the photographer for its 2025 campaign, An Ordinary Day, under Vaccarello's creative direction.Parr, who passed away in December 2025 at the age of 73, remains one of the most recognizable figures in documentary photography. A longtime Magnum Photos member and former president of the agency, he leaves behind a body of work that made the ordinary feel strange, funny and, at times, surprisingly revealing.Autoportrait is on view at Saint Laurent Montaigne in Paris from October 15, 2026, through January 13, 2027.Saint Laurent Montaigne37 Av. Montaigne75008 ParisFrance Click here to view full gallery at Hypebeast

items.title: MODMNT Reworks Military Classics Into Modular Down Jackets
items.text: MODMNT Reworks Military Classics Into Modular Down Jackets MODMNT, a brand developed by NANGA CO., LTD., one of Japan’s leading down manufacturers, has released the second delivery of its 2026 Fall/Winter collection. The lineup features four styles of down wear reinterpreting functional garments rooted in hunting, military, and other distinct eras and purposes, alongside additional fall/winter pieces.MODMNT takes its name from “Modulement,” a coined term combining “Module,” “Mode,” “Equipment,” and “Element.” This season’s theme, “Beautifully Unpredictable,” translates the free-form processes of layering, removing, adding, and rearranging into the designs, offering wear that transforms with how it’s styled.A standout piece in this delivery is the Field Down Jacket, a contemporary reconstruction of the classic hunting jacket. It features details such as a three-dimensional pocket that integrates a flap pocket with a hand warmer, along with leather patches at the shoulders. Beyond a detachable hood, the jacket incorporates a convertible structure that allows the hem’s skirt component to be extended, enabling the silhouette to change depending on how it’s worn. The outer shell uses a waterproof, breathable fabric with 11,000mm of water resistance and 8,500g/m²/24hr of breathability, filled with 180g of 760 fill-power Spanish duck down. It’s priced at ¥110,000 (tax included).The collection also includes the Super Mackinaw (¥99,000), based on the classic Mackinaw jacket and combining the waterproof, breathable fabric Aurora-Tex® with the flame-resistant material Hinok; the Aviator Jacket (¥93,500), based on a bomber jacket design and featuring multiple pockets; and the C-1 Vest (¥60,500), inspired by military radio vests.Combining elements from functional garments with distinct origins, MODMNT’s down wear allows wearers to transform their own style. The second delivery of the 2026 Fall/Winter collection is available now, having launched on Friday, October 16. Click here to view full gallery at Hypebeast

Offering further insulation for the dropping temperatures, the outerwear range also incorporates a standalone Polartec Jacket.The apparel assortment extends into everyday sportswear and durable utility silhouettes, including a long-sleeve Football Top, a Thermal Lined Zip Up Hooded Sweatshirt, Double Knee Denim Utility Pants, and casual Sweatpants. Rounding out the seasonal drop, the duo has prepared cold-weather headwear staples consisting of a Polartec Balaclava and a knit Beanie.The Timberland x Supreme Fall 2026 collection releases on October 22, via the official Supreme webstore and flagship locations, with an Asia release following shortly after on October 24. The capsule extends into functional cold-weather outerwear and technical staples, including the rugged Kith Vancouver Dejan Utility Jacket and the Kith Vancouver Wyona Sweater designed for mountaineers and nature-lovers alike. Everyday layering silhouettes also make an appearance via the Kith Vancouver Nelson Quarter Zip and the Kith Vancouver Nelson Rugby, giving a nod to the Canadian West Coast's natural scenery.Rounding out the apparel selection, the range features graphic essentials such as the Kith Vancouver Geometric Long Sleeve Tee, alongside the Kith for the Vancouver Grizzlies Vintage Jones II Tee offered in both black and white executions. Accessories and headwear finalize the celebratory release with the co-branded Kith & ‘47 for the Vancouver Grizzlies SL Hitch Snapback Cap, a classic cap, and a custom Kith Vancouver Opening Keychain.The Kith Vancouver Commemorative Collection drops on October 19 at 11 a.m. ET as part of the brand’s Monday Program, launching online and in-store at Kith. items.text: Everything Dropping at Palace This Week Summary Palace’s latest Winter 2026 drop centers on the Dascar range, cut in a spread of Realtree camo patternsThe Dascar Jacket, Hockey Jersey and Shirt each take on a different mix of Realtree Cherry, Shadows, Blue and Edge BlueOn Ya Bike jerseys and hoodies balance the camo with solid colorways in blue, navy, black and brown Palace Skateboards has detailed its upcoming Winter 2026 drop, led by the Dascar range and its run of Realtree camouflage patterns across outerwear, jerseys and shirting. The lineup is rounded out by the On Ya Bike jersey and hoodie, which bring a set of solid colorways to the week’s offering.The Dascar Jacket anchors the week, offered in three versions that move from the reddish tones of Realtree Cherry to a cool Realtree Blue, with a straightforward black option for those who want the silhouette without the camo. The Dascar Hockey Jersey carries the same theme into sportswear, arriving in Realtree Shadows and Realtree Blue, while the Dascar Shirt narrows things down to a single Realtree Edge Blue colorway. Spread across the three pieces, the range uses four distinct Realtree patterns, giving each item its own character while keeping the capsule visually cohesive.The On Ya Bike pieces take a cleaner approach. The On Ya Bike Jersey comes in blue and navy, and the On Ya Bike Hoodie is available in Chocco Brown, black and blue, offering pattern-free staples that can be layered beneath or alongside the Dascar outerwear.The drop launches Friday, October 23 at 11:00 a.m. BST in the UK, Europe and the US, followed by Japan, China, Korea and Australia on Saturday, October 24 at 11:00 a.m. local time. items.title: Patta and Carhartt WIP Bring "Hartt and Soul" to Fall 2026 Capsule
items.text: Patta and Carhartt WIP Bring "Hartt and Soul" to Fall 2026 Capsule Summary Patta and Carhartt WIP have reunited for Fall 2026 to deliver an eight-piece capsule titled "Hartt and Soul"The collection reinterprets signature utilitarian pieces such as the OG Active Jacket and Double Knee Pant with collegiate graphics and custom rivetsEarly access opens October 19 on the Carhartt WIP App followed by a global rollout on October 23 Carhartt WIP and Amsterdam-based streetwear imprint Patta have reunited to launch the collaborative Fall 2026 "Hartt and Soul" capsule collection. Channeling the spirit of their 2014 collaboration, the eight-piece project brings collegiate appliqués and exaggerated rivet detailing to heritage workwear silhouettes.Anchoring the lineup are reimagined staples including the OG Active Jacket and Double Knee Pant, each treated with bold collegiate-inspired lettering and tactile hardware. The utilitarian offering is complemented by a classic work Vest and a cotton hooded sweatshirt, both sporting an oversized collaborative logo lockup across the back.The collection introduces a striking safety orange half-zip knit sweater emblazoned with an elemental work-inspired graphic. Essential layers include graphic T-shirts detailed with a tonal "Hartt and Soul" screenprint on the reverse and a woven co-branded Square Label. The same custom label appears alongside silver-tone rivets on Carhartt WIP’s iconic Watch Hat, while a matching hip bag rounds out the utilitarian accessories.The accompanying campaign was captured by Accra-based photographer Nana Yaw Oduro, who framed the collection across open plains and sunlit coastal backdrops exploring themes of identity and self-acceptance.The Patta x Carhartt WIP collection launches early on October 19, 2026, exclusively via the Carhartt WIP App, followed by a global release on October 23, 2026, at Carhartt WIP stores, online and select retailers. items.title: Getting Ready for the Night Shift Is Like Clockwork for Naz Hassan
items.text: Getting Ready for the Night Shift Is Like Clockwork for Naz Hassan If there’s one process that signals the start of chef Naz Hassan’s night, it’s changing his shoes. Having worked in kitchens across Milan and now London, the simple act of swapping his lace-ups for a pair of work-ready clogs remains constant, helping him get physically and mentally into gear for a busy shift making Italian plates.Exploring what functionality in style means to the chef, Hypebeast heads to his acclaimed neighborhood restaurant, Ornella, for a new two-part UGG campaign. With the debut installment capturing stylist Joel Lyall moving through the night, the latest feature shows how Hassan adapts to the energy behind the counter, as well as the moment he winds down with the brand’s functional Fall 2026 offering. "During a busy day, we’re like an orchestra, and everyone needs to play their instrument in the best way."“Service starts when the first customer comes through the door,” Hassan explains, once he’s slipped into his chef whites and the UGG Otzo Western Clog. “What kicks in is that sense of duty: you have to perform because you’re selling goods that need to be served to the highest level it possibly can.” Today, the chef begins service by making risotto, one of his favorite dishes on the menu. “During a busy day, we’re like an orchestra, and everyone needs to play their instrument in the best way,” he shares. It's not just about the individual performance, though. Hassan mentions how, more importantly, they need to “stay in harmony” so the kitchen can run like clockwork. To keep him in top form, he is drawn to the silhouette’s contoured EVA footbed and lightweight rubber outsole for its support throughout the day. “Having a comfortable pair of shoes is non-negotiable because I’m standing on my feet for 16 hours,” he says. “Shoes are the only part of my uniform that can be personalized, so it's nice when I can bring a bit of myself to my work.”Though Hassan has over a decade of experience perfecting his routine to meet the demands of restaurants, his success comes down to the customers. “What has kept me going when I work at night is seeing the smiles when people enjoy my food,” he reflects on his time as a chef. “The best memories I have are around the table at Christmas, Diwali and birthday parties, so I want them just to enjoy the moment and forget they’re in a restaurant.”"Having a comfortable pair of shoes is non-negotiable because I’m standing on my feet for 16 hours."H

items.title: Waymo Plans First Canadian Robotaxi Expansion in Toronto for 2028
items.text: Waymo Plans First Canadian Robotaxi Expansion in Toronto for 2028 Summary Alphabet subsidiary Waymo has announced plans to launch its driverless taxi service in Toronto by 2028Groundwork begins in the coming days with road mapping and software validation under Ontario's autonomous vehicle pilot programLocal partner Element Fleet Management will oversee all on-the-ground fleet maintenance charging and logistical operations Waymo has officially announced plans to launch its driverless robotaxi service in Toronto, marking the autonomous mobility company's first commercial expansion into Canada. The Alphabet subsidiary targets 2028 to transport its first public riders as technical groundwork begins across the city.Initial deployment kicks off in the coming days with high-definition street mapping and software training led by human specialists behind the wheel under Ontario's provincial autonomous pilot framework. Day-to-day operations—spanning vehicle maintenance, depot charging, and rider readiness—will be managed by Toronto-based partner Element Fleet Management, which currently oversees Waymo’s infrastructure in San Diego. "As a Canadian company, we are proud to be expanding our partnership with Waymo," stated Laura Dottori-Attanasio, chief executive of Element Fleet Management. Longtime backers CPP Investments and automotive parts manufacturer Magna also continue to support the company’s capital and vehicle assembly efforts.Waymo reports that its autonomous fleet has driven more than 400 million kilometers to date, yielding 95% fewer serious-injury collisions than human drivers. While the initiative has earned support from accessibility advocates such as CNIB for offering independent transportation, critics note that navigating heavy traffic and severe winter conditions will pose a rigorous test for the system. The Canadian rollout builds on Waymo's broader international roadmap alongside London and Tokyo.Waymo is scheduled to launch its driverless taxi service to riders in Toronto in 2028. items.title: Quentin Tarantino Confirms Finishing Script for 10th Film but Delays Production to "Live a Little"
items.text: Quentin Tarantino Confirms Finishing Script for 10th Film but Delays Production to "Live a Little" Summary Quentin Tarantino has completed writing the script for his tenth and final feature filmThe filmmaker is delaying production to focus on his London stage play 'The Popinjay Cavalier' and spend time with familyThe swashbuckling comedy starring Sacha Baron Cohen opens at the Phoenix Theatre next March and runs through June 13 Quentin Tarantino has completed the script for his 10th feature film, though the director plans to hold off on production until his London stage production finishes its run. The filmmaker shared the update during an appearance on The Graham Norton Show, marking his first visit to the program in over a decade.Tarantino reaffirmed his longstanding plan to retire from filmmaking after ten features, but made it clear that he will not rush into production. "I've written a script that I really like, but I want to do the play and see who I am; then I'll then go back and spend time with my family and live a little and then see what I want to do,” Tarantino said.His immediate creative focus is centered on The Popinjay Cavalier, which originated as a screenplay before transitioning into a stage production. “It really worked as a play,” Tarantino explained, adding, “I think it will be thrilling.” Billed as a swashbuckling comedy starring Sacha Baron Cohen, the production marks the filmmaker’s West End debut following his 2019 Oscar-winning film Once Upon a Time in Hollywood. “I’m keen with anticipation to give the West End a great night out,” Tarantino noted.The Popinjay Cavalier begins previews in late February before officially opening at London’s Phoenix Theatre next March, running through June 13. items.text: Nike Honors Día de los Muertos With the Kobe 3 Low Protro "Mamba Eterno" Summary Nike is preparing to release the Kobe 3 Low Protro in a vibrant Mamba Eterno colorway inspired by Día de los MuertosThe performance silhouette features floral artwork set beneath a translucent molded cage in Safety Orange Picante Red and SundialPairs are scheduled to launch on October 30 2026 via Nike and select retailers for $190 USD Name: Nike Kobe 3 Low Protro "Mamba Eterno"Colorway: Safety Orange/Sundial-Picante RedSKU: IO6260-800MSRP: $190 USDRelease Date: October 30, 2026Where to Buy: NikeNike is expanding its signature basketball roster with the upcoming Kobe 3 Low Protro "Mamba Eterno". The commemorative edition draws direct inspiration from Día de los Muertos and Kobe Bryant’s deep-rooted connection to the Mexican community in Los Angeles.Departing from the cleaner, monochromatic looks previously seen on the model, the "Mamba Eterno"—translating to "Eternal Mamba"—aligns with the tradition of remembering and celebrating family members who have passed away. The palette combines Safety Orange, Picante Red, and Sundial across the upper in an organic mix rather than traditional color blocking, supplemented by hits of pink and purple.Underneath the signature translucent cage, intricate floral graphics run across different segments of the silhouette. This graphic placement elevates the underlying artwork into a focal design component, contrasting the shoe's molded construction and nodding to Vanessa Bryant's heritage through personal cultural storytelling.The Nike Kobe 3 Low Protro “Mamba Eterno” drops October 30, 2026, via Nike and select Nike Basketball retailers, priced at $190 USD for men's sizing alongside grade school options. items.title: Kylie Jenner Makes Victoria's Secret Runway Debut in $50 Million USD Diamond-Encrusted Jacob & Co. Fantasy Bra
items.text: Kylie Jenner Makes Victoria's Secret Runway Debut in $50 Million USD Diamond-Encrusted Jacob & Co. Fantasy Bra Summary Kylie Jenner made her Victoria’s Secret runway debut at the 2026 Victoria’s Secret Fashion Show wearing the iconic Fantasy BraValued at $50 million USD the one-of-a-kind Jacob & Co. creation is the most expensive Fantasy Bra in the brand’s historyCrafted with 4,410 natural diamonds and a 75.54-carat yellow diamond centerpiece the design marks the return of the runway tradition for the first time since 2018 Kylie Jenner made her surprise runway debut at the 2026 Victoria’s Secret Fashion Show wearing the label's revived Fantasy Bra, a $50 million USD high-jewelry creation engineered in collaboration with Jacob & Co. The appearance marked the KHY founder’s first time ever walking a Victoria’s Secret catwalk.Designed by Jacob Arabo, the showpiece drew inspiration from Jacob & Co.’s Rare Touch Jewelry Collection and reimagined the traditional lingerie staple without using any fabric. Handcrafted by 15 artisans over more than 1,000 hours, the structure incorporates 3,218 individually designed components engineered to move with the body like lingerie. At the center sits a 75.54-carat natural Fancy Vivid Yellow diamond, encircled by 4,409 natural diamonds totaling 1,373 carats in an array of cuts, including the jeweler's signature Angel-Cut. Made entirely of precious metals and stones, covered in shimmering crystals, and finished with delicate fringe along the base, the $50 million USD piece stands as the most valuable Fantasy Bra ever produced.Jenner paired the diamond-encrusted top with a low-slung silver thong, an iridescent white miniskirt, clear PVC heels, and large feathery white wings as partner Timothée Chalamet and mother Kris Jenner cheered from the audience. The runway appearance brought the Fantasy Bra back to the stage for the first time since Elsa Hosk wore it in 2018, following historic iterations previously donned by Claudia Schiffer in 1996, Alessandra Ambrosio, and Adriana Lima. View this post on InstagramA post shared by JACOB & CO. (@jacobandco) Click here to view full gallery at Hypebeast

items.title: Apple's iPhone Duo Reportedly Sells Out Moments After Pre-Orders Open
items.text: Apple's iPhone Duo Reportedly Sells Out Moments After Pre-Orders Open Summary Apple’s all-new iPhone Duo entered backorder status minutes after pre-orders went liveDelivery estimates across all configurations quickly slipped to mid and late November due to tight initial supply and high demandIn-store retail availability and initial customer shipments officially begin on October 23 Apple has seen its newly announced iPhone Duo rapidly sell out across digital storefronts, with delivery windows slipping moments after pre-orders opened at 8 a.m. ET. According to Apple Insider, the initial supply of the new hardware was quickly depleted across all configurations.Within minutes of launch, shipping windows for the device slipped back to November 16 and subsequently to November 23. While Apple traditionally maintains secrecy regarding exact launch inventory numbers, the extended dispatch times point to both significant early buyer demand and constrained launch-day volume. Reports highlight that the phone's intricate design has introduced complex manufacturing hurdles, limiting the initial production yield compared to conventional releases.Arriving as the most expensive iPhone model Apple has ever produced, the launch comes against the backdrop of an ongoing global chip shortage that has pushed electronics costs upward across the tech landscape. While customers can still submit backorders through online channels, supply for day-one fulfillment remains tightly restricted.The Apple iPhone Duo officially arrives in retail stores and begins initial customer deliveries on October 23, 2026. items.title: Philadelphia 76ers Convert Tacko Fall to Two-Way Contract
items.text: Philadelphia 76ers Convert Tacko Fall to Two-Way Contract Summary The Philadelphia 76ers have officially converted center Tacko Fall to a two-way contract ahead of the regular seasonThe roster move follows key frontcourt injuries including a season-ending Achilles tear for backup center Ariel HukportiFall enters his fourth NBA season after previously competing overseas for the Ningbo Rockets The Philadelphia 76ers have officially signed 7-foot-6 center Tacko Fall to a two-way contract, addressing frontcourt depth following multiple injuries during the preseason. The franchise announced the roster move on Saturday.Fall initially signed an Exhibit 10 deal with Philadelphia last month before earning an elevated roster designation. The frontcourt opening emerged after projected backup center Ariel Hukporti sustained a season-ending right Achilles tear during preseason play. Depth concerns compounded further with center Adem Bona sidelined by a foot ailment and Dominick Barlow missing the entire preseason slate due to persistent back soreness.The transaction marks Fall's return to the NBA for his fourth career campaign and his first appearance since the 2021-22 season with the Cleveland Cavaliers. The 30-year-old big man spent his initial two seasons with the Boston Celtics alongside current Sixers forward Jaylen Brown, before most recently playing in the Chinese Basketball Association with the Ningbo Rockets.Fall joins the 76ers' active rotation as the team works to stabilize its frontcourt rotation heading into the regular season. items.title: Apple Announces its Designers of Tomorrow for 2026
items.text: Apple Announces its Designers of Tomorrow for 2026 Apple has announced Parafernalia, Yoonjeong Lee, Salem S. Charabi and Isabel Rower as the four recipients of its "Designers of Tomorrow" award for 2026. The news was unveiled at an exhibition taking place during this year's Design Miami Paris, with new works by each of the four designers on view, each responding to the theme of "Design for Presence"."Each of the works invites you to look closer and engage in multiple senses," said juror member Jennifer Dunlop Fletcher, who is a curator at SFMOMA. "Instead of spectacle, each work beckons a one-on-one encounter to notice detail. These details bring the intimate experience of the work into a moment of focus and presence."For Parafernalia, a studio made up of designers Sebastián Zorrilla and Genki Matsumura (who are based between Monterrey and Mexico City respectively) the theme made them think about conviviality of presence, noting that it is "seldom a singular condition"This manifested in MonoAmbiente 1, a multifunctional piece that explores how different forms of presence – such as a conversation, or a game of chess – can coexist within a single object.Closed, they describe the unit as a "landscape" with acid-etched stainless steel surfaces. Inside, you find stools and a table and a chess board – one set of pieces made by Matsumura, and the other by Zorrilla. Egyptian Danish architect Salem S. Charabi turned to one of the oldest ways of drawing people together. “Light is something we’re all instinctively drawn to, dating back to our earliest fires,” he said, a thought that led him to the lantern.The result is The Eminence of Light. Its veil is made from banana paper, using Japanese techniques applied to Egyptian palm, and sits over a skeleton of hand-stacked date palm fronds on a grooved limestone base. Each strand is three millimetres wide, split by hand and drilled, with ends sharpened by chisel so they interlock. Brooklyn-based Isabel Rower is interested in what happens when an everyday object is made from something people can’t immediately identify. Her Padded Chair 1860 takes its exaggerated proportions from 18th- and 19th-century papier-mâché furniture and objets d’art, setting a high-gloss finish against a fringe of ceramic beads along the seat. “The surface functions as a site for curiosity for me,” explains Rower. “People don’t always know what my pieces are made of, even as they’re touching them. items.title: Roger Gastman on Why Visibility Doesn't Equal Longevity in Art
items.text: Roger Gastman on Why Visibility Doesn't Equal Longevity in Art Summary 'State of Art' is a new HypeArt series inviting artists, curators, collectors and other leading voices to weigh in on the ideas, debates and cultural shifts shaping contemporary art. Through intimate questions and personal recommendations, the series offers a closer look at what is exciting the art world, what needs to change and where things may be heading next. Getting noticed has never been easier for artists. A single post can reach millions, independent exhibitions can attract collectors, and entire careers can take shape outside the traditional gallery system. But turning that attention into something lasting is another story.Few understand that distinction quite like Roger Gastman. The curator, filmmaker, and founder of BEYOND THE STREETS has spent decades championing artists from graffiti, skateboarding, punk, and other creative communities that built their own audiences long before receiving institutional recognition.For the latest installment of State of Art, Gastman reflects on what separates a moment of attention from a meaningful career. While social media has given artists more independence, he argues that visibility alone isn't enough. The relationships, infrastructure, and long-term thinking behind the work are just as important as the work itself.From the value of gallery representation to the importance of making something undeniable, Gastman offers a perspective on what artists should really be chasing."The important thing is that somebody is thinking beyond the next sale."Has social media changed the balance of power between artists and galleries?Absolutely. Artists used to need galleries, magazines, critics, museums and a handful of gatekeepers just to get their work seen or considered. Now an artist can make something in their studio in the morning and have a thousands of people looking at it that same afternoon. That’s incredible.But visibility and career aren’t necessarily the same thing. Social media is very good at creating attention. Building a meaningful body of work and sustaining a career for thirty or forty years is something else entirely.Artists have a lot more control today. They can build an audience and create momentum on their own, which means a gallery relationship can actually be a choice rather than the only path forward.Can an artist build a serious, lasting career outside of the traditional gallery system?Of course. items.title: Announcing Hypebeast Magazine #38: The Juice Issue
items.text: Announcing Hypebeast Magazine #38: The Juice Issue It's been called sauce, swag, aura, and charisma, but none of those words quite do the job. Hypebeast Magazine #38: The Juice Issue is dedicated to Juice, the energy behind the artists, designers, and builders who move culture forward. Across 288 pages, we trace where Juice comes from and how it travels: from a beat uploaded in someone's bedroom, to a sold-out concert, to a creative director's moodboard.Buy HereThe issue arrives with three covers. Xaviersobased, New York's defining Gen Z rapper and producer, opens up to writer John Norris about protecting his independence, taking underground rap mainstream, and why caring about people matters more than playing the part. Yohji Yamamoto, who rarely gives interviews, speaks with Ashley Ogawa Clarke while preparing his SS27 womenswear show about music, his worries for the next generation of designers, and why he still starts every collection from zero. And Tite Kubo, creator of the infamous manga BLEACH, drew an exclusive, original illustration for his cover, and sits down with Ora Margolis to talk about 15 years of weekly deadlines and why the series still endures a decade after it concluded.Buy HereOn the music front, the issue features in-depth stories on Knocked Loose, Syd, and Cash Cobain, plus an exclusive China tour diary from Berlin techno-punk duo Brutalismus 3000.Fashion stories go inside Kei Ninomiya's debut DSM Kei Ninomiya runway show and spotlight LVMH Prize winner Soshi Otsuki, CFDA winner Melitta Baumeister, Taiwanese label Professor.E, Italian designer Mattias Gollin, and Jaden Smith's first menswear collection at Christian Louboutin.Art and design features dive into Raymond Pettibon's album cover art, Los Angeles portraitist Kohshin Finley, British maker-designer Max Lamb, and NYC lighting studio Vy Voi.Buy HereElsewhere, we profile Memphis Depay, the Netherlands' all-time top football scorer; talk with British author Gabriel Krauze about his novella celebrating the Nike Air Max 95; and meet Psyche Olive Oil founder Theophilos Constantinou.Our guides include Eddie Huang's Tropical Tripe Crudo recipe, Gunther Werks' reimagined Porsche 911s, and a roundup of transparent home goods, alongside portfolios from Professor.E's Forgotten Materials line and Max Lamb.Hypebeast Magazine #38: The Juice Issue is available starting today on HBX, shipping worldwide.See past issues of Hypebeast Magazine here.
