items.title: A. Lange & Söhne Marks 20 Years of the Datograph Perpetual in Platinum
items.text: A. Lange & Söhne Marks 20 Years of the Datograph Perpetual in Platinum Summary A. Lange & Söhne marks 20 years of the Datograph Perpetual with a new platinum edition.The black dial features 11 baguette-cut diamond hour markers.Its hand-wound L952.1 calibre combines flyback chronograph and perpetual calendar functions. To celebrate the 20th anniversary of the Datograph Perpetual, A. Lange & Söhne has introduced a highly exclusive 50-piece limited-edition update to the iconic grand complication model. First launched in 2006, the Datograph Perpetual was the brand's first wristwatch to seamlessly integrate a classic column-wheel flyback chronograph with a mechanical perpetual calendar and an outsize date.This new iteration elevates the original design by pairing a 41mm 950 platinum case and matching platinum bracelet with a striking black and rhodié-colored 925 silver dial. Further enhancing its prestige, the dial features eleven manually applied baguette-cut diamonds serving as hour markers, omitting indices at 4 and 8 o’clock to accommodate the prominent rhodié auxiliary dials.The dial is anchored by the signature Lange outsize date at 12 o'clock, which forms the tip of an equilateral triangle with the two main subdials. The subdial at 9 o'clock tracks small seconds, the day of the week, and a day/night indicator, while the 3 o'clock subdial displays the jumping minute counter, the month, and the leap-year cycle. A precise moon-phase display sits at 6 o'clock, completing the triangle.The perpetual calendar mechanism is programmed to remain accurate until March 2100, while the moon phase will deviate by a single day only after 122.6 years of continuous operation. Adjusting these displays is remarkably simple, utilizing a single rapid-correction pusher at 10 o'clock or individual recessed correctors.Driving these dual complications is the meticulously crafted L952.1 manually wound manufacture caliber, visible through a sapphire-crystal caseback. Assembled twice by hand, the 556-part movement features plates and bridges made of untreated German silver, a hand-engraved balance cock, and a classic column wheel to coordinate the chronograph's precise switching sequences. The complex architecture provides 36 hours of power reserve while operating at a frequency of 18,000 semi-oscillations per hour.For more information regarding the timepiece's price and availability, head over to A. Lange & Söhne's official website. Click here to view full gallery at Hypebeast

items.title: Matt Hui's SS27 “Live to the Fullest” Collection Reimagines the Uniforms of Childhood
items.text: Matt Hui's SS27 “Live to the Fullest” Collection Reimagines the Uniforms of Childhood Summary Matt Hui's SS27 “Live to the Fullest” collection explores childhood nostalgia, freedom and self-discovery.School uniforms, scout attire and workwear inspire reconstructed tailoring, delicate knitwear and floral embellishments.A dreamlike campaign explores identity through playful contrasts between reality and illusion. What if growing up didn't mean leaving behind the freedom and fearlessness of childhood? Hong Kong-based designer Matt Hui explores this question through his Spring/Summer 2027 collection, “Live to the Fullest,” a nostalgic yet forward-looking study of identity, self-expression and the possibilities of rediscovering one's younger self.Following his debut collection, which drew from old family photographs and childhood drawings, Hui continues his introspective approach by revisiting the uniforms and everyday clothing that shaped his formative years. School uniforms, physical education kits, scout attire, workwear and even pajamas become the starting points for a wardrobe that challenges the boundaries between discipline and individuality. Hui reinterprets these underlying codes through unexpected proportions, softened tailoring and playful construction, exploring how the conventions of adulthood might coexist with the uninhibited spirit of youth.Throughout the range, traditional wardrobe elements are reconstructed into unconventional yet understated silhouettes. Scarves and ties are incorporated directly into garments, transforming accessories typically associated with formal dressing into integral design features. Classic pinstripes recur across the lineup, referencing the rigidity of uniforms while taking on a more relaxed, contemporary character. Hui balances structured tailoring with lightweight cotton lawn, soft cotton jersey, paper yarn and fine cashmere, introducing tactile contrasts that lend the pieces an effortless, lived-in quality.Delicate floral embroidery, pointelle lace knitting and fully fashioned construction further soften the collection's minimalist aesthetic, while hand-crocheted floral accessories introduce a sense of warmth and personal sentiment. Building on the one-size-fits-all philosophy of his previous season, Hui continues experimenting with adaptable proportions and considered craftsmanship, allowing familiar garments to take on new expressions without losing their original references.The collection's themes of memory and

items.title: Maison Margiela Celebrates 20 Years of Its Ebisu Tokyo Store With New "Folders" Chapter
items.text: Maison Margiela Celebrates 20 Years of Its Ebisu Tokyo Store With New "Folders" Chapter Summary Maison Margiela has introduced a new chapter of its documentation project titled Maison Margiela/folders to honor 20 years of its Ebisu Tokyo flagshipThe project highlights the building's evolution from a former electrical products factory alongside interviews with local Tabi collectors and original staffThe rollout includes a limited-edition zine and an in-store Line 2 cultural dialogue installation open to the public from November 5 to November 15 Maison Margiela has officially unveiled a new chapter of MaisonMargiela/folders, celebrating 20 years at its foundational Tokyo boutique located at 2-8-13 Ebisu Minami.In September 2000, 12 years into the house's history, the brand opened its first-ever standalone store not in Paris or Belgium, but in a traditional residential home in the Tokyo suburb of Ebisu at 3-3-3 Ebisu Minami. When required to relocate in 2006, the label avoided commercial strips and instead deepened its commitment to the neighborhood by acquiring a former electrical products factory just five minutes away at 2-8-13 Ebisu Minami. Retaining team members who have worked at the location since its inception, the space has served as the physical anchor for the brand's identity and creative milestones in Japan for the past two decades.Titled "Maison Margiela Tokyo: 20 Years at 2-8-13," the documentation project records oral histories from staff, investigates the district's creative landscape, and spotlights the local community of Tabi collectors. Alongside the historical survey, the initiative documents "Line 2: Unravelled Memory, Rewoven Future," which captures a cross-cultural collaboration between Japanese artist Mio Suzuki and French tapestry fabricators Les Manufactures Nationales – Sèvres & Mobilier National.The initial archive preview is accessible now via the Maison Margiela website, while the physical limited-edition ZINE will distribute across Ebisu on November 5 alongside the Line 2 installation, which remains on view in-store through November 15. items.title: Marmot x CITY COUNTRY CITY’s “Everywhere” Capsule Layers Up for Winter
items.text: Marmot x CITY COUNTRY CITY’s “Everywhere” Capsule Layers Up for Winter Summary Marmot and CITY COUNTRY CITY reunite for their sixth capsule collection, titled the “Everywhere” seriesA puffer jacket pairs PrimaLoft insulation with a Pertex Quantum shell, while a Polartec 100 fleece jacket comes with matching pants and a capLong- and short-sleeve tees feature archive-inspired graphics on a cotton-like, moisture-wicking body Marmot and CITY COUNTRY CITY have teamed up again on the “Everywhere” series, their sixth collaborative capsule. Designed for the cold months ahead, the collection centers on technical insulation and fleece layers, rounded out by a pair of graphic tees that bring the same performance focus to everyday basics.The puffer jacket leads the lineup, built from two well-known performance materials. PrimaLoft synthetic insulation provides warmth, while the outer shell is made from Pertex Quantum, a lightweight fabric designed to pack down small. Together, they give the jacket substantial insulation without excess bulk.A fleece set offers a lighter layering option. The jacket is cut from Polartec 100 fleece and loaded with an array of pockets for storage, and it is joined by pants and a cap made from the same fabric, allowing the three pieces to be worn as a matching outfit or mixed into other looks.The capsule closes with two T-shirts, offered in long and short sleeves. Both carry graphics inspired by archival designs, printed on a body that feels like cotton but absorbs moisture and dries quickly. The choice extends the collection’s technical approach to the most basic layer in the range.The Marmot x CITY COUNTRY CITY “Everywhere” capsule drops October 24. items.title: YOKE Channels Jean Arp for FW26 at BELOWGROUND Pop-up
items.text: YOKE Channels Jean Arp for FW26 at BELOWGROUND Pop-up YOKE has officially presented its Fall/Winter 2026 collection, titled "Beyond Form," alongside the announcement of its first international pop-up space at BELOWGROUND in Hong Kong.Founded in 2018 by designer Norio Terada, YOKE derives its name from the tailoring term for the pattern piece that connects and joins fabric together, framing the brand's core ethos: “Things connect people, people connect people, and people connect things.” For the FW26 season, the Tokyo Fashion Award-winning designer channels his background in fine art to merge sculpture with daily wear, drawing heavily from the surrealist work of Jean Arp.Guided by Arp’s philosophy that “nature knows no straight lines,” the collection departs from rigid structures in favor of organic contours and accidental form. Classic garments receive subtle, rounded proportions, while trench coats incorporate internal wiring that allows wearers to freely sculpt and manipulate the silhouette. Surrealist techniques also manifest through fabric bonding on glen check overcoats, capturing the visual state of loosely and casually positioned cloth. To translate this tactile concept to the runway during its Paris presentation, Terada placed self-crafted ceramics on venue seats, encouraging guests to touch the organic curves and experience the materials firsthand.Marking a major milestone in the brand's global presence, YOKE is bringing the collection to Hong Kong for its first international pop-up in collaboration with Gallery HBX. Hosted at BELOWGROUND, the installation will showcase the complete FW26 collection alongside an exclusive specialty piece brought over from the label's Aoyama flagship store. In an exclusive conversation with Hypebeast, the designer delves deeper into his inspirations and how he developed the concept for his latest collection.Hypebeast: For FW26, you translated Jean Arp's concept of “accidental beauty” into wearable pieces like wired trench coats. How did it directly inspire this collection?Norio Terada: For this season—the FW26 season's theme, I built the whole collection around Jean Arp. One of my favorite works by Jean Arp is a piece called "Torso." The other is a work where he tore up paper and let it fall to the floor, then took the shapes formed by chance and turned them into a collage. items.title: 8 Must-See Shows in Paris Right Now
items.text: 8 Must-See Shows in Paris Right Now The Grand Palais alone isn’t enough to contain Art Basel Paris. One of the art world’s most anticipated weeks, each year the event, now in its fifth edition, gives life to new perspectives and possibilities, be it at the fair floor, satellite shows, or overheards at the afters.But this year’s edition feels especially urgent. Protests over education cuts and the rising cost of living have left several fairs, museums, and galleries to scale back their weekend programming. While this means an abrupt end to the main event, it’s also a wake-up to the reality of living, a subject that, for centuries, artists never feared to confront. ⁠What’s happening outside the white cube is defining our look inside of it. From new ways of seeing, ancestral histories, and trips through Paris’ own protest history, we’ve rounded up a list of must-see satellite moments, many of which are up through next year. Artists have always had a way with capturing the world, and in these shows, they’re not just facing, but imagining it anew. ⁠Jenny Holzer’s ‘J’ai Vu’ at Musée d’OrsayOn view until February 21, 2027.There’s no one "right place" for Jenny Holzer’s texts. From the streets to the world’s most esteemed museums, the conceptual artist has spent decades turning art into tools of confrontation. At Musée d’Orsay, Holzer pulls from the museum’s own archives, putting yesterday’s writings into monumental LED installations, projects, stone sculptures, and metal paintings into conversation with today’s conflicts and contradictions.Barbara Kruger’s ‘The History of Tears’ at Bourse de CommerceOn view until January 25, 2027.Barbara Kruger’s massive Bourse de Commerce commission sizes up to both her own artistic imprint and ceaseless exploration of visual systems that rule us. Streams of text, video, and collage pour through the rotunda, bringing issues of power, sexuality, and alienation to light. Highlights include “Power, Pleasure, Desire, Disgust,” her 1996 video work that inaugurated Jeffrey Deitch’s 18 Wooster space back in ’97, and the wise words of authors George Orwell and Aimé Césaire, bolded and blown-up around the space. Take it from her floor installation, which riffs off 1984: “If you want a picture of the future, imagine a boot stamping on a human face, forever.”Ibrahim Mahama’s ‘The Harvest Season’ at Fondation CartierOn view until February 28, 2027.Remnants of the industrial past become raw material for tomorrow in The Harvest Season by Ibra

items.text: Ye Plots Yeezy Revival & Kartik Research Heads for Pitti Uomo in This Week's Top Fashion News SummaryZane Li takes the CFDA/Vogue Fashion Fund prize, while Kartik Research prepares for Pitti Uomo.Ye plots a Yeezy runway return in LA, and Virgil Abloh’s archives hit NYC.Kylie Jenner debuts a $50M Fantasy Bra, and adidas taps Willy Chavarria.Ye Reportedly Plans YEEZY Runway Return at New Los Angeles FlagshipYe is reportedly gearing up to host a Yeezy runway presentation at the brand’s new Los Angeles flagship store. The event would mark the label's first runway showcase in over four years. Sources indicate the show will take place at the recently opened retail location at Beverly Boulevard and Kingsley Drive, a space established following Yeezy's soft relaunch earlier this year. Industry insiders also suggest the presentation serves as the official launchpad for the rumored Yeezy 800 sneaker, a tactical runner teased on social media ahead of the holiday season.Kartik Research Named Pitti Uomo Guest DesignerNew Delhi’s Kartik Research is officially the next Guest Designer for Pitti Uomo 111, scheduled to take place in Florence on January 13, 2027. Kumra joins an impressive lineage of Pitti Uomo alumni, spanning from Giorgio Armani to Raf Simons. items.title: Meet Alba, Milan’s New Approach to Golf Apparel
items.text: Meet Alba, Milan’s New Approach to Golf Apparel Most new golf brands introduce themselves online. They build an Instagram following, share a visual world and, eventually, show the product. Alba took a different route. After years of development largely out of public view, the Milan-based label made its first impression in person: a tournament at Circolo Golf Villa d'Este, hosted in collaboration with Porsche Italy.The setting instantly communicated its intent. Founded in 1926, Villa d'Este is among Italy's oldest golf clubs, with a history that gives the occasion a sense of importance before anyone reaches the bag drop. And for a brand's first event, it was an ambitious introduction. Porsche's involvement, meanwhile, suggested that Alba had already built relationships well beyond the usual circle of emerging golf labels.Coming from Milan brings its own expectations. A golf brand from a city so closely associated with fashion invites scrutiny of its fabrics, construction and overall aesthetic. Alba seemed prepared for that. The collection shown at Villa d'Este felt considered from the start, with an attention to material and finish that can take younger brands years to develop.Its appeal lies in the relationship between refined clothing and equipment made to play in. Some pieces had the natural hand feel and restraint you might expect from an Italian fashion label. Elsewhere, nylon, concealed zippers and seam-sealed outerwear made the functional intent clear. Alba also drew on production expertise close to home and sourced fabrics farther away, including Scotland. The result was understated, but it wasn't an absence of ideas disguised as minimalism.The guest list reflected a similarly refined approach. Milanese watchmakers played alongside brand executives, designers and agency founders. Fabio Fognini was there, as were visitors from the UK and France, including people connected to Pluto of St Andrews and Palace Skateboards. It was a gathering of golfers and people whose work touches fashion, design and culture, even if they do not all belong to an established golf scene.Then the tournament began, and the day became distinctly Italian. Breakfast meant cured meats and cheeses alongside espresso, cappuccinos and small croissants. On the course, everyone played their own ball and was expected to return a score. There was a social side to the outing, certainly, but the golf was treated as golf.That balance appears central to Alba's ambitions. The brand had alre

items.title: A Closer Look: How The North Face Designed the Ultimate Reversible Pertex Nuptse
items.text: A Closer Look: How The North Face Designed the Ultimate Reversible Pertex Nuptse The North Face Pertex Nuptse Reversible Jacket delivers a thoughtful upgrade to one of street culture’s most enduring cold-weather staples. Let's take a closer look at the details that make this release stand out. Moving beyond a traditional single-sided build, this update introduces a fully reversible construction while preserving the signature boxy fit and oversized proportions that defined the original. On the primary face, the jacket features classic high-gloss blue and black color-blocking, pronounced horizontal baffles, and the iconic white embroidered chest logo. The outer layer utilizes durable Pertex Quantum fabric—an ultra-lightweight, high-density weave that maximizes thermal efficiency while reliably preventing down leaks.Reversing the jacket reveals a distinctly streamlined, low-profile alternative. This secondary side replaces the glossy baffle aesthetic with a clean, matte blue finish defined by smooth, unstitched paneling. Subtle detailing takes over, featuring a tonal embroidered North Face logo on the chest in place of the high-contrast white branding. While delivering the exact same high-level insulation, this face offers an understated, technical aesthetic designed for minimalist styling.Beneath the shell, the technical specifications are carefully dialed in for cold-weather performance. Packed with 700-fill recycled goose down insulation, the jacket provides exceptional thermal retention without the heavy, restrictive weight of a conventional winter parka. Functional design elements include smooth dual-sided center zippers, reverse-coil zip hand pockets, and articulated sleeve construction for natural movement. Additionally, the high-wear shoulder panels are constructed without prominent seams to reduce bulk when wearing backpacks or layering underneath.Every detail is engineered for versatility and winter defense. A tall stand collar seals out wind, while elastic-bound cuffs and an adjustable hem cinch allow for a customized fit and crop. The relaxed cut offers ample room for heavy knits or hoodies, making it an ideal piece for daily rotation. Combining classic high-shine baffles on one side and a refined matte finish on the other, the design delivers two fully functional, insulated outerwear options in a single garment. items.title: Hypeart Visits: Yichen Ji on the Human Side of Technology
items.text: Hypeart Visits: Yichen Ji on the Human Side of Technology For Yichen Ji, technology is more than a tool for making art. It's a way to explore how we experience the world, connect with one another and make sense of things that don't always have clear answers.Raised in Shanghai and now based in New York, Ji works across digital media, sculpture, installation and printmaking, often bringing computational processes into conversation with traditional materials. His work moves between the familiar and the futuristic, finding unexpected ways to make abstract ideas feel tangible.In "Synthetic Genesis," visitors can pick up a futuristic payphone and speak with more than 100,000 fictional AI personas, each with their own identity and personality. His "Lattice" series takes crystalline structures that could never exist in the physical world and gives them new life through silkscreen printing. Meanwhile, "Chaos Clock" turns the simple act of telling time into something unpredictable, reflecting his own experience of living with ADHD.Across these projects, Ji is less concerned with celebrating technology or warning against it than with understanding what happens when it becomes part of our everyday lives.For this edition of our Visits series, we caught up with Ji to talk about growing up between two fast-moving cities, why he finds beauty in the friction between digital and handmade processes, and what he's messing with next."The push and pull between the polished and the raw, the digital and the physical, comes a lot from living in both."Your practice moves between digital media, sculpture, installation and printmaking. How do you decide what form an idea ultimately takes?Honestly, I let the idea tell me. I usually start with a question or a feeling rather than a medium, and then I ask myself what the viewer actually needs to do to understand it. If the idea is about perception or the passage of time, it probably needs to be physical and interactive, something you have to move around to complete. If it's about images, systems, or the way things are generated, it often wants to stay flatter, like a print. I try not to force an idea into a medium just because it's what I'm comfortable with. The form is just whatever gives the concept the most direct path to the person experiencing it.You grew up in Shanghai and are now based in New York. items.title: Marvel’s Real-Gem Infinity Gauntlet Is Up for Grabs — If You Can Get Approved to Bid
items.text: Marvel’s Real-Gem Infinity Gauntlet Is Up for Grabs — If You Can Get Approved to Bid Summary The one-of-one Marvel Infinity Gauntlet replica set with real gemstones is heading to auction for the first time this DecemberEach of its six gems stands in for an Infinity Stone, and none of them has been treated or enhancedThe piece will tour Bahrain throughout November before going under the hammer in Abu Dhabi The Marvel Infinity Gauntlet replica created by East Continental Gems is set to be auctioned this December, marking the first time the one-of-one piece has been offered for sale. Built using the same design files behind the gauntlet seen on screen, the commission swaps the film prop’s fictional stones for six real gems, each matched to one of the Infinity Stones.The gems are what separate this gauntlet from every other replica on the market. Most stones sold today have undergone some form of treatment to improve their color or clarity, but all six set into this piece are untouched, a combination Julien’s Auctions suggests may not come together again. The standout is the emerald chosen for the Time Stone, a gem first unearthed more than 100 years ago that East Continental Gems kept in its own collection for over three decades and repeatedly refused to sell before releasing it for this project.The construction is rooted in Marvel’s own blueprints. The studio opened up the layered design files behind the screen-used gauntlet, allowing East Continental Gems to reproduce the prop’s form faithfully while substituting precious stones for the props’ fabricated ones. The New York jeweler, a family business working out of the same office since 1972, handled the task of translating each fictional stone into a real-world counterpart.The project traces back to 2019, when East Continental Gems CEO Adam Mirzoeff noticed a toy Infinity Gauntlet sitting on a senior Marvel executive’s desk and floated the idea, mostly as a joke, of making a real one. The finished piece was later shown publicly at San Diego Comic-Con in 2022.The gauntlet will serve as a headline lot of Julien’s Auctions’ Celebrity & Culture Experience, with the sale itself titled Pop Culture Legends. “Presenting it in Abu Dhabi, as part of Pop Culture Legends auction, gives it a stage worthy of what it is: a true 1-of-1,” Julien’s Auctions CEO Ken Citron said in a statement. items.title: The Square-Toe Nike Air Force 1 Low “Triple Black” Is Arriving This November
items.text: The Square-Toe Nike Air Force 1 Low “Triple Black” Is Arriving This November Name: Nike Air Force 1 Low Square Toe “Triple Black”Colorway: Black/BlackSKU: JF7766-001MSRP: $130 USDRelease Date: November 6Where to Buy: NikeThe Nike Air Force 1 Low Square Toe “Triple Black” isolates its redesign to a single zone, reshaping the front of the shoe while leaving the familiar blacked-out AF1 Low largely intact. Viewed from behind or in profile at the heel, the pair reads as the same tonal sneaker that has filled closets for decades, and the real story only reveals itself at the forefoot.The toe box is where Nike made its move, pushing the front of the shoe farther forward and swapping the trademark curve for a straight leading edge framed by angular corners. The effect is most dramatic from a top-down view, where the outline shifts from soft and rounded to something closer to a squared silhouette, giving the low-top a longer, more architectural stance.Everything behind that modification sticks to the standard recipe. The upper is cut from black leather in the same monochrome treatment as the regular “Triple Black,” and the remaining panels and proportions follow the classic Air Force 1 Low blueprint, so the new front end carries the entire visual change on its own.That restraint is what makes the release worth a second look. By editing one element instead of overhauling the whole silhouette, Nike shows how much a single shape adjustment can alter a sneaker this familiar, and anyone hoping for a ground-up rethink should know the updates stay confined to the forefoot.The square-toe treatment also extends to a “Triple White” pair launching in tandem, so both of the AF1’s best-known monochrome colorways get the reworked shape. Each keeps its palette strictly tonal, letting the new toe do the talking. Click here to view full gallery at Hypebeast

items.title: The Weeknd’s New Song “Hong Kong” Is Built on a Faye Wong Cantopop Classic
items.text: The Weeknd’s New Song “Hong Kong” Is Built on a Faye Wong Cantopop Classic Summary The Weeknd premiered an unreleased song titled “Hong Kong” on October 24 during the first of his "After Hours Til Dawn" shows at Kai Tak StadiumThe track is anchored by a sample of "季候風" (“Seasonal Wind”), Faye Wong’s 1993 Cantonese hit, set against his moody R&B productionA visual made exclusively for the Hong Kong dates ran on the stadium’s walls The Weeknd used the opening night of his "After Hours Til Dawn Tour" stop in Hong Kong to unveil “Hong Kong,” an unreleased song written with the city in mind. Performed at Kai Tak Stadium on October 24, the track loops in Faye Wong’s 1993 Cantonese single "季候風" (“Seasonal Wind”), folding one of Cantopop’s defining voices into the brooding sound that has carried his catalog.The reveal landed in the middle of the set, cued by the song’s title flashing across the venue’s oversized displays as the lighting rig flipped to neon. The choice of sample does most of the storytelling. Reaching for a 1993 Cantonese recording ties the song to a specific chapter of the city’s pop history instead of a generic nod to its skyline, and setting it inside The Weeknd’s late-night production lets two very different eras of nocturnal, melancholic music share a single track.The live debut also came with its own Hong Kong-only music video, projected across the stadium’s screens. Its frames lean on after-dark streetscapes, pulling the singer’s moody visual identity into the language of Hong Kong film.Watch the visual below. View this post on Instagram A post shared by Abel (@theweeknd) Click here to view full gallery at Hypebeast

items.text: Everything Coming To HBO Max in November 2026 Summary The Gilded Age returns for an eight-episode fourth season, with the Russell family facing the fallout of Bertha’s social ascent City of God: The Fight Rages On picks up its second season as rival factions battle for control after a drug lord’s death New documentaries from Dawn Porter, Ben Proudfoot and Rachel Fleit arrive alongside a deep bench of holiday classics HBO Max opens its November lineup with The Gilded Age Season 4, bringing Julian Fellowes’ Gilded Age New York saga back for eight new episodes. The premiere lands November 1, kicking off a month that also delivers a second season of City of God: The Fight Rages On, four new HBO Original documentaries and A24’s Tony.Season 4 finds the Russells dealing with the price of Bertha’s hard-won place at the top of New York Society. Agnes van Rhijn spots a chance to claw back her own standing, Marian sets off in a new direction, and Peggy tries to earn the approval of the family she’s about to marry into. Carrie Coon, Christine Baranski, Cynthia Nixon, Morgan Spector, Louisa Jacobson, Denée Benton and Audra McDonald lead a sprawling ensemble that also features Bill Camp and Phylicia Rashad. Salli Richardson-Whitfield directs and executive produces, with episodes rolling out weekly on Sundays and a companion season of The Gilded Age Podcast arriving the same day.The drama shifts from ballrooms to the favelas on November 8, when City of God: The Fight Rages On returns for six episodes shot across Rio de Janeiro and São Paulo. With drug lord Curió dead, a violent scramble for the territory takes hold. Councilwoman Berenice (Roberta Rodrigues) squares off against corruption and an expanding militia, lawyer Jerusa (Andréia Horta) pursues the people who tore her family apart, and Leka (Luellem de Castro) rallies the neighborhood through funk music and dance parties. Aly Muritiba directs, while Fernando Meirelles and Andrea Barata Ribeiro produce.Documentaries carry the back half of the month. items.title: The NEEDLES x Pendleton Collection Puts Six Pieces of Archival Wool to Work
items.text: The NEEDLES x Pendleton Collection Puts Six Pieces of Archival Wool to Work Summary NEEDLES and Pendleton link up for the first time on a six-piece capsule cut from Pendleton’s traditional plaids and wool fabricsA boxy shirt, a jacket with leather elbow patches and a coat in an archival Pendleton pattern lead the outerwear and shirtingPlaid trousers, a mohair sweater in Pendleton’s signature Native-inspired motif and a fully lined Cowichan knit round out the lineup NEEDLES is teaming up with Pendleton for the first time, debuting a six-piece NEEDLES x Pendleton collection that reworks the American mill’s classic plaids and wool cloth. Every garment starts from Pendleton’s fabric vocabulary, then gets recut through NEEDLES’ lens across shirting, tailoring, trousers and knits. The result is a tight capsule where the textiles do the talking and the construction choices tell you how each piece is meant to be worn.The shirt sets the foundation for the collection with a relaxed, boxy silhouette that gives the plaid wool room to drape rather than cling. That easy cut turns a traditional flannel-weight top into something closer to a light overshirt, built for layering through the colder months. The jacket builds on the same fabric language but adds leather patches at the elbows, a reinforcement detail that nods to hard-wearing workwear and protects one of the first areas to wear through on a wool garment.The coat is the statement piece of the drop, cut from a pattern pulled directly from Pendleton’s archive. Pairing that historical print with a full-length outer layer gives the design the most surface area to show off, making it the clearest showcase of the partnership’s archival focus. Plaid trousers complete the tailoring side, carrying the check pattern from top to bottom so the pieces can be worn as a coordinated set or broken up across a look.The knitwear leans into texture and structure. Pendleton’s staple Native-inspired pattern appears on a sweater knit with mohair, which brings a soft, slightly brushed hand and extra warmth to the fiber blend. The Cowichan sweater, a chunky knit style with deep roots in outdoor dressing, gets a full lining throughout, a finishing step that smooths the interior against the skin and adds an extra layer of insulation.The NEEDLES x Pendleton collection is available at Nepenthes stores and the Nepenthes online store. items.title: The Nike Air Max 90 “Light Orewood Brown” Is All Patent Shine and See-Through Panels
items.text: The Nike Air Max 90 “Light Orewood Brown” Is All Patent Shine and See-Through Panels Name: Nike Air Max 90 “Light Orewood Brown”Colorway: Light Orewood Brown/Blue Tint-Sail-Neutral OliveSKU: IX8056-104MSRP: $145 USDRelease Date: November 1Where to Buy: NikeNike is giving the Air Max 90 a material-driven makeover with the “Light Orewood Brown” colorway, pairing translucent overlays with high-gloss patent leather. The palette stays deliberately muted, sticking mostly to Light Orewood Brown and Sail so that texture and transparency become the main event. The result is a quiet take on Tinker Hatfield’s runner that rewards a closer look.The upper is built in layers that play off one another. Textured mesh forms the base across the toe box and collar, while translucent panels sweep along the sidewalls and frame the lacing system, letting the mesh show through from beneath. Down low, the mudguards are finished in glossy beige patent leather, adding shine and contrast without breaking from the tonal color scheme.Nike carries the see-through concept into the branding as well. The tongue labels and heel tabs are rendered in the same clear material, so the logos underneath remain visible through a glassy top layer. Cream laces and a matching lining keep the interior and lacing in step with the exterior, while a tonal midsole houses the silhouette’s signature visible Air unit in the heel.Underfoot, a semi-translucent outsole continues the theme from top to bottom. The standout accessory is a metallic Swoosh hangtag clipped to the laces, engraved with an intricate pattern that is echoed on the printed insoles. That artwork links the pair to a wider set of releases, with forthcoming Air Max 95 and Air Force 1 styles set to carry the same engraved motif alongside their own patent leather and translucent details. items.title: White Mountaineering x Alpha Industries Splice Three Military Classics Into Two Hybrid Jackets
items.text: White Mountaineering x Alpha Industries Splice Three Military Classics Into Two Hybrid Jackets Summary White Mountaineering and ALPHA INDUSTRIES return for a third collaboration, built around two military-derived outerwear stylesA hybrid coat starts from the N-3B and borrows details from the MA-1 and CWU-45P, while a hybrid flight jacket pairs an MA-1 silhouette with N-3B elementsBoth styles combine water-repellent, high-density shells with a breathable, windproof WINDSTOPPER lining White Mountaineering and Alpha Industries have reunited for their third collaboration, a two-piece outerwear release that blends the American military outfitter’s archive with the Japanese label’s functional design. Rather than reissuing a single classic, each jacket mixes elements from several military flight and cold-weather styles into one hybrid build.The hybrid coat takes the N-3B as its foundation, keeping the longer, cold-weather proportions of the original while adding details drawn from both the MA-1 and the CWU-45P. Combining three distinct references in one garment gives the coat a familiar military feel without tying it to any single archival piece.The hybrid flight jacket works the same idea in reverse. It keeps the shorter, instantly recognizable silhouette of the MA-1 and layers in details from the N-3B, bringing some of the parka’s practicality into a more compact flight-jacket shape.Both styles share the same technical foundation. Each is cut from a densely woven fabric treated with a water-repellent finish to handle wet conditions, while the interior is lined with WINDSTOPPER, a membrane that blocks wind while letting moisture escape. That pairing allows both jackets to protect against the elements without trapping heat and sweat inside.The White Mountaineering x Alpha Industries collaboration drops October 31 via White Mountaineering stores, the White Mountaineering online store and select stockists across Japan. items.title: The Evolutions of Jerry Hsu
items.text: The Evolutions of Jerry Hsu All of Jerry Hsu’s pictures are self-portraits. Pink and white flowers strewn in a chain-link fence to make a heart. Hellish plumes of smoke in plain daylight. And car wrecks, most memorably an SUV tipped on its side, the soft red glow of its taillights cradling a “4A POEM” plate. He’s rarely, if ever, in-frame, but there in feeling. Just wait for it.The San Jose-born photographer and skateboarder has a near sixth sense when it comes to capturing these sobering ironies of life, many of which land across the pages of How About Never, his latest book with MACK. Shot over the last 15 years, the project maps Hsu’s inner world through the love and loss that comes with a city as complicated as Los Angeles, where he’s lived since 2011, and what it means to make it home.Early photo blogs and titles, like Table for One or The Beautiful Flower Is the World, too, poke at humanity’s chaotic, often funny, underbelly. But this book, the first dedicated to his film practice, is also his most personal project yet. “There’s a level of isolation I felt living there. I think that’s relatable to a lot of people,” he says, reflecting on his experience in LA through its making. Flipping through its pages, where there’s decay, there’s rebirth. If there’s violence, forgiveness isn’t far off. Just as isolation is the feeling of walking an empty block, it’s also alchemized into intimacy, like being let in on a secret.When you think of Hsu, a number of other portraits come to mind. He went pro at 16, and came into photography through artists skate magazines sent to shoot him and his friends. Skateboarding handed him the reins to his environment, and allowed him to take in the world on his own terms, an outlook that, paired with an appetite for risk, would be useful in front of and behind the camera. In 2017, he made a hasty exit from his pro career, dropping his sponsors in search of the art venture that would eventually become his label, Sci-Fi Fantasy. Most of his days are spent running the company, and while he wishes he had more time for his photography, it’s perhaps a subconscious effort, he muses, of protecting another practice from becoming all-consuming.Told through luminous fragments, the book, much like LA, offers a more nuanced portrait of who we know Hsu, the artist, to be, beyond the weight of his skating career. items.title: Magnum Photos Blurs Fact and Fiction in Latest Square Print Sale
items.text: Magnum Photos Blurs Fact and Fiction in Latest Square Print Sale Summary Magnum Photos' latest Square Print Sale explores the line between reality and imagination, featuring over 70 works by Martin Parr, Bruce Davidson, Susan Meiselas and more.Running from October 26 through November 1, the sale offers signed and estate-stamped prints starting at $110 USD, with a new 9 x 9-inch format available for the first time. Magnum Photos is back with another Square Print Sale, this time looking at the blurry relationship between fact and fiction. Titled "Fact/Fiction," the sale brings together more than 70 photographs that show how the camera can capture reality while also making us question what we're seeing.The lineup includes works by Martin Parr, Chris Killip, Bruce Davidson, Susan Meiselas and Cristina De Middel, among others. Some images capture everyday moments that feel almost staged, while others take a more deliberate approach to storytelling. It's a reminder that even a photograph taken in the moment can leave plenty of room for interpretation.The theme also raises questions about how we look at photography today, especially when images can be so easily manipulated and taken out of context. Rather than offering a clear answer, "Fact/Fiction" leaves viewers to decide what's believable and what isn't.Running from October 26 through November 1, the sale features signed or estate-stamped, museum-quality 6 x 6-inch prints starting at $110 USD. For the first time, select photographs will also be offered in a larger 9 x 9-inch format. Click here to view full gallery at Hypebeast

items.title: Maison Margiela and Gentle Monster Unveil Fourth Collaborative Eyewear Collection
items.text: Maison Margiela and Gentle Monster Unveil Fourth Collaborative Eyewear Collection Summary Maison Margiela and Gentle Monster have introduced their fourth collaborative collection exploring concepts of deconstruction across 43 sunglasses and 25 optical framesThe designs introduce exaggerated proportions second-skin leather wrapping and floating executions of Margiela’s signature four white stitchesThe launch is accompanied by an Alex Prager-directed short film and dedicated pop-up installations opening October 29 across eight global cities Maison Margiela and Gentle Monster have officially unveiled their fourth collaborative eyewear collection, presenting an extensive line of sunglasses and optical frames anchored by the creative philosophy of deconstruction.Elevating and distorting familiar eyewear silhouettes, the collection comprises 43 sunglasses and 25 optical frames that explore modified, crushed, and reconstructed forms. Exaggerated, high-volume frames shield the wearer’s face while expanding peripheral vision, contrasted by narrow, upswept profiles tightly encased in leather to create a seamless "Second Skin" effect. Throughout the range, Maison Margiela’s four white stitches accent the temples, with slimmer models introducing a new application where the stitching appears woven to float along the frame's perimeter.The launch is supported by a campaign short film directed by Alex Prager, following a protagonist navigating an shifting urban landscape during a ten-minute countdown. To accompany the rollout, immersive pop-up spaces featuring unfinished, irregular architectural aesthetics will open across eight international cities—including Seoul, Tokyo, Shanghai, Beijing, Bangkok, Kuala Lumpur, Melbourne, and Paris. In Seoul, an exclusive live performance conceived by choreographer Damien Jalet and artist Ian McMahon will celebrate the launch by translating deconstruction into physical movement.The fourth Maison Margiela x Gentle Monster eyewear collection launches on October 29, 2026, alongside pop-up locations worldwide, with full release details hosted on Maison Margiela and Gentle Monster.Pop-up Spaces Opening October 29thHaus Nowhere Seoul, 433, Ttukseom-ro, Seongdong-gu, Seoul, KoreaTokyo Aoyama FS, 5-chōme-3-2 Minamiaoyama, Minato City, Tokyo, Japan 107-0062Haus Nowhere Shanghai, 798-812, Mid-HuaiHai Rd., Huangpu District, Shanghai, ChinaBeijing Taikoo Li FS, L1 UNIT S10-15 & L2 UNIT S10-23 & L3 UNIT 10-32, BUILDING 10, NO. 19 SANLITUN ROAD, CHA

items.title: Joshua Renfroe's 'BEAU' Is a Portrait of Black Male Beauty
items.text: Joshua Renfroe's 'BEAU' Is a Portrait of Black Male Beauty Summary The 288-page book features portraits of 22 Black men, including 'Moonlight' actor André Holland.Drawing inspiration from Frederick Douglass and Renfroe's Alabama upbringing, BEAU challenges traditional notions of masculinity and celebrates Black identity. Brooklyn-based photographer and multidisciplinary artist Joshua Renfroe has released BEAU: The Black Male Mystique, a 288-page visual exploration of Black boyhood, manhood and beauty.The title, drawn from the French word for "beautiful" or "handsome," also references Renfroe's upbringing in Tuskegee, Alabama. During his senior year of high school, he participated in the Orchid Club Beautillion, an African American coming-of-age tradition in which young men, known as Beaux, are formally introduced to their communities. That experience would later inform his approach to the book.Through intimate portraiture, Renfroe challenges the narrow ways Black men are often represented, making room for tenderness, elegance and vulnerability alongside more familiar expressions of masculinity. Rather than defining what Black male beauty should look like, *BEAU* invites its subjects to shape that conversation themselves.The project also looks to the past, particularly Frederick Douglass, who recognized photography's potential to challenge racist stereotypes and reclaim control over Black representation. Douglass, one of the most photographed Americans of the 19th century, used portraiture to assert dignity and humanity at a time when those qualities were routinely denied to Black people.Featuring 22 Black men across generations, including Moonlight actor and fellow Alabama native André Holland, the book connects that history of self-representation to contemporary Black culture. It includes a foreword by Douglass Morris, a descendant of Frederick Douglass and Booker T. Washington, with additional writing by Curtis Taylor Jr. and design by Fred Sands IV.BEAU: The Black Male Mystique was released on October 23, 2026 and is now available online and globally. items.title: Audemars Piguet Officially Launches Its Certified Pre-Owned Platform
items.text: Audemars Piguet Officially Launches Its Certified Pre-Owned Platform Summary Audemars Piguet officially launches The Watch Keepers, its new Certified Pre-Owned platform.Eligible watches are authenticated, graded and listed directly through AP’s service network.Buyers receive manufacturer certification, a travel pouch and a two-year warranty. Just days after reports pointed to the imminent arrival of Audemars Piguet’s long-anticipated Certified Pre-Owned programme, the Le Brassus manufacture has made it official. Launching under the name The Watch Keepers, the new end-to-end CPO service gives Audemars Piguet direct oversight of authenticated pre-owned watches returning to the market, building on pilot initiatives the brand had previously tested across Japan, Switzerland and the U.S. Rather than relying on third-party dealers, The Watch Keepers operates through a dedicated digital platform backed by AP’s own service infrastructure, positioning the manufacturer itself as the point of contact for authentication, condition assessment and resale. The platform launches first in Europe and Switzerland, with a progressive international rollout planned thereafter.For sellers, the process begins with registration and online verification of a watch’s serial number and proof of ownership, with eligible pieces required to be at least two years removed from their original sell-out date. Approved watches are transported by insured courier to Audemars Piguet Customer Service, where watchmakers authenticate them against the manufacture’s archive registers, assess their condition and prepare detailed listings supported by high-resolution photography and a five-point grading system covering the case, dial and bracelet.Sellers can then choose between a fixed asking price or bidding format, while retaining control over when the listing goes live; importantly, the watch remains their property and is stored within AP facilities until a transaction is completed. The digital experience itself is built around color-themed virtual rooms and “Expert Watch Keepers” - actual AP staff represented as digital avatars - who guide users through buying, selling and editorial content.On the buying side, approximately 100 watches will be presented on the platform at any given time, spanning different collections and eras, with transactional access reserved for registered users. items.title: 'BLEACH' Creator Tite Kubo Designed a New Character for a Limited-Edition Hypebeast Capsule
items.text: 'BLEACH' Creator Tite Kubo Designed a New Character for a Limited-Edition Hypebeast Capsule BLEACH creator Tite Kubo is one of our cover stars for Hypebeast Magazine Issue 38: The Juice Issue, and to celebrate, we're releasing an exclusive two-piece collection with the manga legend.Over 15 years and 686 chapters, Kubo turned BLEACH into one of the best-selling manga of all time, with more than 130 million copies sold. Its influence on the generation that followed, including Demon Slayer and Jujutsu Kaisen, makes it a blueprint for the modern fighting genre.The Hypebeast x TITE KUBO Graphic T-Shirt comes in black 100% cotton with a semi-oversized fit and ribbed crewneck. Kubo's original artwork is printed in lavender across the back, with the issue title and his name in English and Japanese printed and embroidered at the chest.The Hypebeast x TITE KUBO Graphic Ball Cap is a black six-panel style with a curved brim, "TITE KUBO" and 久保帯人 embroidered on the front, and an adjustable buckle strap finished with a Hypebeast label.Both pieces are made in Korea and produced in limited quantities.Fashion has always been part of Kubo's work. He styled BLEACH's cast by mixing street style with runway references from Maison Margiela and Dior, sometimes basing a character's look on a shirt he'd bought for himself. So it’s only right that his Hypebeast cover comes with a capsule collection to match.The collection drops today exclusively on HBX.Read the full cover story on Kubo here. items.title: Palace Skateboards and Nike's Manor Place FC Collection Brings Back the Early-’00s Football Kit
items.text: Palace Skateboards and Nike's Manor Place FC Collection Brings Back the Early-’00s Football Kit Summary Palace Skateboards and Nike are marking one year of Manor Place with the Manor Place FC capsule, a football-inspired collection dressed in Black and TealA custom Manor Place crest runs through every piece, with Orange accents and Swoosh placements that echo football kits from the early 2000sThe lineup revisits the duo’s first P90 collection through tracksuits, training gear, jerseys, outerwear, tees, hoodies and accessories Palace Skateboards and Nike have unveiled the Palace Nike Manor Place FC collection, a capsule built to celebrate the first anniversary of Manor Place, the South London space the two brands have run as a home for skaters, footballers and emerging artists. Designed as a tribute to the regulars and key contributors who keep the venue’s projects moving, the range leans fully into football uniform codes while keeping Palace’s skate roots in view.Black and Teal form the base of the entire collection, giving each piece a dark, club-ready foundation. Against that backdrop, every style picks up hits of Orange, and the Nike Swoosh is positioned the way it appeared on football shirts at the turn of the millennium, so the capsule reads as a throwback kit rather than a standard graphic drop.A dedicated Manor Place badge ties the range together, appearing across the lineup much like a club crest would on a full team strip. That shared emblem turns the collection into something closer to a uniform for the space itself, rooting each garment in the venue it was made to celebrate.The silhouettes look back to where the partnership began. Taking cues from Palace and Nike’s debut P90 collection, the capsule returns to tracksuits, training shorts and jerseys, then extends into outerwear, hooded sweatshirts, a broad run of tees and a selection of accessories, covering everything from matchday layers to off-pitch basics.Beyond the product, the brands are bringing the celebration back to the venue. Palace and Nike will host a skate jam at Manor Place on Saturday, October 31, with skaters and spectators alike invited to take part.The Palace Nike Manor Place FC collection drops Friday, October 30, via Palace online and Palace retail locations across the UK, Europe and North America, with Manor Place, DSM London and DSM LA also stocking it. items.title: Yoichi Takahashi’s ‘Captain Tsubasa’ Art Exhibition Heads to Milan
items.text: Yoichi Takahashi’s ‘Captain Tsubasa’ Art Exhibition Heads to Milan Summary Captain Tsubasa – ONE WORLD ONE TEAM brings Yoichi Takahashi’s original artwork to Milan.The five-day exhibition follows stops across the U.S. and Asia.Limited merchandise and original works accompany the gallery presentation. The global reach of Captain Tsubasa moves from the football pitch into the gallery with Captain Tsubasa – ONE WORLD ONE TEAM Art Exhibition 2026, a touring presentation dedicated to creator Yoichi Takahashi’s original artwork. Following stops in San Francisco, New York, Singapore and Hong Kong, the exhibition arrives in Milan for a five-day run from October 28 through November 1 at iKonica Art Gallery.Framed around the series’ ability to connect fans across borders through a shared love of football, the project translates that same sense of international community into an art setting, bringing Takahashi’s characters and distinctive hand-drawn imagery into closer view. The Milan edition presents original works that are both exhibited and available for purchase, offering a more intimate look at the drawing style behind the globally recognized franchise.The exhibition’s central visual gathers Captain Tsubasa players in national-team colors, reinforcing the “One World One Team” theme through the sport’s universal language rather than focusing on a single club or country. Documentation from earlier tour stops also shows the exhibition operating as more than a static display: previous editions have included football-and-art programming in Tokyo, Takahashi presenting new work, opening events in San Francisco and gallery presentations in New York. In a message accompanying the Milan show, Takahashi expresses his hope that, just as Captain Tsubasa has spread around the world, the exhibition can become a place where new connections are formed.Open daily from 11 a.m. to 6 p.m., the Milan stop also offers several ticket packages combining admission with limited merchandise, including postcard sets, stickers, a T-shirt and cap, with entry beginning at €18 EUR (approx. $20 USD). Each paying visitor can also bring one guest under the age of 18 free of charge when accompanied by an adult. Following Milan, the ONE WORLD ONE TEAM Art Exhibition 2026 continues to Barcelona from December 2 through 6, with a Tokyo edition still to be announced, extending the project’s globe-spanning journey through the end of the year.iKonica Art GalleryVia Nicola Antonio Porpora,16/A, 20131 Milan

items.title: PUMA Gives the CELL GEO 1 an Earthy “Galactic Dust/Loden” Treatment
items.text: PUMA Gives the CELL GEO 1 an Earthy “Galactic Dust/Loden” Treatment Name: PUMA CELL GEO 1 “Galactic Dust/Loden”Colorway: Galactic Dust/LodenSKU: 405336-08MSRP: ¥25,300 JPY (approx. $161 USD)Release Date: November 1Where to Buy: PUMAPUMA continues to push its archival CELL technology into more sculptural territory with the latest CELL GEO 1, arriving in a single “Galactic Dust/Loden” colorway. The chunky runner comes dressed in a muted mix of dusty brown, taupe and mossy olive tones, giving its technical construction a distinctly earthy finish. The upper combines textile with layered leather panels, shifting between smoother surfaces and more tactile textures to emphasize the model’s exaggerated geometry. Darker Loden accents run through the overlays and branding, while tonal laces keep the palette cohesive rather than introducing sharp contrast.Much of the CELL GEO 1’s visual weight sits at the heel, where a pronounced ridged structure gives the sneaker its architectural profile and frames PUMA’s CELL cushioning technology. The bulky rear construction is balanced by a more streamlined forefoot, while a segmented rubber outsole and layered sidewalls reinforce its late-’90s running DNA. Originally developed as one of PUMA’s defining cushioning systems of the era, CELL is reinterpreted here through a more contemporary, fashion-oriented silhouette that places as much emphasis on texture and form as on performance heritage. items.title: AURALEE x TEKLA Brings the Outdoors Into the Home for FW26
items.text: AURALEE x TEKLA Brings the Outdoors Into the Home for FW26 Summary AURALEE and TEKLA reunite for their second collaboration, exploring Scandinavian winter living.Highlights include wool-cashmere knitwear, checked flannel sleepwear, shearling slippers and home textiles.Launching October 28, the collection blends Japanese craftsmanship with Scandinavian comfort. Finding comfort in the colder months is at the heart of AURALEE and TEKLA's second collaborative capsule, which brings together Japanese textile craftsmanship and Scandinavian sensibilities for Fall/Winter 2026. Following their inaugural partnership back in 2024, the two labels reunite to explore the concept of “wintering,” drawing inspiration from the contrast between the harsh Nordic outdoors and the warmth of domestic spaces.Rooted in the Scandinavian philosophy of friluftsliv, which emphasizes the importance of spending time in nature, the collection reflects a lifestyle that embraces the elements while finding equal pleasure in the comforts of home. AURALEE's expertise in fabric development and understated layering meets TEKLA's refined approach to home textiles, resulting in a coordinated assortment of knitwear, sleepwear, bedding and accessories designed to move seamlessly between indoor relaxation and everyday dressing.The collection's knitwear is crafted from a soft blend of 70% wool and 30% cashmere, offered in earthy Forest Green and Soil Brown colorways that echo the natural landscape. Crewneck cardigans and boatneck sweaters are accompanied by matching arm warmers and neck warmers, encouraging tonal layering through relaxed silhouettes and tactile textures.Sleepwear, a returning category from the brands' first collaboration, receives an update in brushed organic cotton flannel, featuring a purple-and-orange “Dawn Checks” pattern inspired by the sky before sunrise. The print appears across long-sleeve shirts, relaxed pants and boxer shorts, introducing a warmer, more expressive palette to the collection's otherwise subdued aesthetic. Together, the pieces emphasize comfort through considered fabric choices, with AURALEE's signature material development bringing a refined finish to familiar wardrobe essentials.Extending the collaboration into the home, the capsule introduces pale green shearling slippers, striped lambswool blankets and deep brown percale bedding, alongside cotton socks in muted blue and grey tones. items.title: AFEW x Saucony’s ProGrid Omni 9 “Tara Hawk” Sneaker Takes Cues From a Venomous Wasp
items.text: AFEW x Saucony’s ProGrid Omni 9 “Tara Hawk” Sneaker Takes Cues From a Venomous Wasp Name: AFEW x Saucony ProGrid Omni 9 "Tara Hawk"Colorway: "Tara Hawk"SKU: S71049-1MSRP: TBCRelease Date: November 7Where to Buy: AFEWAFEW has once again joined forces with Saucony to deliver a more conceptual take on the ProGrid Omni 9, drawing inspiration from one of nature’s most formidable predators: the tarantula hawk wasp.The collaborative "Tara Hawk" sneaker seamlessly blends technical running heritage with an aggressive, nature-inspired design language. Its aesthetic translates the terrifying beauty of the insect into a bold colorway, built around a dark base punctuated by shifting, iridescent surfaces. Translucent blue TPU and synthetic overlays wrap the quarter and heel, producing a glossy, color-changing effect that references the wasp’s metallic body, while gradient mesh underneath moves through flashes of red, orange, yellow, blue and purple. An orange midfoot stabilizer provides a warmer focal point against the cooler sheen, allowing the layered construction of the Y2K runner to become part of the color story.The concept extends beyond color into texture, drawing from both the insect and the tarantulas it hunts. Black pony hair covers portions of the tongue and collar, giving the upper a deliberately coarse, tactile finish that contrasts with the smooth, translucent cage surrounding it. Black leather structures the toe, lace panel and collar, while darker grey and black tooling grounds the otherwise highly reflective upper and retains the ProGrid Omni 9’s chunky early-2000s profile. items.title: First Look at the L’Art de L’Automobile x Salomon XT-QUEST 2
items.text: First Look at the L’Art de L’Automobile x Salomon XT-QUEST 2 Name: L'Art de L'Automobile x Salomon XT-QUEST 2Colorway: “Olive”SKU: TBCMSRP: TBCRelease Date: October 28Where to Buy: L'Art de L'Automobile, Salomon JPL’Art de L’Automobile and Salomon are shifting their long-running fascination with speed toward the people who keep cars moving. First-look photos shared by L’Art de L’Automobile reveals a new collaborative XT-QUEST 2, conceived around the idea of “Mechanic Walking Shoes” and dressed in a single muted olive and black treatment. The upper leans into the model’s hiking heritage with olive nubuck and textured panels, reinforced by an oversized black toe cap that wraps around the forefoot for a tougher, workwear-like finish. Tonal stitching keeps the build understated, while polished silver hardware and multicolored rope laces introduce flashes of metallic shine and color against the otherwise utilitarian palette.The detailing becomes more automotive on closer inspection. A circular car graphic is embossed near the heel, while white L’ART lettering appears across the tongue and Salomon branding sits against the black forefoot guard. Underfoot, the XT-QUEST 2 retains its substantial trail-ready construction, combining a stability-focused bottom unit with a deeply lugged outsole; brown-to-olive marbling along the midsole adds a weathered, almost oil-stained effect that suits the garage-inspired concept. items.title: Hermès Opens ‘HERMÈSTORIES,’ an Immersive Exhibition and Theater Experience in Hong Kong
items.text: Hermès Opens ‘HERMÈSTORIES,’ an Immersive Exhibition and Theater Experience in Hong Kong Summary Hermès presents HERMÈSTORIES , an immersive exhibition and theatrical experience celebrating its heritage in Hong Kong.Highlights include iconic creations, artisanal craftsmanship and surrealist storytelling.Running until November 8 at Freespace, with free admission upon registration. What stories lie behind some of fashion's most recognizable objects? Hermès is inviting audiences to uncover the history, craftsmanship and creative spirit of the French luxury house through HERMÈSTORIES, an immersive exhibition and theatrical experience at Freespace in Hong Kong's West Kowloon Cultural District. Running from October 24 to November 8, 2026, the limited-time presentation offers an unconventional exploration of the maison's nearly two-century legacy, combining an imaginative exhibition with a surrealist stage production. Founded in 1837 as a Parisian saddlery and harness-making workshop, Hermès has since evolved into a luxury house spanning 16 métiers, encompassing leather goods, silk, ready-to-wear and accessories. Rather than approaching this history through a conventional retrospective, HERMÈSTORIES celebrates the anecdotes, creative encounters and artisanal traditions that have shaped the house and its most recognizable creations.Conceived as a theatrical storeroom, the accompanying exhibition offers visitors an intimate encounter with the objects and craftsmanship that define Hermès' identity. The installation invites audiences to wander among iconic creations, discovering their histories, construction and artistic significance through an imaginative presentation that blurs the boundaries between exhibition and stage design. From the house's leatherworking expertise and its celebrated Kelly and Birkin bags to the vibrant silk scarves rooted in its equestrian heritage, the exhibition highlights the breadth of Hermès' 16 métiers and the creative ingenuity behind its enduring designs. Beyond showcasing these objects, the experience explores the relationship between functionality, material innovation and artistic expression, offering a closer look at how generations of artisans and designers have continued to reinterpret the maison's heritage.Bringing these stories to life through performance, the theatrical component of HERMÈSTORIES is written by Pauline Bayle and directed by Joe Hufton. items.title: Tissot’s PRX Skeleton Damian Lillard Edition Is Built Around “Dame Time”
items.text: Tissot’s PRX Skeleton Damian Lillard Edition Is Built Around “Dame Time” Tissot is taking its ongoing partnership with Damian Lillard into more experimental territory with the PRX Skeleton Damian Lillard Special Edition, a 44mm mechanical interpretation of the integrated-sports-watch line developed closely with the NBA star. Lillard has served as a Tissot ambassador since 2021, and this latest project moves beyond simple signature branding by drawing directly from his upbringing and “Dame Time” philosophy of preparation, discipline and perseverance.The familiar PRX silhouette is rendered in stainless steel with deep lateral engravings, while an openworked dial exposes the movement beneath. Burgundy runs across the dial and straps, contrasted by silver-toned architecture and gold-colored mechanical elements, while a seconds hand shaped around Lillard’s monogram and his signature across the transparent caseback add the most immediate personal references.Beating at its heart is a manual-winding Swiss skeleton movement, shifting the PRX away from the automatic movements more commonly associated with the collection and placing greater emphasis on the mechanics themselves. Lillard’s story continues through the accessories: the burgundy rubber strap carries a geometric “milk-crate” pattern referencing the makeshift basketball hoops of his childhood, while a second burgundy leather strap is designed to develop its own patina over time. Both use a quick-release system, but the most unconventional addition is a dedicated leather conversion set that allows the watch head to be removed from its strap and worn as a pocket watch, extending the collaboration beyond the PRX’s usual wristwatch format.The release also arrives as part of a wider homecoming narrative for Lillard. Tissot previouslt previewed the project during the Portland Trail Blazers’ Fan Fest before officially launching the special-edition timepiece in time for Portland’s season opener against the Phoenix Suns. Priced at $2,075 USD, PRX Skeleton Damian Lillard Special Edition is available now through Tissot. View this post on Instagram Click here to view full gallery at Hypebeast

items.title: 'Grand Theft Auto' Beers May Be Coming to Life Ahead of 'GTA 6'
items.text: 'Grand Theft Auto' Beers May Be Coming to Life Ahead of 'GTA 6' Summary Three beverage labels tied to Grand Theft Auto 6 have reportedly cleared the US Alcohol and Tobacco Tax and Trade BureauSubmissions by Florida craft outfit Tripping Animals Brewing include in-game beers Pißwasser and Patriot alongside a new Vice City lagerNeither Rockstar Games nor the brewery has officially confirmed the collaborative drop or announced retail availability Rockstar Games and Florida craft outfit Tripping Animals Brewing may be bringing the franchise's fictional brews to physical shelves with real-world iterations of Pißwasser, Patriot, and No Mames Vice City. According to regulatory records first uncovered by iGrandTheftAuto, official label approvals for the beverages have surfaced within the public database of the US Alcohol and Tobacco Tax and Trade Bureau (TTB).Filings submitted by Doral-based brewery Tripping Animals Brewing indicate that three separate label applications tied to the video game series have received regulatory clearance. The registry includes franchise favorites Pißwasser and Patriot alongside No Mames Vice City, a 6% ABV lager. Suggested imagery shows the No Mames Vice City packaging displaying GTA VI branding, a sunset backdrop, and a dog wearing sunglasses paired with a gold Vice City chain. Government logs show Pißwasser gained label approval on September 29, followed by No Mames Vice City on October 9 and Patriot on October 15.While the registered filings suggest a commercial launch could be in development, neither Rockstar Games nor Tripping Animals Brewing has officially announced the collaboration or provided retail details.DISCLAIMER: We discourage irresponsible and/or underage drinking. items.text: teenage engineering’s EP–35 Is a Guitar Amp, Karaoke Rig and Camp Light With Room for Your Drink Summary teenage engineering’s EP–35 is a battery-powered speaker and amp with line, microphone and guitar inputs plus Bluetooth and USB audioEight guitar fx and eight mic fx run from dedicated dials, ranging from surf-rock twang to a vocal effect called “frog”A storage compartment hides the gain controls, a camp light with a disco mode and enough space for cables, accessories or a drink teenage engineering’s EP–35 is a multi-input speaker and amplifier built to handle a microphone, a guitar, a line-level device, Bluetooth and USB audio all at once. It works as a standalone portable speaker or as a central hub for a full setup, with built-in fx, a hidden storage compartment and the ability to link several units together wirelessly.Every input sits on the top of the unit, each tuned for a different kind of source. A 3.5mm stereo line input feeds straight to the speaker with no processing, which suits other EP series devices, while an XLR microphone input offers up to 54 dB of analog gain and switchable 48V phantom power for condenser mics. The 6.35mm guitar input takes guitars and basses, and a hi mode drops its gain by 6 dB to accommodate active pickups or a pedal chain. Wireless playback runs over Bluetooth 5.3 with LE Audio support.The fx section splits into two banks of eight, each with its own selector and amount dial. Guitar players get clean, twang, blues, od, indie, env, ag and b, covering everything from surf-style tremolo and overdrive to an auto wah and a thickened bass tone. Vocalists can cycle through clean, radio, pop, rock, bass synth, robo choir, frog and megaphone, with the amount dial layering in combinations of reverb, delay, phaser and flanger depending on the setting.Sound comes from a mono 1+1 configuration pairing a 4-inch woofer with a 1-inch tweeter, pushing 35 watts of output with a frequency response of 50 Hz to 20 kHz and a maximum SPL of 94 dB at one meter. A tone knob tilts the EQ toward bass and treble in one direction or boosts the mids in the other. items.title: PAÑPURI’s New Hong Kong Boutique Is Designed as a Moment of Pause
items.text: PAÑPURI’s New Hong Kong Boutique Is Designed as a Moment of Pause Summary PAÑPURI opens a new Sensorial Boutique at Hysan Place in Causeway Bay.“Lush Reminiscence” translates Hong Kong through olive tones, reflections and shifting light.The boutique extends PAÑPURI’s wider philosophy of scent, ritual and holistic wellbeing. In a city built around constant movement, PAÑPURI’s newest Hong Kong boutique is designed around the moments that almost pass unnoticed. Located inside Hysan Place in Causeway Bay, the Thai fragrance and holistic wellness brand introduces “Lush Reminiscence,” a retail concept shaped not by Hong Kong’s familiar landmarks, but by impressions collected while moving through them: greenery flashing between towers, light glancing across glass, reflections slipping out of view and fragments of the city that remain suspended in memory. The idea gives PAÑPURI’s latest Sensorial Boutique a quieter rhythm than its surroundings, offering a pause within one of Hong Kong’s busiest retail districts while extending the brand’s growing network across the city and wider Asia.Inside, those fleeting impressions are translated into an earthy palette of olive green, warm neutrals and muted metallic tones. Curved counters and softened architectural forms temper the geometry of the retail environment, while translucent surfaces, textured glass and reflective finishes allow light to appear, disappear and shift as visitors move through the space. Rather than presenting nature literally, the boutique hints at it - a wash of green here, a hazy reflection there - creating the sense of a garden remembered rather than directly recreated.At its center sits the Scent Altar, where softly illuminated forms partially conceal the fragrances within, encouraging discovery through curiosity instead of immediately revealing every bottle. From there, the experience unfolds across the Perfume Wall, Ritual Sink and Sensory Table, moving between fine fragrance, bath and body care, skincare, home ambience and gifting before arriving at the brand’s personalized Art of Gifting service.Beyond its retail spaces, the brand operates multiple PAÑPURI WELLNESS destinations and more compact PAÑPURI WELLNESS SUITE formats across Thailand, ranging from its flagship urban sanctuary at Gaysorn Tower in Bangkok to the shoreline setting of Andaz Pattaya Jomtien Beach. items.title: WIND AND SEA Teams Up With 'Ultraman' for a Capsule Collection
items.text: WIND AND SEA Teams Up With 'Ultraman' for a Capsule Collection Summary WIND AND SEA partners with Ultraman for a nostalgic collaborative capsule.The drop features heavyweight hoodies, tees, and monster graphics starring actor Shiro Sano.Dropping October 31, 2026, online and across flagship stores. One of Japan's most enduring pop culture heroes is getting a streetwear makeover as WIND AND SEA joins forces with Ultraman for a collaborative capsule.First introduced by Tsuburaya Productions in 1966, Ultraman has become a defining fixture of Japanese science-fiction entertainment, recognized for its towering silver-and-red hero, extraterrestrial adversaries and elaborate monster designs. The partnership arrives during the franchise's 60th anniversary year, offering an apparel-focused interpretation of its visual legacy while connecting nostalgic television imagery with WIND AND SEA's contemporary streetwear identity.The collection merges classic kaiju and superhero lore with WIND AND SEA’s signature typography and relaxed streetwear silhouettes. Across the lineup, heavyweight graphic hoodies, crewneck sweatshirts, long-sleeve shirts, and casual tees showcase archival imagery of Ultraman alongside iconic kaiju monsters and co-branded retro emblems. Rendered with vintage poster-style prints, distressed finishes, and bold color blocking, each garment reinterprets the vibrant special-effects visuals of 1960s and 70s Japanese television into versatile, daily wardrobe staples.Reinforcing the cultural narrative and authenticity of the project, the campaign teaser prominently features acclaimed Japanese actor Shiro Sano- widely recognized as a passionate, lifelong devotee of the Ultraman series - bridging vintage science-fiction fandom with modern Tokyo street culture.The WIND AND SEA x Ultraman capsule collection is set to release on October 31, 2026, and will be available online via the WIND AND SEA official webstore, across the brand’s flagship retail doors in Tokyo and Osaka, alongside select authorized stockists. View this post on Instagram A post shared by WIND AND SEA (@windandsea_wear) Click here to view full gallery at Hypebeast

items.title: WACKO MARIA and Champion Reimagine Reverse Weave Classics for Their First Collaboration
items.text: WACKO MARIA and Champion Reimagine Reverse Weave Classics for Their First Collaboration Summary WACKO MARIA and Champion unite for their first Reverse Weave capsule.The five-style collection features heavyweight fleece, TIM LEHI artwork and bold graphics.Launching October 31, the range includes sweatshirts, hoodies and sweatpants in multiple colorways. Champion's iconic Reverse Weave sweatshirt gets a rebellious makeover as the American sportswear label joins forces with WACKO MARIA for their first collaborative capsule.The collaboration centers on Reverse Weave, Champion's signature construction method developed in the 1930s to minimize shrinkage by cutting fleece fabric horizontally rather than vertically. Reinforced with expansion gussets along the sides, the technique has become synonymous with the brand's durable sweatshirts, providing a familiar foundation for WACKO MARIA's more graphic-driven aesthetic.The five-style capsule comprises a crewneck sweatshirt, two pullover hoodies, a full-zip hoodie and matching sweatpants, all constructed from heavyweight 11.5 oz cotton-blend terry fleece. Leading the assortment is a crewneck featuring subtle embroidery at the chest and a striking back graphic created by tattoo artist TIM LEHI, a longtime collaborator of WACKO MARIA. Available in Silver Grey, Black, Amber Brown, Light Blue and Light Pink, the piece introduces the broadest color palette of the collection.The remaining styles adopt a more restrained Silver Grey and Black offering, allowing their contrasting graphics to take center stage. One pullover hoodie displays an oversized WACKO MARIA graphic across the front, while another pairs co-branded chest embroidery with a prominent “Wacko Maria Paradise” print on the back. The full-zip hoodie follows a similar design language with a bold rear graphic, complemented by relaxed sweatpants featuring embroidered branding at the thigh and ribbed cuffs. Across the range, WACKO MARIA's original patterns and Champion's archival-inspired blue single-color neck labels, referencing its 1970s designs, add further character to the familiar athletic silhouettes.The WACKO MARIA x Champion Reverse Weave collection is scheduled to launch on October 31, 2026, at 12 p.m. JST through Champion's official Japanese online store, Champion Harajuku and Champion Brand House Shinsaibashi Osaka, alongside WACKO MARIA's own stores, online platform and select retailers.
