items.title: Kia’s EV4 GT Clay Concept Is the Ultimate Tribute to Rafael Nadal
items.text: Kia’s EV4 GT Clay Concept Is the Ultimate Tribute to Rafael Nadal With 63 clay-court titles under his belt, Rafael Nadal’s reputation as the undisputed "King of Clay" has brought his legacy beyond tennis to fashion and lifestyle. Now, Korean car brand Kia is honoring the acclaimed player with a one-of-a-kind concept befitting his nickname. The full-scale EV4 GT clay concept features a top-to-bottom transformation, where the doors, bonnet, and windows are all dressed in a red-orange tone. Enhancing the court inspiration, white lines run across the angular edges, matching the white inscribed signature on the back and Kia logo.In an official statement, Rafael Nadal shared, “Kia has been by my side throughout my career, through all the highs and the challenges. Receiving this tribute, created from the material that has defined so much of my journey, is incredibly meaningful. It is a special reminder of everything we have shared, and I am honored by this gesture.”Commemorating a partnership that has lasted more than two decades, the clay concept provides a joint tribute to the player’s career as well as the innovation Kia has focused on over that time. A closer look at the car reveals how these two worlds have been brought together, with a blend of tennis court clay and automotive modelling clay. This combination gives the car a unique texture that's tactile while subtly matted. As the model reinforces Kia’s commitment to “movement that inspires,” Soohang Chang, President and CEO of Kia Europe, shared, “Rafael’s determination and resilience have inspired tennis players and fans around the world, and those values have been central to our partnership since 2004.” “This tribute celebrates Rafael’s remarkable achievements and the journey we have shared. Through tennis and our wider sporting partnerships, Kia aims to bring people together and inspire future generations,” he adds. Discover the car in the images shot at the Rafa Nadal Academy in Mallorca.To find out more about the Kia EV4 GT, head to the brand’s website now. Click here to view full gallery at Hypebeast

items.title: Carhartt WIP and Nike Reunite for Apparel and Air Max Goadome Low Collaboration Collection
items.text: Carhartt WIP and Nike Reunite for Apparel and Air Max Goadome Low Collaboration Collection Summary Carhartt WIP and Nike have reunited for a collaborative collection featuring six apparel pieces and three Air Max Goadome Low WIP colorwaysThe capsule merges Nike's Windrunner chevron with Carhartt WIP's stone-washed Dearborn Canvas and Double Knee utility pant detailingEarly access begins November 12 through Carhartt WIP followed by a wider SNKRS and retail release on November 20 Carhartt WIP and Nike have reunited to introduce a brand-new collaborative collection headlined by the Air Max Goadome Low WIP and a six-piece utilitarian apparel range. Arriving eight years after the duo's debut collaboration, the capsule explores modern utility through purpose-built garments engineered for daily wear.The apparel selection bridges archival outerwear hallmarks from both brands, anchored by the Windrunner Active Jacket. The hybrid garment incorporates a running-inspired mesh lining, contrasting chevron chest blocking, and toggle fastenings from Nike's running shell, constructed from Carhartt WIP’s heavy-duty, stone-washed Dearborn Canvas with triple-stitched seams and a front kangaroo pocket. Accompanying the jacket is the Windrunner Drewe Pant, which merges a relaxed profile with Double Knee utility details like a hammer loop, tool pockets, and reinforced knee panels angled at Nike's signature 26-degree chevron. Complementing the outerwear are heavyweight brushed cotton hoodies, graphic T-shirts, pigment-dyed waffle knit long-sleeves, and stretch-cotton beanies finished in WIP H Brown, Black, Cypress, and Fleur de Sel tones.Rounding out the release is the Air Max Goadome Low WIP, reimagining the rugged outdoor silhouette in a low-profile stance inspired by the Half Dome. Built to endure and age with wear, the boot features a multi-layered upper crafted from durable canvas reinforced with suede and leather overlays. Refined metallic eyelets and miniature metallic Swoosh branding contrast the rugged tooling, anchored by subtle Carhartt WIP branding along the foxing. The silhouette arrives in "Black," "British Tan," and an exclusive "Green" colorway.The Carhartt WIP x Nike collection pre-launches via early access on November 12, 2026, at select Carhartt WIP stores, online, and the Carhartt WIP App, followed by a global release on November 20 via Nike SNKRS and select retail partners. items.title: The Best Car Builds We Saw This Year at SEMA 2026
items.text: The Best Car Builds We Saw This Year at SEMA 2026 This year's Specialty Equipment Market Association (SEMA) show is going on right now, and we were once again witness to some really awesome car builds.For this year's SEMA show, we were presented with a conundrum – how do we cover a show that has consistently showcased some of the most incredible cars in the United States? We've been going to the Las Vegas tradeshow for five years now and each time we attempt at eyeing specific trends. This year however, while a few patterns were noticed, we went with our gut and captured literally anything that stopped us in our tracks – subjectively objective.We're more than familiar with the exotic stuff, but seeing exotics torn apart and rebuilt into widebody monsters transcends the hub bub of restomods and RWB. One of our highlight spots was a Ferrari Testarossa 6x6 – aptly nicknamed the Ferrari F6 – by Gas Monkey Garage that couldn't have been more of a spectacle if it had just another set of wheels attached. Our friend Greg Park also showed up with a widebody converted Bugatti EB110 courtesy of designer Jon Sibal, alongside a McLaren 750S wearing a custom-fabricated Mercedes-Benz CLK GTR tuxedo created by S Klub LA.A plethora of Pocketbunny GTR builds made their US debut across the show, giving kei cars with decent power – SR20, Mazda rotary – the spot light they deserve. OEMs also took the opportunity to show off their special projects, like Toyota's family of tank-tracked pickups and Nissan's tuner-friendly Sentra Spec V concept car.Mike Spagnola – CEO of SEMA – confirmed with us just how substantial SEMA continues to be – the automotive aftermarket accounts for $383 billion USD in total annual economic impact and over 1.25 million jobs across America. Community was a byword during our press trip this year, and it shows with its estimated 160,000 tradeshow attendance and growing sectors of motorcycles, powersports, lowriders and more.SEMA took place between November 3-6 – with the last day being public – but moves on in the form of PRI (Performance Racing Industry, its subsidiary show) from December 10-12 in Las Vegas, Nevada. items.title: Hendrikx Brings Italian Artisanship and 1940s Heritage to Modern Golf Apparel
items.text: Hendrikx Brings Italian Artisanship and 1940s Heritage to Modern Golf Apparel Summary European golf apparel label Hendrikx has launched its debut collection featuring an Italian-made half-zip and poloEach garment is produced end to end in family-run Italian workshops using extra-fine merino wool and ELS Giza cottonBoth machine-washable pieces launch in two colorways with prices ranging from €260 to €390 EUR European golf apparel label Hendrikx has officially debuted its inaugural collection, introducing the Italian-crafted Merino Wool Half-Zip and Cotton Piqué Polo. Founded in 2025 by Jan Hendrikx alongside his partner Karolina, the brand draws upon a family heritage immersed in golf since the 1940s, setting out to infuse the sport with authentic European craftsmanship and timeless, fashion-first design intended for everyday life beyond the green.Following months of extensive textile sourcing and sampling, the founders partnered with a select group of family-run workshops across Italy committed to premium natural fibers. Emphasizing complete production transparency, every garment is manufactured end to end in Italy, extending down to the localized sourcing of the labels and hangtags. Shot on location at Château d’Augerville, a historic castle located south of Paris, the inaugural campaign highlights an ethos centered on warmth, openness, and uncompromising construction across two debut silhouettes presented in two colorways each.The half-zip sweater is spun from 19.5-micron extra-fine merino wool, featuring a custom eco-leather zip puller and the label's submark embroidered on the left hip. The short-sleeve polo is cut from 178 gsm Italian cotton piqué, finished with structured collars and cuffs knitted from extra-long staple (ELS) Giza cotton. Elevated detailing on the polo includes subtle body-colored submark embroidery and custom six-hole corozo (tagua nut) buttons, individually sewn on by hand with thread forming a distinctive sideways 'H'. Both garments are crafted from 100% natural fibers and are fully machine washable. View this post on InstagramA post shared by Hendrikx (@hendrikxgolf) Click here to view full gallery at Hypebeast

items.title: Nintendo Switch 2 Sales Drop Nearly 40% After a Price Hike
items.text: Nintendo Switch 2 Sales Drop Nearly 40% After a Price Hike Summary Nintendo experienced a 37.4 percent year-over-year decline in Switch 2 hardware sales during the first two quarters of its fiscal year following a price hikeDespite the drop in console adoption, operating profits surged 49.1 percent to $1.3 billion due to heavy software and multimedia momentumThe brand maintained its projection of 16.5 million hardware units for the current fiscal year, comfortably offsetting the launch-window cool-off The post-launch honeymoon phase is officially cooling down for Nintendo. Over the first two quarters of its fiscal year, ending on September 30, sales of the Switch 2 fell by 37.4 percent compared with the exact same period last year. During this six-month stretch, the Japanese gaming giant moved 6.49 million units of the next-generation console. Breaking down that shifting momentum, Nintendo shipped 3.82 million units in the first quarter before slowing to 2.67 million units in the second quarter. The sharp hardware decline stands in contrast to the 10.36 million consoles sold during the same six-month window in the previous fiscal year, a surge driven by initial demand after the hardware originally launched on June 5, 2025.A major catalyst for this hardware dip arrived in early May, when Nintendo raised the price of the Switch 2 by $50 USD, bringing the retail cost up to $500 USD in the US. The brand attributed the premium to escalating memory costs alongside complex US tariffs. Nintendo noted that tariffs related to refunds were primarily borne directly by the company, rather than being passed on to consumers through product prices. The resulting drop in hardware unit sales took a toll on revenue streams, with Nintendo reporting a 12.1 percent decrease in overall net sales for the six months ended September 30, 2026. This financial downturn was primarily driven by reduced hardware output, which brought down the company's dedicated video game platform segment by 15.3 percent to $5.7 billion USD.Despite the drop in console adoption, the financial architecture behind the brand proved resilient. In contrast to the hardware decline, Nintendo saw its operating profit surge by 49.1 percent, climbing to ¥216.5 billion JPY, or approximately $1.3 billion USD. Overall net profit also rose 11 percent from a year earlier. This bottom-line expansion was supported by a strategic first-quarter US tariff refund and heavy cultural crossover success. items.title: Sony Reports a 44% Jump in Quarterly Net Profit Driven by 'Spider-Man: Brand New Day' and PlayStation
items.text: Sony Reports a 44% Jump in Quarterly Net Profit Driven by 'Spider-Man: Brand New Day' and PlayStation Summary Sony reported a 44 percent net profit increase in Q2 2026, reaching $2.84 billionSpider-Man: Brand New Day drove a massive 527 percent jump in Sony Pictures earningsPlayStation software sales climbed despite hardware dips and an organized player blackout On November 5, Sony published its Q2 earnings materials for the 2026 fiscal year, revealing a massive financial surge driven by its entertainment and gaming divisions. The conglomerate reported net profits of ¥449.60 billion JPY, or approximately $2.84 billion USD, for the three months ending in September. Those numbers represented a steep 44 percent increase compared to the 311.4 billion yen, or roughly $1.96 billion, reported during the same period in 2025. This profit spike was largely fueled by its PlayStation business and the massive theatrical dominance of Spider-Man: Brand New Day.The cinematic return of the web-slinger completely reshaped the balance sheet for the film wing of the company. Released in July, Spider-Man: Brand New Day obliterated the global box office, taking in $2.52 billion during its theatrical run. That massive haul officially cemented the project as the third-highest grossing movie in history. Consequently, Sony Pictures Entertainment posted earnings of $581 million for the three months ended September. The Pictures division’s earnings marked a 527 percent jump from the $93 million reported for the same period in 2025.Over in the interactive division, the financial reality presented a stark split between hardware adoption and software consumption. Sales of PlayStation 5 consoles fell to 2.6 million units during the second quarter. By comparison, Sony sold 4 million PlayStation 5 units during Q2 2025. However, overall PlayStation game sales increased across both digital downloads and physical discs. The high-profile, Sony-exclusive game Marvel’s Wolverine generated significant commercial traction, selling 2.4 million units worldwide against a reported development budget of $300 million.That upward trajectory in software sales carries profound implications for the brand, as the overall growth occurred despite a week-long player blackout organized in August. The widespread protest was explicitly formed to push back against Sony's overarching plans to phase out physical game discs entirely. items.title: James Wan and Jason Blum Unveil Merged Production Banner Blumhouse Atomic
items.text: James Wan and Jason Blum Unveil Merged Production Banner Blumhouse Atomic Summary James Wan and Jason Blum have officially unveiled Blumhouse Atomic as the new umbrella title for their merged production companiesBoth Blumhouse and Atomic Monster will maintain distinct production labels while developing film and television projectsThe announcement follows a combined $2.5 billion USD global box office run and precedes an extensive 2027 horror slate Horror titans Jason Blum and James Wan have officially introduced Blumhouse Atomic, the new umbrella banner uniting their merged production companies Blumhouse and Atomic Monster. The joint corporate identity formalizes the creative alliance between the two genre powerhouses while allowing both labels to continue operating as distinct production entities.“When we merged our companies, we believed the whole would be greater than the sum of its parts and that is exactly what has happened,” stated Jason Blum. “We have the output of a studio with the creative freedom and financial discipline of an independent company, and more opportunities than ever to take these stories beyond the theater and into television, games and live experiences.” Since combining operations in 2024, the collaborative banners have grossed over $2.5 billion globally against production budgets under $330 million, bolstered in 2026 by Curry Barker’s Obsession and Kane Parsons’ Backrooms.“The future of horror comes from new voices, and Blumhouse Atomic gives us more ways to find them and support them for the long haul,” added James Wan. To support this micro-budget framework, the company appointed Sam Zimmerman as senior vice president of development and acquisitions to oversee genre features budgeted under $5 million, alongside a first-look agreement with Divide/Conquer ahead of a 2027 theatrical slate featuring The Exorcist: Martyrs and Blair Witch. items.title: Secret Deals Expose HYBE and ADOR's Firm Grip on K-Pop Sensation NewJeans
items.text: Secret Deals Expose HYBE and ADOR's Firm Grip on K-Pop Sensation NewJeans Summary An investigation by The New York Times reveals restrictive confidential contracts signed by NewJeans under ADOR and HYBEThe agreements omitted standard government child protections while imposing severe behavioral conduct clauses and heavy exit penaltiesProvisions grant the label perpetual rights to the members' likenesses and AI-generated voice clones beyond the contract term An investigative report into confidential agreements signed by record-breaking K-pop group NewJeans has revealed the extraordinary level of institutional control exerted by label ADOR and parent conglomerate HYBE. The New York Times obtained contracts—signed when members were between ages 14 and 17—which exposed how standard protections were stripped away beneath the surface of the group’s global commercial rise.According to the documents, the contracts removed key safeguards established in the South Korean government’s standard entertainment template, including guarantees for basic human rights, mental and physical health, education, and limits on excessive working hours. Instead, the agreements introduced strict behavioral mandates barring an “insincere attitude,” “neglect of self-management,” “inappropriate romantic relationships,” and making statements that could harm the company’s reputation. “This contract is unusually aggressive,” stated Seoul-based entertainment lawyer Jong-eon Roh. “It restricts the artists’ freedom to a degree rarely seen, even in recent major-label contracts.” U.S. entertainment attorney Dina LaPolt emphasized the stark industry contrast, noting, “In K-pop, you either do what they say, dress as they say, do your hair as they say, or you’re going to get replaced.”The contracts also enforced aggressive financial mechanisms, requiring members to repay trainee-era cosmetic procedures and establishing calculated exit penalties that only factor in profitable months. Following the group's attempted exit—which member Hanni Pham framed by stating, “Staying at the company will only prolong our psychological pain”—ADOR terminated member Danielle Marsh in December 2025 and filed a roughly $22 million USD lawsuit over unauthorized solo appearances. items.title: Paul Bettany Joins Steven Yeun in Netflix Supernatural Drama Series 'Pagans'
items.text: Paul Bettany Joins Steven Yeun in Netflix Supernatural Drama Series 'Pagans' Summary Paul Bettany has joined Steven Yeun in the upcoming Netflix supernatural drama series PagansCreated and showrun by Joshua Zetumer the series explores a fracturing family confronting sinister circumstancesBettany is set to portray a charismatic stranger named Mag alongside an ensemble including Marin Ireland and Logan Kim Streaming giant Netflix has officially cast Paul Bettany to star opposite Steven Yeun in the upcoming supernatural drama series Pagans. The high-profile project is created and executive produced by Say Nothing creator Joshua Zetumer, exploring the unsettling darkness and emotional tension buried within contemporary family life.The narrative follows Gus, portrayed by Yeun, who is left as the sole caretaker of his two children following the sudden and tragic loss of his wife. While his son Nate, played by Logan Kim, navigates a conventional upbringing, his daughter Alice, played by Sabine Grace, begins displaying deeply unsettling behavior. What initially appears as a strained relationship between father and daughter gradually transforms into something far more sinister. Bettany joins the cast as Mag, an enigmatic and charismatic stranger, starring alongside Marin Ireland as single mother Janelle and Intae Kim as Gus’ younger brother Casey.Zetumer serves as lead showrunner and executive producer alongside Drew Goddard and Sarah Esberg for Goddard Textiles, Jonathan van Tulleken, Erica Kay, and Celadon Pictures’ Yeun and Christina Oh. The high-profile casting continues Bettany’s active television run following his portrayal of the synthezoid Vision in Marvel's Disney+ series VisionQuest and Antonio Salieri in Sky Originals’ Amadeus. items.title: Electronic Arts Launches 25 Classic PC Games on Steam for the First Time
items.text: Electronic Arts Launches 25 Classic PC Games on Steam for the First Time Summary Electronic Arts dropped 25 classic PC titles on Steam, GOG and the EA AppThe massive release features seven fully restored Anniversary Editions for Road Rash and Wing CommanderThe preservation effort utilized a newly discovered vault of physical media to rescue and reedit original master sequences The video game industry faces a growing cultural crisis as classic titles increasingly risk being lost to time, trapped behind incompatible modern hardware, deprecating physical media and forgotten storage archives. Stepping up to combat this digital decay, Electronic Arts launched 25 classic PC games on Steam for the first time. The drop, which is also available on GOG and the EA App, serves as a crucial preservation milestone that rescues foundational gaming history from technological obsolescence.The sprawling release was sparked by an internal archaeological find. Jim Vessella, a Senior Producer with the EA Partners team, was part of the group that initiated the dedicated game preservation effort at Electronic Arts. That initiative struck gold when the team discovered a physical media vault containing thousands of Betacam, VHS and D1 tapes alongside other assets. Through a meticulous digitization process, EA recovered master Full-Motion Video (FMV) sequences. Using these master tapes, the team reedited the archival footage to restore more than 1,500 scenes in higher resolution.The crown jewels of this archival drop are seven newly restored Anniversary Editions encompassing the motorcycle racer Road Rash and six Wing Commander titles, all priced at $9.99 USD each. These specialized releases maintain the original look and feel of the games while packing in essential quality-of-life updates to improve overall performance and ensure support for modern systems and controls. The 35th Anniversary Editions bundle Wing Commander and Wing Commander II: Vengeance of the Kilrathi. The 30th Anniversary Editions bring back Road Rash, Wing Commander III: Heart of the Tiger, Wing Commander IV: The Price of Freedom, Wing Commander Prophecy and Privateer 2: The Darkening. In a nod to the dedicated fanbases that kept these universes alive, the updated Wing Commander titles officially incorporate community-made mods.Beyond the flagship restorations, the remainder of the classic games cost $4.99 USF each. items.title: Art Collaboration Kyoto Spotlights Global Gallery Partnerships
items.text: Art Collaboration Kyoto Spotlights Global Gallery Partnerships Summary The 2026 edition brings together 63 galleries from 18 countries and regions, spotlighting collaborations between Japanese and international galleries.Beyond the fair, visitors can explore experimental installations, artist talks, and exhibitions across Kyoto’s historic temples and cultural landmarks. Art Collaboration Kyoto (ACK) returns for its sixth edition from November 7 to 9, bringing together 63 galleries from 18 countries and regions at the Kyoto International Conference Center. With an expanded international presence and a newly established leadership structure, the 2026 fair continues its mission of fostering cross-cultural exchange between Japan's contemporary art scene and the wider global art community.At the heart of ACK are two signature sections: Gallery Collaborations and Kyoto Meetings. The former pairs Japanese galleries with international counterparts in shared exhibition spaces, encouraging dialogue across artistic practices and cultural perspectives. This year's participants include Tokyo's NANZUKA, which joins forces with New York's Jeffrey Deitch, TARO NASU with Hauser & Wirth, and Tokyo Gallery + BTAP with Seoul's Gallery Hyundai. Meanwhile, Kyoto Meetings spotlights artists and works connected to the historic city, with presentations from galleries including Perrotin, Art Court Gallery, and Kiang Malingue.Beyond the gallery presentations, ACK introduces ACK Intersections, a curated exhibition led by Leonhard Bartolomeus of the Yamaguchi Center for Arts and Media (YCAM). Titled Out of Bounds, the program explores the invisible boundaries that shape our relationships with art, architecture, and one another. Featuring works by Ernesto Neto, Efrain Almeida, Piotr Kowalski, and others, the exhibition activates the Kyoto International Conference Center's distinctive architectural spaces. Additional programming includes installations by Aiko Miyanaga, Eriko Mukai, and Ryunosuke Okazaki, alongside a series of conversations featuring influential figures such as Arthur Jafa, Kazuyo Sejima, and Tomio Koyama.The fair's cultural footprint also extends throughout Kyoto through its What's On initiative, which highlights exhibitions staged across the city's galleries, temples, and historic landmarks. items.title: Christopher Nolan's 'The Odyssey' Returns to IMAX 70mm Theaters This December
items.text: Christopher Nolan's 'The Odyssey' Returns to IMAX 70mm Theaters This December Summary Universal Pictures will re-release Christopher Nolan's The Odyssey in more than 1000 theaters across the United States and CanadaThe epic was the first film shot entirely on Imax cameras and grossed over 1.8 billion USD worldwideThe film returns to all theatrical formats including Imax 70mm beginning December 11 Film studio Universal Pictures has announced that Christopher Nolan's historical epic The Odyssey will return to theaters nationwide for an expansive theatrical re-release. Starting December 11, the studio will bring the blockbuster back to more than 1,000 screens across the United States and Canada in all formats, highlighted by screenings in IMAX and the coveted IMAX 70mm format.Originally released on July 17, the three-hour historical drama grossed $626 million USD domestically and $1.8 billion USD worldwide, solidifying its place as both Universal's and Nolan's highest-grossing film to date and the second-highest grossing cinematic release of 2026 behind Spider-Man: Brand New Day. Groundbreaking in its technical execution, the feature stands as the first movie filmed entirely with Imax cameras, generating $550 million USD across IMAX screens globally and setting records for both the highest-grossing IMAX title of all time and the biggest domestic opening in IMAX 70mm history.Based on the ancient Greek epic poem, the narrative chronicles King Odysseus of Ithaca's treacherous journey home following victory in the Trojan War. Matt Damon leads the ensemble as Odysseus alongside Tom Holland, Anne Hathaway, Robert Pattinson, Zendaya, Lupita Nyong’o, Charlize Theron, John Leguizamo, Elliot Page, and Jon Bernthal, positioning the film as a prime frontrunner ahead of awards season.The Odyssey returns to over 1,000 theaters across the U.S. and Canada in all formats, including IMAX 70mm, starting December 11. items.title: Instagram’s Edits App Is Now Available on Mac Desktop for Free
items.text: Instagram’s Edits App Is Now Available on Mac Desktop for Free Summary Instagram is expanding its Edits application to Mac desktop for freeThe software features 4K watermark-free exports and a multi-track timelineBuilt-in publishing eliminates the friction of transferring files to phones for native tagging Instagram is officially bringing its short-form video editing app, Edits, to the Mac desktop. Originally launched last year, the platform has already amassed a footprint of more than 50 million creators currently running the mobile version. Now, the company is scaling up the experience, dropping the desktop application entirely for free. Helmed by Brett Westervelt, who serves as the head of Edits, the move signals a shift in how the platform enables creators to build and finalize visual content. By stepping off the phone and onto the monitor, the software delivers a suite designed for intensive, precision-based production.The Edits desktop application comes fully loaded with a comprehensive multi-track timeline, alongside audio waveforms designed for securing precise cuts. Creators can dial in visuals using keyframes for transitions, while seamlessly alternating between horizontal and vertical video formats. The workspace itself is highly adaptable: users can import custom font files and either build customized keyboard shortcuts from scratch or import mapping from other editing software. To build out the timeline, the desktop version supplies an expansive library of licensed and royalty-free music, stacked alongside diverse sound and video effects. It also integrates a dedicated tool for generating automatic captions across multiple languages, letting producers finalize global-ready clips and export finished videos watermark-free in 4K resolution.Bridging the gap between the studio and the street, the interface keeps ecosystems connected. Audio and text styles saved on the mobile app sync automatically to the desktop application. Instagram plans to push weekly updates to continuously improve the desktop editor. Currently, developers are building functionality that will allow creators to edit a single project back and forth across desktop and mobile platforms, ensuring the creative process continues uninterrupted when moving away from a keyboard.The expansion integrates direct platform publishing into the desktop editor. items.title: The Headphones That Came With the First Sony Walkman Are Back, Now With USB-C
items.text: The Headphones That Came With the First Sony Walkman Are Back, Now With USB-C Summary Sony’s MDR-3R is a modern remake of the 1979 MDR-3, the headphones that debuted alongside the very first WalkmanThe silver on-ear set reproduces the original’s headband bend, perforated sound holes and “Dynamic Stereo Headphones” marking down to the vintage-style packagingA plug-in USB-C connection, in-line remote and built-in mic replace batteries and Bluetooth pairing entirely Sony is reissuing one of the most important headphones in its catalog with the MDR-3R, a reworked version of the MDR-3 that shipped with the original Walkman in 1979. The silver pair keeps the lightweight, open-air formula that made portable listening possible in the first place, then rewires it for modern phones, tablets and laptops through a direct USB-C plug.To understand why the MDR-3R matters, you have to go back to the cassette era. Sony’s first Walkman, the TPS-L2, arrived with the MDR-3 as its companion, and together the two turned music into something people could carry through the city rather than leave at home on a stereo. The original Walkman launched in Japan in July 1979 and famously featured two headphone jacks so a pair of listeners could share a tape. At a time when most headphones were heavy, studio-style cans, the MDR-3’s featherweight build helped make the whole concept wearable.Sony has treated the reissue with collector-level care. The SONY logo and “Dynamic Stereo Headphones” lettering are precision-finished to match the 1979 model, and the distinctive headband curve and perforated sound holes return unchanged. The rolled side arms from the original are back as well, though here they serve a practical purpose, fine-tuning how the earpads sit against the ear for a more comfortable fit. Even the box and instruction manual adopt the vintage graphic style, and the individual packaging is plastic-free.The earpads are the most playful nod to the past. Both the blue and orange cushions associated with the classic MDR-3 come in the box, and swapping between them takes seconds, so the same pair can shift from muted to loud depending on the outfit. Sony has also kept the frame remarkably light, with the headphones weighing roughly 38g without the cable, making the MDR-3R the brand’s lightest over-head model. items.text: New Arrivals From HBX: Moncler Brand Information: Moncler is an Italian luxury brand founded in 1952 by Réné Ramillion in the French alpine village, Monestier-de-Clermont. Over the past six decades, Moncler has cemented itself as a pioneer in the field of functional outerwear. The world-famous outerwear label is especially well-known for its trademark quilted down jackets. In 1968, Moncler designed the professional team uniform for the French alpine skiing team at the Winter Olympics in Grenoble. Today, under the current president and creative director Remo Ruffini, Moncler stands strong as a global lifestyle brand that develops urbane and masculine styles of quilted down jackets, vests, parkas, knit accessories, and even casual wear like T-shirts, sweatpants, and tipped polo shirts. By using patent fabrics and fur details, Moncler injects a modern feel to heritage looks, whilst combining extreme warmth with day-to-day city life. See also Moncler Genius and its collaboration with Palm Angels.Price Range: $350.00 USD - $2,385.00 USDWhere to Buy: Available now on HBX Click here to view full gallery at Hypebeast

items.text: Official Images Surface for the Bad Bunny x adidas Badbo 1.1 "Blanch Blue" Summary adidas and Bad Bunny have revealed official imagery of the Badbo 1.1 in a Blanch Blue colorwayThe low-top silhouette features pale blue suede triangular mesh cutouts and a classic gum rubber outsoleThe pair is expected to release during Holiday 2026 for $120 USD via adidas CONFIRMED and select retailers Name: Bad Bunny x adidas Badbo 1.1 "Blanch Blue"Colorway: Blanch Blue/WhiteSKU: LB9014MSRP: $120 USDRelease Date: Holiday 2026Where to Buy: adidasadidas has unveiled official imagery for the upcoming Bad Bunny x adidas Badbo 1.1 “Blanch Blue”, showcasing the latest iteration of the collaborative low-top silhouetteThe forthcoming release follows previously revealed “Chalk White” and “Simple Brown” editions, expanding the Puerto Rican artist’s signature footwear line ahead of the winter season.Carrying over the fundamental design language of the Badbo 1.0, this updated version modifies the silhouette with a lowered collar and reworked ankle panelling. The upper is constructed primarily in pale blue suede, layered cleanly over lighter blue mesh underlays exposed via distinctive triangular cutouts along both lateral and medial quarter panels. The soft color scheme calls back to the palette previously utilized on the Badbo 1.0 “Puerto Rican Night.”Crisp white accents hit the tongue and midsole to break up the tonal upper, balanced by light grey trim along the collar lining and tongue edges. Grounding the build, a classic gum rubber outsole provides contrast and traction beneath the low-profile runner.The Bad Bunny x adidas Badbo 1.1 “Blanch Blue” is expected to arrive in Holiday 2026, likely in December, for $120 USD via adidas CONFIRMED and select global retailers.Set your reminders and get ahead of what’s dropping next on Hypebeast Drops. items.title: Alpha Industries x No Problemo Map Mount Kailash Across the CWU-45 Jacket
items.text: Alpha Industries x No Problemo Map Mount Kailash Across the CWU-45 Jacket Summary Alpha Industries and No Problemo reunite for FW26, moving from the MA-1 of their first collaboration to the CWU-45 flight jacketThe sage green jacket keeps the CWU-45’s fold-down collar, high-set pockets and structured shapeGraphics from No Problemo’s “Mount Kailash” collection cover the back, and tonal branding runs along the sleeve Alpha Industries and No Problemo have released the Alpha Industries x No Problemo CWU-45, the second chapter of a partnership that started with a take on the MA-1. Finished in sage green for FW26, the jacket brings the graphic world of No Problemo’s Mount Kailash collection to one of Alpha’s most structured military silhouettes.The CWU-45 was first issued to Air Force and Navy pilots in 1972, and its build is very different from the MA-1 the brands reworked last time. A fold-down collar replaces the bomber’s ribbed neck, the pockets sit higher on the body and the overall cut is more structured. The collaboration keeps all three features, using them as the base for No Problemo’s graphic treatment instead of redesigning the jacket.Most of the change happens on the back panel, where hand-drawn figures, symbols and abstract shapes spread across the full width of the jacket. The artwork comes from Mount Kailash, No Problemo’s FW26 collection, which draws on the myths, geometric patterns and charged atmosphere associated with the 6,666-meter Tibetan peak. Against the muted sage base, the line work reads like a coded map more than a typical back print.The branding is more restrained elsewhere on the jacket. No Problemo’s logo runs down one sleeve in a tonal finish that blends into the base color, while a co-branded patch on the chest marks the collaboration. Alpha Industries’ signature red Remove Before Flight tag completes the jacket and adds the only bright color to an otherwise subdued palette.The Alpha Industries x No Problemo CWU-45 will be available online, via the Alpha Industries store in Frankfurt, Aries, Aries Soho in London and select retailers. items.title: Superblue Kyoto to Open in Early 2027 With Landmark James Turrell Exhibition
items.text: Superblue Kyoto to Open in Early 2027 With Landmark James Turrell Exhibition Summary Superblue has announced its first international art center Superblue Kyoto opening in early 2027The venue will inaugurate with a major long-term solo exhibition by Light and Space artist James TurrellLocated directly opposite teamLab Biovortex Kyoto the indigo-clad space will announce full programming details in December Experiential art company Superblue has officially announced the opening of Superblue Kyoto, launching its first international venue in Japan in early 2027 with a major solo exhibition by Light and Space pioneer James Turrell. Situated directly across from teamLab Biovortex Kyoto in the Kyoto Station Southeast Area, the new center expands the Miami-born art platform into Asia with an expansive, long-term survey exploring human perception.surveys the American artist’s six-decade investigation into light as a physical medium from the 1960s through his contemporary practice. Visitors will encounter immersive installations that transform light from an illuminator into the physical subject itself, spanning early works like his 1966 Afrum-Proto projection—which casts the illusion of a glowing three-dimensional cube into a wall corner—to his renowned Skyspaces, Ganzfelds, and research connected to Roden Crater, his monumental naked-eye celestial observatory inside an extinct Arizona volcano.Designed by teamLab Architects, the Superblue Kyoto venue mirrors its neighbor with a distinct indigo-blue exterior, establishing a unified creative nexus within the City of Kyoto's urban revitalization zone. Together with teamLab's largest domestic museum, the two cultural institutions create a walkable district dedicated to large-scale, multisensory contemporary art.Superblue Kyoto is scheduled to open to the public in early 2027, with further details regarding featured artworks and opening dates slated for reveal in December. Take a look at the renderings above. Click here to view full gallery at Hypebeast

items.title: Barbour x Paraboot Trade Waxed Canvas and French Leather for FW26
items.text: Barbour x Paraboot Trade Waxed Canvas and French Leather for FW26 Summary Barbour and Paraboot reunite seven years after their first collaboration with a Bedale jacket and a Chambord derbyEach piece borrows a signature material from its partner, putting olive waxed canvas on the shoe and Paraboot leather on the jacketA co-branded medallion, leather tassel and Barbour tartan lining connect the two designs Barbour and Paraboot have teamed up again for Fall/Winter 2026, pairing a reworked Bedale jacket with a Chambord derby that each take on materials from the other house. The two-piece capsule is the brands’ second collaboration, arriving seven years after their first, and it focuses on construction and craft rather than a broad product lineup.The capsule rests on a straightforward exchange of materials, with each piece lending a signature fabric to the other so the jacket and shoes read as a matched set. The British waxed canvas goes onto the French footwear, and the French leather moves onto the British outerwear, so neither design is just a logo swap.Paraboot’s piece starts from the Chambord, a flat-top derby the house first made for city wear in Paris over 40 years ago. Its core construction stays the same, with five eyelets, a full leather lining, a Norwegian welt finished with a square-edged welt, and a rubber sole. The upper changes, mixing brown “gringo” nubuck with olive waxed canvas taken directly from Barbour’s jacket language.The finishing details make the shoe clearly a collaboration. A co-branded medallion and a leather tassel, both made specifically for this release, hang from the laces, and Barbour’s classic tartan lines the interior. Every pair comes in a Paraboot box with a matching co-branded tartan dust bag inside.Barbour’s half reworks the Bedale in Oban waxed canvas, given a brushed finish meant to build character over time. The jacket keeps its usual roomy cut, low gusseted pockets and corduroy collar, while Paraboot leather forms the chest pocket and both brand names are embroidered on the lower pockets. The same medallion and tassel from the derby appear on the jacket, and the tartan shows under the collar and across the lining.That tartan is what ties the capsule together, running through the collar, the jacket lining, the inside of the shoe and its dust bag. As a result, the Bedale and the Chambord work as a coordinated pair when worn together, while each still holds up as a standalone piece.The Barbour x Paraboot collection is ava

items.title: Clive Christian’s “Uncovered” Perfume Hides a Warm Heart Beneath an Icy Exterior
items.text: Clive Christian’s “Uncovered” Perfume Hides a Warm Heart Beneath an Icy Exterior Summary Clive Christian unveils "Uncovered," its first transparent perfume, crafted by Elise Pierre.The floral musk shifts from icy aldehydes and eucalyptus to warm immortelle, orris and amber.A sculpted clear glass bottle and ice-block box complete its cold-to-warm story. Clive Christian’s "Uncovered", the house’s first transparent perfume, unfolds like the moment frost gives way to morning light. Selected from 14 competing compositions at the CPL Fragrance House Conference, perfumer Elise Pierre’s floral musk opens with a crisp, almost glacial brightness. Sparkling aldehydes and cool eucalyptus reach the senses first, sharpened by a flicker of pink pepper and lifted by the sunny tang of bergamot. Picture a winter window as the sun breaks through: clean, bracing and quietly inviting a closer look.As that initial chill recedes, the fragrance reveals a warmer core. Immortelle absolute lends a honeyed, sun-dried richness, while powdery orris and creamy ylang oil round out the edges, and a salty accord adds an intimate, skin-close quality. The drydown settles into white musk, sandalwood, moss and amber, glowing slowly like embers seen through clear glass. Composed at a 40% concentration from 164 ingredients, the scent is built around the idea of quiet self-revelation, appearing simple at first impression yet continuing to unveil new layers the longer it rests on the skin.The packaging completes this story of a cool exterior concealing inner warmth. "Uncovered" is presented in a sculpted, crystal-clear glass flacon with nothing to obscure what lies inside, a vessel meant to reflect its wearer as both vulnerable and resilient. Its outer box takes the form of a block of ice, turning the act of unwrapping into a kind of thaw that leads to the treasure beneath.Unveiled as a limited edition for the holiday season, the 50 ml fragrance retails for $500 USD in the US and is available from November 15, 2026 through January 2027, or while stock lasts, at Clive Christian boutiques, select retailers worldwide and clivechristian.com. Click here to view full gallery at Hypebeast

Rose brings her signature subcultural edge to the heritage luxury house, signaling a new shift in Balenciaga's aesthetic trajectory. items.title: Joaquin Phoenix Is the Face of Gentle Monster's Intelligent Eyewear
items.text: Joaquin Phoenix Is the Face of Gentle Monster's Intelligent Eyewear Summary Gentle Monster has tapped Joaquin Phoenix to star in its first intelligent eyewear campaign, directed by Jonathan Glazer.The surreal film follows Phoenix through a mysterious hotel where intelligent eyewear becomes a tool for communicating with the unknown.Pre-orders open November 12, followed by a public preview in New York City from November 13 to 23. Gentle Monster is entering the world of intelligent eyewear, and it's enlisted Joaquin Phoenix and filmmaker Jonathan Glazer to introduce its latest venture.The South Korean eyewear brand has unveiled the first teaser for its upcoming campaign film, which explores the relationship between humanity and technology through a surreal narrative that blurs the line between reality and illusion.Directed by Glazer, best known for The Zone of Interest and Under the Skin, the film follows Phoenix as a salesman navigating a mysterious hotel where increasingly bizarre encounters begin to distort his perception of reality. As he comes face-to-face with unfamiliar entities, Gentle Monster's intelligent eyewear becomes a tool for communication, allowing him to understand and interact with a world that initially seems incomprehensible.Rather than taking a conventional approach to showcasing the technology, Gentle Monster places its capabilities at the center of the film's narrative, exploring how intelligent eyewear could change the way people communicate and experience their surroundings.The campaign marks a new chapter for Gentle Monster as it expands beyond traditional eyewear into wearable technology, bringing its experimental design language into a new product category.The full campaign film is set to premiere later this month, with pre-orders for the Intelligent Eyewear Collection opening on November 12. A public preview will also take place in New York City from November 13 to 23, with registration available through Gentle Monster's official website. Read more at Hypebeast

items.title: Batman to Bond? Robert Pattinson Reportedly Screen Tested for 007
items.text: Batman to Bond? Robert Pattinson Reportedly Screen Tested for 007 Summary Robert Pattinson is among the actors who have screen tested to play James Bond, according to 'The Hollywood Reporter'He reportedly joins a shortlist that includes Callum Turner, Jack Lowden, Josh O’Connor and possibly Nicholas HoultThe casting search is the first under Amazon, which took creative control of the franchise from the Broccoli family in February 2025 Robert Pattinson has reportedly screen tested to play James Bond, making the 40-year-old Batman star the most famous name yet linked to Amazon’s search for the next 007. Multiple sources told The Hollywood Reporter that Pattinson read for the part alongside fellow hopefuls Callum Turner, Jack Lowden and Josh O’Connor.According to THR, the tests took place over the weekend of October 24 in London, where Pattinson is currently filming The Batman Part II. The outlet had previously reported that four or possibly five actors were in contention, though only three names had surfaced at that point. Nicholas Hoult is now said to be another contender, which would set up a rematch of sorts, since Hoult finished as runner-up to Pattinson when the Batman role was cast years ago. Amazon declined to comment on the screen tests.Pattinson’s inclusion cuts against the long-held assumption that the next Bond would be a rising name rather than an established global star. He is one of the most prominent actors of his generation and already fronts DC Studios’ Batman franchise, which makes him an unusual fit for a role that has typically gone to someone audiences can grow into.The strongest link may run through Denis Villeneuve, who is directing the next Bond film. Pattinson worked with the filmmaker on Dune: Part 3, which arrives December 18, and the collaboration is said to have gone well for both of them.Pattinson has built his résumé around ambitious directors, working with Robert Eggers, the Safdie brothers and Christopher Nolan, whose 2020 espionage thriller Tenet now looks like an unofficial dry run for 007. This year has been his strongest yet, with a key role in Nolan’s The Odyssey, a co-lead turn in the A24 hit The Drama and the lead in A24’s well-received Primetime.The franchise itself is in uncharted territory, as this will be the first Bond film made under Amazon, which bought creative control from the Broccoli family in February 2025. items.title: The Miami Heat Hit Six Stars With the Cactus Jack x Nike x 'GTA VI' Vice City Uniforms
items.text: The Miami Heat Hit Six Stars With the Cactus Jack x Nike x 'GTA VI' Vice City Uniforms Summary Cactus Jack, Nike and 'GTA VI' team up with the NBA and the Miami Heat on a black-and-pink Vice City uniformThe set pairs a script-front jersey with matching shorts carrying GTA VI palm-tree branding and six pink starsThe Heat will take the court in an exclusive Cactus Jack Nike version during their November 18 game Travis Scott's Cactus Jack, Nike and Grand Theft Auto VI have joined forces with the NBA and the Miami Heat on the Vice City uniform, a black-and-pink jersey and shorts set that pulls four very different worlds into one basketball kit. The drop includes the Swingman Vice City Jersey and the Vice City Shorts, with the Heat set to debut an exclusive on-court version of the look the same night it releases.The Swingman Vice City Jersey is built on a black base, with “Vice City” written across the chest in a looping pink script outlined in white and a pink-and-white jersey number sitting underneath. Stacked pink and white ribbing traces the collar and armholes before running down the side panels. On the chest, the Nike logo is printed in pink and mirrored, with the Swoosh flipped in reverse in a nod to La Flame's signature backward Swoosh.A GTA VI patch sits opposite the Nike logo, its Roman numerals filled with pink-and-black palm-tree silhouettes. Lower down, a pink Cactus Jack logo marks one side of the hem, while a row of six pink stars runs above the jock tag, likely referencing the game’s six-star maximum wanted level. The tag itself is co-branded with the Rockstar Games and Miami Heat logos and labeled “Cactus Jack Edition.”The Vice City Shorts match in black with a glossy sheen, carrying the GTA VI logo on the waistband and a pink Cactus Jack mark near the hip. A column of six pink stars runs down one leg toward a pink Heat logo, while the mirrored Nike logo and pink-and-white side striping finish the opposite leg and both hems.The Swingman Vice City Jersey and Vice City Shorts release in limited quantities starting November 18. items.title: MARK & LONA x ASICS Black Out the Tassel Striders for FW26
items.text: MARK & LONA x ASICS Black Out the Tassel Striders for FW26 Name: MARK & LONA x ASICS Tassel StridersColorway: BlackSKU: MLS-26C-SS03MSRP: ¥47,300 JPY (approx. $300 USD)Release Date: Available nowWhere to Buy: MARK & LONAMARK & LONA and ASICS are giving the Tassel Striders a monochrome reset for FW26, rebuilding the collaborative golf shoe in black nubuck-style leather and white patent accents. The new model keeps the shape of the earlier, well-received Tassel Striders while reworking its materials and colors from top to bottom.The silhouette starts on the basketball court. The Tassel Striders is based on the FABRE JAPAN S, a basketball shoe ASICS released in 1981 that became a long-running favorite with players. MARK & LONA adapted that design for golf and layered in its own design language, and this latest version keeps that shape intact while changing almost everything on the surface.Most of the change is in the upper, which is made from a black synthetic leather with a soft, nubuck-like finish. MARK & LONA’s BLOCK logo is embossed across the entire surface, adding raised texture without introducing any new color. The ASICS stripes stand out in glossy white patent synthetic leather, and the contrast between the matte black base and the shiny stripes gives the shoe its look.The function is aimed at the course. A removable cover over the laces cuts down on sand and debris getting in, and the shoe looks noticeably different with the cover on or off. Two sets of laces in different colors come in the box for further adjustments. Inside, a water-repellent lining handles changing conditions during a round, though MARK & LONA notes the shoe is not fully waterproof. A spikeless outsole built specifically for golf provides grip and stability on the grass across long rounds.The shoe is designed to be unisex and comes in sizes from 23 to 29.5 centimeters. That wide range and the clean black-and-white palette make the Tassel Striders easy to pair with a broad range of golf wardrobes.Set your reminders and get ahead of what’s dropping next on Hypebeast Drops. items.title: Gorsch’s FW26 “The Dancing People” Collection Is Cut for Movement and Built From Rare Cloth
items.text: Gorsch’s FW26 “The Dancing People” Collection Is Cut for Movement and Built From Rare Cloth Summary Gorsch’s Fall/Winter 2026 offering, titled “The Dancing People,” closes out the second half of the Iwate label’s fourteenth seasonDesigner Eiichi Suzuki mixes rare deadstock fabrics with custom and locally made textiles across a run of unisex cutsHighlights include a black flannel cape coat and a denim set colored with kakishibu, a dye made from fermented persimmon tannin Gorsch has unveiled “The Dancing People,” its Fall/Winter 2026 collection, a lineup of outerwear, shirting and trousers from Iwate-based designer Eiichi Suzuki that puts fabric and fit ahead of everything else. The season completes the second chapter of the Japanese label’s fourteenth season, leaning into heavy flannels, a signature herringbone and a persimmon-dyed denim set built around how clothes behave on a moving body.Suzuki’s design language falls somewhere between vintage work garments and proper tailoring, but the cuts are engineered for everyday ease rather than period costume. Every piece is drawn as unisex, with proportions intended to sit well on a broad spread of body types. The fabric strategy follows the same thinking, pairing hard-to-find deadstock cloth with textiles developed specifically for the brand and others produced locally.This season’s direction comes from movement, with Bazar Cirque performers Ken Sakagami and Aoi Kagaya, both friends of the label who perform in Iwate, shaping the collection and fronting its campaign, which was shot in the prefecture by photographer Atsushi Meguro and styled by Suzuki himself. That brief translates directly into the build, with dense, cushy fabrics, oversized proportions and a weighty drape that swings when the wearer moves and settles cleanly when they stand still.The Flannel Wool Cape Coat in black anchors the outerwear, while the most technically interesting piece is a denim set colored with kakishibu, a dye made from fermented persimmon tannin. The set pairs a Short Length Jacket with matching Two Tuck Trousers, giving the dye treatment a full head-to-toe canvas.Elsewhere, the Brushed Collar Wide Shirt arrives in an off-white linen-wool blend, and the trouser offering runs deep. The Wool Two Tuck Trousers come in black flannel as well as the collection’s Dynamic Herringbone weave in navy and terracotta, with the Flannel Wool Easy Trousers in brown rounding out the lineup.Gorsch’s FW26 “The Dancing People” selection is availabl

items.title: Adam Driver Confirms He Is Done Playing Kylo Ren
items.text: Adam Driver Confirms He Is Done Playing Kylo Ren Summary Adam Driver says he will not return as Kylo Ren, closing the door on the shelved standalone film 'The Hunt for Ben Solo'Driver and Steven Soderbergh spent several years developing the project before Disney’s top executives turned it downFans campaigned to save the film with billboards and a banner flown over Walt Disney Studios in Burbank Adam Driver has ruled out playing Kylo Ren again, saying The Hunt for Ben Solo, the standalone Star Wars film he developed with Steven Soderbergh, is no longer in play. Asked on a recent episode of The Rich Eisen Show whether he could see himself returning as the character, Driver said, “Yeah, it’s over… No more ‘Star Wars.’”The project began as a long-term collaboration between Driver and Soderbergh, who was attached to direct. Over several years, the pair worked on a screenplay together with writers Scott Burns and Rebecca Blunt, building a story around Ben Solo as the lead of his own film. Driver told Eisen the group put serious effort into the script and that he thought the result was strong.Lucasfilm was on board at first. Driver has previously said the studio responded well to the pitch and understood the angle the team was taking. The project stalled once it reached Disney’s top leadership, when CEO Bob Iger and Alan Bergman declined to move forward because they could not see how Ben Solo, who dies at the end of the sequel trilogy, could plausibly be alive. Driver summed up the decision to Eisen by saying the executives told him the character was dead.Once the news became public, fans responded on a large scale. Supporters paid for billboards and hired a plane to fly a “Save The Hunt for Ben Solo” banner over Walt Disney Studios in Burbank, California. Driver said he was surprised and moved by the scale of the response, especially the billboards and the plane over Disney’s lot.None of that changed the outcome. Soderbergh signaled in April that the film would already have happened if it were going to, and Driver’s latest comments go further. Pressed by Eisen on whether he would come back if someone revived the project, Driver said that would be up to the studio, not to him or Soderbergh, before adding, “I think the ship has sailed though.” Click here to view full gallery at Hypebeast

items.title: South Korea’s Médongaule Modern Garden Turns Nietzsche Into Pavilions, Paths and a Maze
items.text: South Korea’s Médongaule Modern Garden Turns Nietzsche Into Pavilions, Paths and a Maze Summary Médongaule Garden has opened its Modern Garden in Yangpyeong, South Korea, the second phase of a 14-year plan to build the country’s first humanities gardenChilean studio Pezo von Ellrichshausen designed the pavilions while French landscape architect Guillaume Gosse de Gorre shaped the plantingWalkways built from salvaged stone, waste concrete and preserved dead trees turn the grounds into a route through philosophy and history Médongaule Garden has opened its Modern Garden in Yangpyeong, Gyeonggi Province, South Korea, a landscape that translates the ideas of Nietzsche and a roster of other thinkers into architecture, planting and circulation. The new grounds arrive 14 years after the project began and build on the site’s Korean Garden, which opened in September 2025. Together, they push the destination toward its goal of becoming the country’s first dedicated humanities garden.Where the Korean Garden reworked a traditional garden culture that was cut off by the colonial era and industrialization, the Modern Garden layers a Nietzschean framework on top and opens the conversation to a global audience. The site is organized along two axes. The “Island of Thought” interprets thinkers including Nietzsche, Plato, Saint-Exupéry, Kazantzakis, the Buddha and Levinas through buildings, walking routes and sightlines, and it is meant to send visitors away with new questions rather than fixed answers. The “Story of Korea” landscapes the country’s arc from a nation of scholars through industrialization and democratization to the present, so a personal stroll becomes part of a shared national memory.Chilean studio Pezo von Ellrichshausen, whose work has been shown at MoMA and the Venice Architecture Biennale, designed the Über House and the garden’s main pavilions. The studio’s buildings are placed to coexist with the terrain instead of dominating it, keeping the landscape as the main event.The planting comes from Guillaume Gosse de Gorre, a French landscape architect from a family line of garden makers. He visited Korea every season during the design process, studying the angle of the sunlight, the movement of the wind and where each plant would settle. His approach is clearest in the meadow garden, a 25,000-plant field that changes completely from season to season. items.title: BEAMS’ “DEAR VINTAGE COLLECTION” Dresses the 2026 MAMA AWARDS in Band T-Shirt Nostalgia
items.text: BEAMS’ “DEAR VINTAGE COLLECTION” Dresses the 2026 MAMA AWARDS in Band T-Shirt Nostalgia Summary BEAMS teams up with CJ ENM’s 2026 MAMA AWARDS on the DEAR VINTAGE COLLECTION, a line of official merchandise for the eventThe graphics draw on vintage band tees, festival shirts and corporate promotional teesThe six-piece lineup covers a logo T-shirt, game shirt, zip-up hoodie, tote bag, cap and bandana BEAMS has partnered with the 2026 MAMA AWARDS on the DEAR VINTAGE COLLECTION, official merchandise for CJ ENM’s awards show, taking place on November 20 and 21. Instead of standard event merch, the Japanese retailer has based the range on the graphic styles of collectible vintage tees.The design approach draws on three familiar kinds of printed tee. Band shirts, music festival tees and corporate promotional shirts all serve as references, so the MAMA AWARDS logo is treated less like event branding and more like a find from a vintage rack. The result is merchandise meant to be worn well after the show is over.Apparel makes up half of the lineup. A logo T-shirt anchors the collection, a game shirt brings in a sports-uniform cut, and a zip-up hoodie adds a heavier layer for the winter event dates. Each carries the collaboration’s MAMA AWARDS branding in the vintage-inspired graphic style.The other three pieces are accessories that carry the same graphic treatment at a smaller scale. A tote bag, a cap and a bandana complete the six-piece offering, giving fans lower-commitment ways to pick up the collaboration alongside, or instead of, the apparel.The BEAMS x 2026 MAMA AWARDS DEAR VINTAGE COLLECTION will be available via the BEAMS official online store, BEAMS Namba and the official 2026 MAMA AWARDS MD booth. items.title: The Overlay-Free Nike Air Max 90 SP “Black Leather” Receives a November 2026 Release Date
items.text: The Overlay-Free Nike Air Max 90 SP “Black Leather” Receives a November 2026 Release Date Name: Nike Air Max 90 SP “Black Leather”Colorway: BlackSKU: IV4504-001MSRP: $170 USDRelease Date: November 13Where to Buy: NikeThe Nike Air Max 90 SP “Black Leather” now has a firm release date, with the pared-down take on the classic runner set to arrive on November 13. Part of Nike’s Fall 2026 slate, the pair swaps the silhouette’s signature layering for a mostly leather build defined by stitching instead of stacked panels.With the date locked in, the focus turns to how different this pair looks from a standard Air Max 90. A typical version builds its shape from leather, mesh and plastic pieces layered on top of one another, but this release handles nearly everything in leather. Rather than adding separate overlays, Nike uses stitch lines to trace the Swoosh, the mudguard and the side panels. Each element stays readable against the black, while the overall surface ends up noticeably flatter and cleaner than the model’s usual profile.Perforated leather takes over the areas that normally use contrasting materials. The plastic eyestays are gone, replaced with punched leather that sits flush with the rest of the upper, and the same material wraps the heel, where Nike has dropped the usual Nike Air branding. A tonal logo on the tongue is the only obvious mark left, and black laces disappear into the upper instead of breaking up the colorway.All of the reworking stops at the sole. The familiar Air Max 90 midsole and visible heel Air unit carry over unchanged, finished in black along with the rubber outsole. The one break in the dark palette is a faint blue tint inside the Air window. The stripped-back result sits closer to the minimal styles NikeLab has released over the years than to a typical Air Max 90.Set your reminders and get ahead of what’s dropping next on Hypebeast Drops. items.title: Hollywood Shockwave: James Gunn and Peter Safran Abruptly Step Down as DC Studios Heads
items.text: Hollywood Shockwave: James Gunn and Peter Safran Abruptly Step Down as DC Studios Heads Summary James Gunn and Peter Safran are stepping down as co-presidents of DC Studios after four years leading the comic book divisionMarvel veteran Jeremy Latcham has been named president and chief creative officer to lead all film television and animationGunn and Safran will return full time to creative storytelling including writing and directing next summer's Superman Man of Tomorrow In a stunning industry shakeup, DC Studios co-presidents James Gunn and Peter Safran are stepping down from their executive posts, handing leadership of the superhero universe to Marvel veteran Jeremy Latcham. Latcham, who produced foundational Marvel Cinematic Universe hits including Iron Man and The Avengers, will take over as president and chief creative officer under parent company Skydance.Gunn and Safran’s sudden exit comes after four years steering DC's comic book division through a mixed commercial reset—ranging from the $618 million USD global success of Superman to the steep box-office stumbling of Supergirl. Stepping away from executive management to return full-time to creative filmmaking, Gunn and Safran reflected, “Four years ago, we set out to unite DC under one creative vision. In that time, we helped restore Superman to the heart of DC, while opening new doors and telling new stories in film and television... We’ve shared a creative history with Jeremy going back to Marvel, and we’re eager to see the perspective he brings to DC’s next chapter. We’re excited to return to what drew us to this job in the first place, which is telling the stories we love, including the next chapter of Clark and Lex’s journey in Man of Tomorrow.”Reporting to Skydance Motion Picture Group co-chairs Dana Goldberg and Josh Greenstein, Latcham will now oversee DC’s entire film, television, and animation slate, including the upcoming Superman: Man of Tomorrow, 2028’s The Batman: Part II, and the 2027 miniseries The People v Gorilla Grodd. “DC’s pantheon of characters is among the most iconic in American popular culture,” said Latcham. “The chance to steward the incredible cast of DC characters to the screen in a way that excites lifelong fans while introducing their timeless stories to the next generation is a massive responsibility that I do not take lightly.” Click here to view full gallery at Hypebeast

items.title: London's Design Museum Surveys Contemporary Black Design in New Show
items.text: London's Design Museum Surveys Contemporary Black Design in New Show London’s Design Museum has unveiled an exhibition that charts the work of 16 Black designers, marking one of the most extensive exhibitions on contemporary Black design ever held in the UK.Guest-curated by author and journalist Charlene Prempeh, The Nue Black Aesthetic brings together over 100 objects, ranging from fashion and furniture to architecture, product design and sculpture. Split across six sections, the show is built around a single question: “What does it mean to be a Black designer working today?”Its title draws on two earlier moments: the Black Aesthetic of the 1960s, theorised by writer Larry Neal, and the New Black Aesthetic, which novelist Trey Ellis named in a 1989 essay for the journal Callaloo. “Nue” comes from the Middle French nuer, meaning to make shades of colour, and points to an era defined by nuance, in which there is no single way to be a Black designer.“The idea that Black design is not monolithic should not be surprising or controversial and yet there has historically been very little interrogation about the complexities and inspiration of contemporary Black designers or about how the specific experience of creating in a predominantly white space influences their practice,” Prempeh said.The featured designers are Tejumola Adenuga, Taiba Akhuetie, Ini Archibong, Simone Brewster, Mac Collins, Phoebe Collings-James, Foday Dumbuya, Feben, Nifemi Marcus-Bello, Andu Masebo, Saul Nash, Tosin Oshinowo, Bianca Saunders, Rachel Scott, Samuel Ross and Giles Tettey Nartey.The show opens with Towards a Nue Black Aesthetic, a section of historical context covering seven decades of Black design. Works and graphics by more than 20 designers, from textile designer Althea McNish to Yinka Ilori, set out the groundwork that today’s practitioners are building on.Identity as Inspiration follows, focusing on designers who use their own identity as a starting point. Highlights include the suit Bianca Saunders designed for Usher at the 2023 Met Gala, a piece that reflects her ongoing challenge to hypermasculine ideas of menswear. Nearby, Nigerian British artist Taiba Akhuetie shows domestic furniture made from synthetic hair, including a chair and a lampshade. Akhuetie grew up in Kingston, southwest London, seeing Black hair treated as something to be managed or controlled, and her pieces recast hairstyling as a communal ritual.Community Building looks at design as a way of creating b

items.title: HAVEN and Converse Rework the Chuck 70 in Textured Cashmere Suede
items.text: HAVEN and Converse Rework the Chuck 70 in Textured Cashmere Suede Summary HAVEN and Converse have officially unveiled a collaborative Chuck 70 inspired by tactile craftsmanshipThe silhouette features smooth cashmere suede contrasting hairy suede a leather toe cap and a lateral side zipperThe sneaker releases on November 12 via HAVEN before arriving at Converse channels on November 17 Canadian menswear retailer HAVEN has officially collaborated with Converse to introduce the collaborative Converse Chuck 70, combining functional utilitarian upgrades with a dedicated focus on artisanal craft. Framed through the organic woodworking practice of visual artist and carpenter Graham Landin, the collaborative footwear project updates the classic court silhouette through subtle technical intervention and tactile materiality.Preserving the recognizable proportions of the heritage model, the Chuck 70 features a tonal interplay that contrasts smooth cashmere suede against textured hairy suede panels for noticeable surface depth. Elevated craftsmanship is highlighted throughout the exterior, which incorporates refined leather piping, a practical heel pull, and a leather toe cap that replaces the standard rubber toe bumper.To introduce functional ease while maintaining an understated aesthetic, the design integrates a discreet lateral side zipper running along the medial quarter. Much like Landin’s studio practice—which utilizes chainsaws and traditional hand tools to sculpt weathered wood into refined forms—the shoe's understated character emerges through the quiet dialogue between honest raw materials, purposeful utility, and classic design.The HAVEN / Converse Chuck 70 is scheduled to release on November 12 at HAVEN online, in-stores, and the HAVEN pop-up at the BEAKER Seongsu flagship, followed by a release on Converse channels and select retail partners on November 17. items.title: Supreme x Elliott Smith Fall 2026 Collaboration Collection
items.text: Supreme x Elliott Smith Fall 2026 Collaboration Collection Supreme is honoring Elliott Smith with a new Supreme x Elliott Smith collection, created with the permission of the late singer-songwriter’s estate for Fall 2026. The capsule includes outerwear, fleece, layering pieces and accessories. Archival-feeling photography and album references link the clothing directly to Smith’s catalog.The lineup is short and focused, with seven pieces in total. At the top of the range are a Work Jacket and a Zip Up Hooded Sweatshirt, followed by a Thermal, three T-shirts and a Beanie. Supreme hasn’t yet shared colorways or graphic details for the jacket, hoodie, standard Tee or Beanie. The rest of the collection relies on photography and references to Smith’s catalog.The photography carries the strongest visual weight. The Thermal features original images of Smith by Autumn de Wilde, a photographer closely tied to his visual identity who also shot the cover of 2000’s Figure 8. The Mask Tee uses original photography by Deb Pastor. A separate Either/Or Tee references the 1997 record many fans see as Smith’s defining work.That album marks the turning point in his catalog. Smith, born in 1969, grew up between northern Texas and Portland, Oregon, before attending Hampshire College to study philosophy. There he met Neil Gust, and after graduating the two moved back to Portland and formed Heatmiser, which released three albums before breaking up in 1996. By then, Smith was already recording on his own. His solo debut, Roman Candle, was recorded in the basement of then-girlfriend and Heatmiser manager JJ Gonson and released in 1994, despite Smith never expecting the full album to come out. It and the self-titled Elliott Smith from 1995 set a stripped-down, lo-fi template built on close-mic’d vocals and acoustic guitar.Either/Or bridged that sparse early sound and the fuller arrangements of 1998’s XO and 2000’s Figure 8, the last albums released during his lifetime. The record also brought Smith to a much wider audience. Gus Van Sant placed three of its songs in his 1997 film Good Will Hunting and commissioned an original track, “Miss Misery,” which went on to earn an Academy Award nomination for Best Original Song.Smith died at 34, but his influence continues to grow across new generations of songwriters. He maintained that his lyrics were stories rather than straight confessions. Still, the honesty in how he wrote about his struggles is a big part of why the music endures, and

items.title: MING Gives Titanium the Warmth of Rose Gold With Its 51.01 Halo
items.text: MING Gives Titanium the Warmth of Rose Gold With Its 51.01 Halo Summary MING introduces the 51.01 Halo dress watch in a 37mm crystallized titanium case.Features a 5N rose gold PVD coating, black opaline dial, and sapphire-engraved lacquer indices.Powered by the ultra-thin, manual-wind La Joux-Perret Calibre 7380.M1 with 90 hours of reserve. MING is putting its own spin on the dress watch with the new 51.01 Halo, a compact manual-wind piece that pairs gloss black with warm rose gold tones, a combination the independent brand says its team loves but has rarely used. It debuts an all-new case and handset design, measuring 37mm across, 8mm thick and a wrist-friendly 43mm lug-to-lug. The rose gold look isn't actually gold. The case is machined from grade-5 titanium, then heated in a vacuum chamber to as high as 1,200°C and cooled under strict control, which makes the metal's natural crystalline grains grow larger. An acid etch brings that grain pattern to the surface, and a 5N PVD coating gives the case its rose gold color.The dial and hands continue the warm-on-black theme. The lacquered black dial has a polished center and a circular-brushed outer ring, which creates an opaline sheen, while the new ultra-slim hands are coated in 5N and finished with a mix of brushed, sandblasted and polished surfaces. As on other MING watches, the hour indices are engraved into the box-shaped sapphire crystal rather than applied to the dial. Here they are filled with 5N-colored lacquer instead of lume, a choice the brand describes in its release as "resisting our intrinsic urge to make the indices glow."Flip the watch over and the sapphire caseback reveals the manual-wind Calibre 7380.M1, MING's second movement collaboration with Manufacture La Joux-Perret after the 37.04 Monopusher. Only 2.7mm thick, it runs at 3 Hz with roughly 90 hours of power reserve. MING heavily reworked the calibre with skeletonized, matte anthracite-coated bridges with hand-finished anglage over a matte black mainplate, plus the brand's signature spoke pattern on the ratchet and barrel wheels.The Halo comes on a black goat leather strap by Jean Rousseau Paris, with curved quick-release spring bars and a flying-blade tuck buckle made from the same 5N-coated crystallized titanium as the case. Water resistance is 50 meters, and the watch carries a two-year limited mechanical warranty. Production is limited to 150 pieces, priced at 10,900 CHF (approx. $10,900 USD) Orders open on November 10 through MING'

items.title: Everything Dropping at Palace This Week
items.text: Everything Dropping at Palace This Week Summary Palace’s seventh Winter 2026 delivery is led by four key pieces spanning outerwear, shirting, tees and fleeceThe Pertex Balaclava Puffa comes in six colorways, from core black to Rhythm Red and Ice GreyThe Vauxhall 1995 line splits across a white shirt and a five-color T-shirt run, while the Check P3 Zip Hoodie arrives in six shades Palace Skateboards' Winter 2026 Week 7 drop goes heavy on color, rolling out its key pieces across 18 colorways in total. The delivery is anchored by the Pertex Balaclava Puffa, the Vauxhall 1995 Shirt and T-Shirt and the Check P3 Zip Hoodie, giving the week a lineup that runs from cold-weather outerwear to easy layering staples.Outerwear takes the lead with the Pertex Balaclava Puffa, a puffer built with a Pertex shell and named for its balaclava-style head coverage. Palace is offering the jacket in six options, with straight Black joined by two-tone Black Navy and Black Yellow takes, plus a punchy Rhythm Red, an earthy Brown and a cooler Ice Grey. The range gives the piece both a stealth option and a few louder statements for the deep-winter months.The Vauxhall 1995 pieces bring a matching theme across two formats. The shirt keeps things clean in a single White colorway, while the T-shirt version opens up the palette with Perfect Blue, White, Black, Pink and Grey Marl, making it the easiest entry point into the week’s graphic story.Rounding out the key callouts, the Check P3 Zip Hoodie lands in six colorways of its own. Navy, Black, Grey Marl and Chocolate Brown cover the everyday bases, while Racey Green and Heavy Purple push the hoodie toward the bolder end of Palace’s seasonal color palette.The latest Palace drop arrives Friday, November 13 at 11:00 AM BST in the UK, Europe and the US, followed by Japan, China, Korea and Australia on Saturday, November 14 at 11:00 AM local time.
